Title: How Teacher-Expert Collaboration Shapes the Quality of AI-Supported Scientific Inquiry Learning
Abstract: As Artificial Intelligence (AI) reshapes scientific practice, K-12 science education must transition from traditional inquiry to AI-supported Scientific Inquiry (SI). Teachers face barriers including limited AI knowledge and saturated curricula. We analyzed 11,112 utterances from 26 co-design sessions with 14 secondary school teachers. Using cluster analysis and Transition Network Analysis (TNA), we identified three teacher design profiles: High-Inquiry, Balanced, and High-Acknowledgment. This work further offers actionable scaffolding guidelines, suggesting that effective training fosters equilibrium between technical exposure and pedagogical agency. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: AI-driven license plate recognition for vehicular monitoring in public safety: A systematic literature review
Abstract: Vehicular monitoring systems have been increasingly adopted to support public safety operations in urban environments. Among available technologies, Automatic License Plate Recognition (ALPR) has attracted attention due to its affordability, scalability, and ease of deployment. However, most existing ALPR applications remain predominantly reactive, relying on static watchlists, deterministic rules, or direct database matching, which may limit their ability to support anticipatory decision-making in dynamic public safety scenarios. To better understand this domain, this article presents a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) on the integration of AI-driven predictive modeling into license plate recognition systems for vehicular monitoring in public safety. The review was conducted across six scientific databases and analyzed different variables, highlighting and comparing critical characteristics in recent literature. The findings show that reactive and rule-based approaches still dominate the field, while predictive solutions remain limited and fragmented, with AI-driven methods gaining relevance to support risk assessment and contextual alert generation. Beyond consolidating existing literature, this review clarifies the transition from reactive plate-recognition applications toward predictive and alert-oriented decision-support systems. Moreover, a technical and governance-oriented taxonomy is proposed to organize the main concepts and guide future research efforts, potentially bringing relevant contributions to the area. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Rough set-based credibility-adjusted clustering for time series data analysis: A fusion of fuzzy membership and rough set theory
Abstract: Time series clustering is critical for analyzing noisy and non-stationary signals such as electroencephalogram (EEG), where conventional methods assume equal credibility across all trials, often degrading cluster quality in artifact-prone data. This paper proposes the Rough Set-based Credibility Adjusted Data-Conscious Clustering Method (RCADCCM), which incorporates trial-wise credibility into the clustering process. Employing fuzzy membership and rough-set lower/upper approximations concepts, RCADCCM emphasizes credible trials during centroid updates while selectively pruning ambiguous trials, thereby improving robustness without requiring labels or deep representation learning. The method is evaluated on three motor imagery EEG datasets (BCI Competition IV Datasets 1, 2a, and 2b) using CSP, OvR-CSP and FBCSP, and further validated on the non-EEG Cylinder-Bell-Funnel (CBF) time series benchmark to provide representative evidence of applicability beyond EEG data. RCADCCM is compared with classical clustering baselines and a lightweight deep clustering approach (autoencoder-based K-means). Across all evaluated datasets, RCADCCM consistently demonstrates superior clustering accuracy and structural compactness. Parameter sensitivity analysis reveals stable performance for moderate retention ratios, confirming an effective balance between data credibility and utilization. Runtime analysis indicates only modest overhead relative to classical clustering, while remaining substantially more efficient than deep clustering approaches. UMAP visualizations further illustrate improved cluster separability and the removal of ambiguous trials near overlap regions. RCADCCM achieves performance comparable to supervised EEG classifiers while operating in a fully unsupervised setting, highlighting its robustness, interpretability, and computational efficiency for noisy time series analysis beyond EEG. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Worker and instance similarity-based label completion for crowdsourcing
Abstract: In real-world crowdsourcing scenarios, it is common for each worker to annotate a few instances only, which leads to a highly sparse crowdsourced label matrix and subsequently impairs the performance of the downstream label integration. The recent work called label distribution propagation-based label completion (LDPLC) has been proven to be an effective algorithm to address this issue. However, it exploits an optimization process to absorb similar instances’ label distributions, which harms its computational efficiency and simplicity. To address this issue, we propose a novel worker and instance similarity-based label completion (WISLC) algorithm. Specifically, we first learn a feature vector for each worker to estimate worker similarity using cosine similarity. Then, we estimate instance similarity by measuring the distances between instances. Finally, we argue that similar workers annotate consistent labels on similar instances and then complete missing labels by worker and instance similarity weighted majority voting. The experimental results show that WISLC significantly outperforms LDPLC in improving the performance of downstream label integration algorithms, yet at the same time maintains the computational efficiency and simplicity (no optimization involved). © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Xu Y.; Zeng F.
Title: VulGAT: A Multi-graph Fusion Framework with Attention Mechanism for Code Vulnerability Detection
Abstract: Software vulnerability detection remains a critical challenge in cybersecurity. Although graph neural networks have shown promise in this area, existing approaches typically treat all nodes and edges equally, failing to capture their varying importance and leading to suboptimal detection performance. To address this limitation, we propose VulGAT, a novel multi-graph fusion framework for vulnerability detection powered by attention mechanisms. First, VulGAT employs specialized node and edge embedding algorithms to process Code Property Graphs. By fusing information from multiple graph representations, our approach comprehensively captures multidimensional code features. Subsequently, we introduce a graph attention mechanism to dynamically assign weights to different nodes and heterogeneous edges. This enables the model to concentrate on core vulnerability indicators while filtering out noise from irrelevant code segments. Extensive experiments on the public FFmpeg and Qemu datasets demonstrate that VulGAT significantly outperforms existing baseline models. Notably, VulGAT achieves an F1 score of 73.19%, representing a 7% to 10% improvement over state-of-the-art general vulnerability detection models. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: An integrated application of parameter estimation and target detection for hybrid STCA radar
Abstract: The high pulse repetition frequency (PRF) can cause range ambiguity in radar systems, which negatively impacts the performance of detection, localization, and estimation. In this paper, we develop a radar scheme consisting of phased array (PA) and space-time coding array (STCA), namely the hybrid STCA radar, to resolve the problem of parameter estimation and target detection. By combining the increased range-transmit degrees of freedom provided by multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO)-STCA radar and the high transmit gain provided by PA radar, an unambiguous method is devised for jointly estimating range and angle, while improving the accuracy of parameter estimation. The Cramér-Rao bounds (CRB) are derived to verify the performance of the parameter estimation. Moreover, an integrated application of range-angle-velocity estimation and adaptive moving target detection is proposed for the case of complex jamming environment. Based on the MIMO-STCA mode of hybrid radar, the generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT) detectors in the condition of available and unavailable training data are constructed. Furthermore, a low-complexity approach of the GLRT detector including rough search and fine search is created for practical application. At the analysis stage, numerical simulations and performance analysis validate the effectiveness of the proposed methods during the analysis stage. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

Title: Educational Innovations for Industry 4.0/5.0: Pedagogical Perspectives on Intelligent Systems and Emerging Technologies
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: The accelerated development of generative artificial intelligence (AI) and intelligent tutoring systems is transforming contemporary education and raising complex pedagogical, ethical, and regulatory questions. This paper examines the integration of AI into formal education from the perspective of educational sciences, emphasizing the principle of pedagogy first, technology second. Drawing on constructivist and sociocultural theories of learning, it argues that AI can enhance instructional adaptability and personalization, while human agency, responsibility, and ethical reflection remain essential to meaningful educational processes. Building on UNESCO guidelines for generative AI, the OECD’s Digital Education Outlook, and the European Union’s AI Act, the paper situates educational applications of AI within a global policy and regulatory framework. Recent meta-analyses indicate that AI-based tools can improve learning outcomes and support the development of 21st-century competencies, although effects are heterogeneous and context-dependent. In response to these challenges, the paper proposes the PTA model (Pedagogy–Technology–Agency), encompassing five dimensions: learning outcomes, instructional design, ethics and data governance, teacher agency, and equity. Two case studies from secondary and higher education illustrate the model’s practical application. The findings suggest that AI in education yields substantial benefits only when embedded in a robust pedagogical framework, guided by ethical standards, and supported by institutional and regulatory policies. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: AI-Driven Analytics of Team-Teaching Talk: Acoustic Patterns Across Experience, Cohorts and the Learning Design
Abstract: As classroom cohorts expand, team teaching is increasingly used to integrate the expertise and pedagogical perspectives of multiple teachers. Yet, there is limited empirical understanding of how team teaching unfolds in practice, particularly regarding differences in teachers’ contributions across experience levels, student cohorts, and learning task design. Prior research on team teaching has largely relied on retrospective self-reports or small-scale observations, offering limited insight into the micro-level processes through which team teaching is enacted. Teacher talk offers a scalable lens on these processes. While research in individual teaching contexts shows that acoustic features of speech (e.g., voice quality, intonation, and loudness) can shape student learning, evidence from team-teaching settings remains scarce. Moreover, capturing such features through manual observation or transcription is especially challenging in team-teaching classrooms, where multiple teachers speak across extended sessions and spatial locations, limiting scalability without automation. Grounded in spatial pedagogy theory and team-teaching research, this paper presents an AI-based speech processing approach to analyse classroom talk in team-teaching settings. We analysed 36 recorded undergraduate and postgraduate sessions involving 12 teachers. Spatial pedagogy behaviours were coded and acoustic features extracted to examine variation across teachers’ experience, student cohorts, and the learning task design. The results reveal systematic differences, most notably in loudness dynamics: high-experience teachers, undergraduate classes and collaborative learning tasks exhibited greater loudness variation, suggesting more frequent modulation of volume to foreground key information and support classroom interaction and engagement. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Guo S.; Li B.; Li F.; Zhang L.; Niu B.; Hou Y.
Title: SwapBackHash: State-Compressed Consistent Hashing Framework for Arbitrary Bucket Removals
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: Information systems increasingly store digital evidence in distributed infrastructures. Given the massive scale of digital evidence, failures in storage nodes may lead to costly index reconstruction, cache invalidation, and large-scale data migration. Modulo-based hashing suffers from extensive data remapping under membership changes. Existing consistent hashing approaches struggle to strike a balance between support for arbitrary node removals, fast lookups, and a low memory footprint. As the number of storage nodes scales and the removal ratio increases, many approaches exhibit significant degradation in both lookup latency and memory overhead. To address these limitations, we propose SwapBackHash, a consistent hashing framework with a compressed state layer for arbitrary bucket removals. SwapBackHash employs a stateless consistent hashing engine for primary mapping and a two-stage lookup mechanism, resorting to secondary remapping only if the primary bucket is unavailable. Moreover, we introduce a compressed state layer comprising a permutation, its inverse, and a rollback stack, which maintains the working buckets as a dense prefix and eliminates replacement-chain traversal during lookup. This design maintains the working-bucket set with O(1) update time while ensuring high-performance lookups. For the proposed framework, we derive complexity bounds and prove balance and monotonicity. Experiments with SwapBackHash instantiated with PowerCH, JumpBackHash, and BinomialHash further demonstrate its effectiveness: under random removals over million-scale bucket spaces, all three instantiations achieve at least a 3 × lookup speedup over the state-of-the-art MementoHash, with even larger gains at higher removal ratios. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: Dynamically robust loss: Unlocking noisy-label learning in named entity recognition
Abstract: The quality of dataset annotations is crucial for Named Entity Recognition (NER), but increasing task complexity exacerbates label noise. While previous studies have made progress in addressing isolated aspects of noisy-label problems, their narrow focus limits real-world applicability. We propose a multi-label dynamically robust loss function that adapts to different noise levels manifesting during disparate training epochs through our dynamically robust manner and dynamically adapting scheme, thereby optimizing the suppression of potential noise from various noise types. We conduct extensive experiments on 10 benchmark datasets of two NER paradigms: 6 standard datasets for flat and nested NER, and 4 real-world single-label noisy datasets from NoiseBench. On standard datasets, our method achieves results that are superior or comparable to existing state-of-the-art baselines, with an average F1-score improvement of 0.2%. On these noisy datasets, we observe more significant gains: an average F1-score improvement of 0.62%, with the maximum improvement reaching 1.32%. Additionally, we evaluate our method’s multi-label architectural robustness under synthetic noise on ACE05, establishing its effectiveness in such settings, while robustness under real-world multi-label noise remains to be assessed when corresponding benchmarks become available. Authors: Lee K.-W.
Title: Motivational Configurations in GenAI-Supported Management Learning: a Qualitative Exploration
Abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen AI) tools such as ChatGPT are increasingly used in management education. Beyond technological affordances, sustained engagement depends on motivational alignment. Drawing on Self-Determination Theory (SDT), this study explores how epistemic curiosity (EC) and teacher support (TS) interact in shaping Gen AI use. A four-quadrant typology is proposed and examined through semi-structured interviews with business students. Results indicate that aligned high EC and TS foster deeper engagement, whereas misalignment results in limited learning. Authors: Hou S.; Liu Z.; Xie L.; Chen G.; Jiao H.; Wu S.; Guan X.; Wu H.
Title: PostGISer: The first end-to-end fine-tuned large language model for PostGIS GeoSQL query generation
Abstract: While natural language to SQL (NL2SQL) tasks powered by large language models (LLMs) have matured considerably, automatic generation of GeoSQL queries for PostGIS (NL2GeoSQL) remains challenging. PostGIS's distinctive syntax and complex spatial analytical reasoning frequently cause syntactic errors and logical flaws, producing non-executable or incorrect SQL statements. Currently, no specialized model exists for GeoSQL generation. To address this gap, we constructed a comprehensive corpus comprising 1807 pre-training samples (PostGIS-PT), 38,178 grammar-level fine-tuning samples (PostGIS-SSFT), 56,661 schema-level fine-tuning samples (PostGIS-TSFT), and 298,716 general SQL samples (WHUSQL-TSFT). Using this corpus, we fine-tuned the Qwen2.5–7B model via LoRA to develop PostGISer-7B, the first LLM designed for GeoSQL generation. We systematically evaluated PostGISer-7B using the GeoSQL-Bench framework across five capability dimensions and four benchmark subsets. Results demonstrate a 10.58% improvement in fundamental PostGIS concept comprehension over the base model, exceeding 90% syntactic validity, and outperforming all baselines by an average of 44% in execution accuracy. Robustness testing confirms consistent performance across multi-turn generation and perturbed datasets. Regarding efficiency, PostGISer-7B achieves an average generation length of 775 tokens and generation time of 3.4 s, ranking first among all compared models. Ablation studies validate the effectiveness of our training corpus and fine-tuning strategy. PostGISer-7B delivers an efficient, accurate, and robust solution for geospatial query generation, advancing LLM integration into intelligent GIS applications. Authors: Gao X.; Yang X.
Title: FedShrink: Tackling Data Heterogeneity in Federated Learning with Adaptive Shrinkage Fusion
Abstract: Data heterogeneity in Federated Learning (FL) stems from statistical discrepancies across distributed clients, often leading to significant performance degradation of the global model. Existing methods generally overlook class-disjoint heterogeneity and excessively sacrifice efficiency to achieve performance gains. To address these issues, we propose FedShrink, a lightweight FL framework that integrates two core modules: (1) the James-Stein (JS) shrinkage fusion module that shrinks noisy local estimates toward a global baseline, and (2) the adaptive heterogeneity-aware adjustment module that dynamically tunes shrinkage intensity by measuring data distribution divergence. Extensive experiments on Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet datasets under varying levels of data heterogeneity demonstrate that our FedShrink outperforms state-of-the-art FL baselines in both accuracy and training efficiency, validating its effectiveness in addressing data heterogeneity. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: LLM-Based Applications for Healthcare: A Systematic Mapping Study
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have been increasingly incorporated into real-world applications, including systems in the healthcare domain. In this context, these models have been applied to tasks such as clinical documentation, information extraction, medical record summarization, and clinical decision support. Despite the rapid growth of the literature on this topic, existing studies often focus on specific applications or techniques, with limited consolidation regarding the characteristics of these systems, the architectural approaches adopted, and the challenges associated with their development. This paper presents a systematic mapping study aimed at identifying the main characteristics of LLM-based healthcare applications, the architectures, patterns, and architectural styles employed in their development, as well as the challenges reported in the literature. The analysis considers recent studies describing LLM applications in healthcare contexts. Title: Multi-view Lumbar MRI for Therapy-Oriented Decision Support System in Low Back Pain
Abstract: Therapy selection for symptomatic low back pain remains challenging since clinical decisions require patient-level synthesis of heterogeneous imaging findings. While AI methods for lumbar MRI mainly target diagnostic or structure-specific tasks, therapy-oriented decision support from multi-view acquisitions remains underexplored. We curated a retrospective multi-view lumbar MRI dataset of 294 patients annotated with three therapeutic pathways: conservative, regenerative, and surgical. Each examination includes five sagittal slices and up to three axial slices at clinically relevant levels. We propose a patient-level model based on a shared 2D slice encoder and attention-based aggregation of sagittal and axial evidence. In 5-fold cross-validation, the proposed model achieved 85.03±4.14% macro-F1, outperforming sagittal-only and axial-only variants. Ablations show that sagittal views provide the main global context, axial slices add complementary information, and pre-training improves performance. These results support the feasibility of therapy-oriented multi-view MRI decision support for low back pain. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: PERUN: Protecting Sensitive Cyber Ecosystems from Upcoming Next Generation and AI-Generated Malware Threats
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: The increasing sophistication and frequency of cyberattacks pose significant risks to critical infrastructures, essential services, and digital ecosystems across the European Union. Addressing challenges such as polymorphic malware, encrypted malicious communications, and AI-generated attacks requires integrated, scalable, and trustworthy cybersecurity solutions. The PERUN (Protecting Sensitive Cyber Ecosystems from Upcoming Next Generation and AI-generated Malware Threats) project, funded within the Horizon Europe framework, develops advanced artificial intelligence-driven tools and methodologies for threat detection, vulnerability assessment, and incident response. Title: The Effect of Generative AI–Supported Learning on Reflective Thinking
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is increasingly integrated into educational contexts, yet its impact on higher-order cognitive processes such as reflective thinking remains insufficiently understood. This study estimates the overall effect of GAI-supported learning on students’ reflective thinking through a systematic quantitative synthesis of controlled studies indexed in Web of Science. Eight experimental studies met the inclusion criteria. An exploratory random-effects meta-analysis yielded a large pooled effect (Hedges’ g = 1.00, 95% CI [0.382, 1.617], p =.006). However, substantial heterogeneity was observed, and the wide prediction interval indicates that the effect varies considerably across instructional contexts. These findings suggest that the impact of GAI on reflective thinking is not uniform, but contingent on how the technology is pedagogically implemented. Overall, the results indicate that GAI has the potential to support reflective thinking when integrated as a structured instructional scaffold. This study provides an early quantitative estimate of this relationship and highlights the critical role of instructional design in mediating the effectiveness of GAI-supported learning. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Uncritical but Overconfident? How Learners Engage with AI-Generated Images of Scientists
Abstract: Generative AI outputs have been shown to reproduce stereotypes. This also extends to portrayals of scientists, which are often depicted as male chemists wearing lab coats and surrounded by laboratory equipment. Such representations align with findings from science education research on how students conceptualize scientists. While adults tend to be skeptical of AI-generated content, school students increasingly use AI for homework, learning, and information seeking and may therefore be less critical, especially when content aligns with existing stereotypes. In an exploratory 2 × 2 pilot study, we investigated how 48 secondary school students respond to images of scientists labeled as either sourced from the internet or generated by AI (source framing) and depicting either stereotypical or more diverse representations in terms of gender and ethnic background (diversity). Quantitative results showed no differences across conditions, indicating students’ uncritical acceptance of AI-generated and stereotypical images. In contrast, a qualitative analysis of students’ discussions identified four types along two dimensions: critical vs. uncritical engagement with AI-generated images, and thematizing vs. not thematizing stereotypical attributes. Most students fell into the two critical types. However, students who engaged uncritically with AI-generated images tended to report higher AI-related self-efficacy, suggesting possible overconfidence among those who overlook limitations of AI-generated output. These findings contribute to research on the impact of AI in science communication and education and highlight the need to foster AI literacy among students, especially those who already perceive themselves as highly competent. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Localize-then-summarize: Enhancing scientific multimodal summarization with facet-aware cross-modal memory
Abstract: Scientific papers follow structured facets (e.g., Introduction, Methods), and modern research dissemination increasingly incorporates multimodal formats like presentation videos and audio. This shift necessitates summarization systems that can process both structured and multimodal information. This work proposes Localize-then-Summarize (LENS), a two-stage scientific summarizer that first localizes relevant presentation segments that align with paper facets; followed by summarizing them via memory-augmented reasoning that models dependencies across modalities and facets. On a new MFS-SciSum dataset with 2.7k aligned paper–presentation pairs, the LENS localizer and summarizer achieve Recall@0.5/0.7 scores of 40.83/23.06, and ROUGE-1/2/L scores of 44.71/15.26/21.64, outperforming strong baselines like CLIP and Transformer by 10–15 points in Recall and 1–5 points in ROUGE (resp.). Title: RealSanitizer: Detecting Floating-Point Errors via a Dynamic Precision Oracle
Abstract: Floating-point numerical errors are a major threat to software reliability. Existing oracle-based dynamic analysis tools typically use a statically configured precision oracle, forcing a trade-off between accuracy and overhead. We present RealSanitizer, an instrumentation tool with an ISREAL-based dynamic precision oracle that adjusts precision per operation while bounding oracle error by a user-specified threshold. On 42 reported GSL error-triggering cases, RealSanitizer detects 39 (93%), outperforming ATOMU and approaching FPCC. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Zhi R.; Wang S.; Yang K.; Xiang A.; Li J.; Tian Y.
Title: TSFI: A two-stage incentive mechanism for heterogeneous federated learning under information asymmetry
Abstract: As an advanced distributed computing paradigm, federated learning has demonstrated immense potential in fostering secure collaborative environments. However, in real-world scenarios, such systems often face incentive dilemmas caused by information asymmetry, as well as challenges in fairly evaluating the contributions of participants. To address the lack of client motivation and the challenge of information asymmetry in federated learning, this paper proposes a Two-Stage Heterogeneous Federated Learning Incentive Mechanism (TSFI). First, to tackle the adverse selection problem caused by client heterogeneity, a constrained contract incorporating contribution fulfillment requirements is designed to induce clients to truthfully reveal their private types, thereby achieving differentiated incentives. Second, to address the moral hazard arising from the unobservable local training processes of clients and statistically heterogeneous (Non-IID) data, a clustered Shapley value contribution evaluation algorithm is proposed. By eliminating the evaluation bias caused by differences in data distribution, this algorithm achieves fair contribution evaluation and identifies malicious behaviors. Furthermore, a contribution-based weight reallocation algorithm is designed to mitigate the impact of low-quality clients on the global model. Simulation experiments averaged over five random seeds demonstrate that, under heterogeneous and information-asymmetric conditions, TSFI effectively incentivizes high-quality client participation while reducing server costs. When the global model achieves the target accuracy, TSFI reduces the server’s incentive costs by 28.2% to 39.6% compared with baseline methods. In addition, TSFI achieves higher mean model accuracy than the baselines, with improvements ranging from 0.93 to 3.65 percentage points, while enhancing both the fairness of contribution evaluation and system robustness in heterogeneous environments. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Nutrilyzer: Vision-Based Nutritional Estimation for Postprandial Glucose Response Prediction
Abstract: Nutrilyzer is a vision-based pipeline replacing manual food diaries with AI-derived nutritional estimates for postprandial glucose prediction. Validated on Menu-Match, the vision component achieves macronutrient MAPEs of 17.6%, 13.4%, 24.7%, and 19.4% for calories, protein, carbs, and fats respectively, using Claude—the best of three evaluated VLMs. On CGMacros (45 participants, dual Abbott Libre Pro / Dexcom G6 Pro CGMs), a 13-model comparison reaches R2=0.831 (Voting Ensemble) with MyFitnessPal (MFP) labels plus biometrics; replacing MFP with AI estimates and confidence filtering raises R2 from 0.70 to 0.783 (Random Forest), recovering 94.2% of manual-label performance. Glucose targets in both tracks are sensor-measured—AI labels feed only inputs. Title: Supporting Autonomy in Dementia Patients with a Cognitive Assistant
Abstract: Dementia affects over 55 million people worldwide and incurs more than one trillion USD in annual societal costs, due to loss of cognitive autonomy and the need for care. Beyond economics, declining independence severely impacts the psychological well-being and quality of life of patients and their families. Recent advances in artificial intelligence enable cognitive assistants that provide continuous everyday support. This paper makes three contributions. First, we identify concrete use cases in which cognitive assistance can extend functional autonomy for people with mild cognitive impairment, grounded in qualitative interviews with patients, caregivers, and family members. Second, we present a prototypical general-purpose cognitive assistant integrating memory support, task guidance, contextual reminders, and adaptive interaction, and show how it addresses these use cases. Third, we analyze unresolved challenges in dementia care. These findings suggest that cognitive assistants could become a scalable component of dementia care, provided the technical and ethical challenges are addressed. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Side Effect Aware Multi-Source Representation Learning for Drug-Drug Interaction Prediction
Abstract: The increasing prevalence of polypharmacy has made drug-drug interactions (DDIs) a critical concern for medication safety. Existing computational approaches exhibit two limitations: most rely on a single feature source or static-weight concatenation, and side-effect data are frequently incomplete, yet few methods address robust prediction under partial modality absence. To improve the modeling of complex pharmacological relationships, this study introduces SEAR-DDI, a side effect aware multi-source representation learning architecture for DDI prediction. The framework jointly exploits four modalities (molecular graph structures, molecular fingerprints, knowledge graph embeddings, and side-effect profiles) into a unified 128-dimensional space and fuses them through a four-modal self-attention module that learns inter-modal importance weights for each drug pair. Evaluated on the DrugBank 86-class benchmark, SEAR-DDI achieves 96.14% accuracy, 92.38% macro-averaged F1, and 96.02% weighted F1, outperforming all compared baselines. Ablation experiments validate the significance of each modality and demonstrate the superiority of the proposed multi-modal attention fusion strategy. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: Too Confident to Correct? How Generative AI Reliability Cues Shape User Overconfidence
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: This research investigates how the reliability of Artificial Intelligence (AI) affects human confidence in the decision-making process. The study used an experimental design, recruiting 192 participants (N = 192) who were assigned to three controlled conditions (No AI, 0%; AI with 75% reliability; and AI with 95% reliability). The research process comprises 10 General-knowledge true-false questions, which were provided to the research participants. Participants were provided with AI-generated suggestions for all true and false statements, along with their assigned reliability level. This research study aimed to evaluate the impact of GenAI reliability and the presence of AI support on participants’ confidence in their decisions, regardless of decision accuracy. The results of ANOVA indicate that AI assistance significantly affects research participants’ overconfidence. Participants in all controlled conditions, including 75% and 95% AI reliability, observed that AI was more accurate and reliable. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Delegating (or not) to machines: How role expectations shape leaders’ willingness to use AI for communication
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly capable of replacing people in interpersonal communication, yet it remains unclear how willing leaders will be to delegate communication to AI. Four preregistered studies examine leaders' willingness to delegate specific employee interactions to AI and explore the underlying psychology behind these preferences. Results indicate that leaders are reluctant to rely on AI assistants to automate employee interactions (Studies 1–4). This reluctance is consistently driven by leaders' role-based expectations to signal care to employees, while leaders' desire to maintain control over interactions with employees plays a more context-dependent role (Studies 2–3). Importantly, we find that leaders’ reluctance to delegate communication to AI is specific to AI and not merely a reluctance to delegate communication in general (Study 3). Finally, building on these findings, we show that leaders are most reluctant to delegate communication to AI assistants when interacting about sensitive issues (i.e., issues that heighten the need to signal care and maintain control), in contrast to operational issues (Study 4). Practical and theoretical implications are discussed. © 2026

Title: Evaluating the Impact of Workshop Interventions on AI Literacy and STEM Career Aspirations with Australian Secondary Students
Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is becoming increasingly important in K–12 educational environments, as well as in the daily lives of young people. Recent reports highlight an urgent need for systemic AI education to prevent a widening “intelligence divide” and to prepare the future workforce for a radically shifted labour market. As a result, fostering foundational AI literacy has emerged as a global priority. This study evaluates the impact of Day of AI Australia’s workshop-based intervention designed to improve AI literacy and conceptual understanding among Australian secondary students (Years 7–10). Using a mixed-methods approach with pre- and post-intervention surveys (N=205), we analyse changes in student cohort’s ability to identify AI in everyday tools, their understanding of AI ethics and training, and their interest in STEM-related careers. Baseline data revealed critical safety risks, with nearly one in five students (18.5%) admitting to sharing deepfakes and 7.3% creating them. Results indicate a significant increase in self-reported AI knowledge (p<.001,r=.445) and AI confidence (p<.001,r=.279) following intervention within the cohort. Students showed a significant improvement in recognising AI within popular platforms such as Netflix (+27.1%), Spotify (+16.2%) and TikTok (+12.8%), highlighting a transition from viewing these systems as simply algorithm-based to AI-driven. Post-workshop, self-reported interest in STEM careers increased (p<.05), though effect sizes were small. This suggests that alternatives to one-off workshops may be required to meaningfully shift long-term career aspirations. These findings contribute to the growing body of evidence on effective AI literacy frameworks and offer practical insights for scaling AI literacy programs. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Huang Z.; Yuan W.; Luo Y.; Pan J.
Title: A Lightweight Cross-Modal Guiding Network with Temporal Contrastive Alignment for Emotion Recognition
Abstract: Multimodal emotion recognition from physiological signals is an important intelligent computing task with broad potential in affective human-computer interaction and biomedical informatics. However, several challenges remain: (1) inherent temporal asynchrony across modalities hinders fine-grained semantic alignment; and (2) the quadratic computational cost of Transformers limits long-range context modeling. To address these, we propose CMGN, a lightweight guiding network with contrastive alignment. CMGN employs an efficient Hyena encoder to capture long-range dependencies with sub-quadratic complexity. We introduce a cross-modal consistency learning (CMCL) module that leverages contrastive learning for global semantic synchronization while utilizing EEG signals to guide local feature modulation within the eye-tracking branch, thereby effectively suppressing subjective noise and modality asynchrony. Experiments on SEED-IV and SEED-VII demonstrate that CMGN achieves accuracies of 87.63% and 73.36%, respectively, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines. Notably, compared with Transformer-based encoders, our model maintains competitive performance with significantly lower computational cost. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of CMGN as an advanced intelligent computing methodology for multimodal affective applications. Title: Validation of an Interpretable AI System for Localizing the SubThalamic Nucleus During DBS Neurosurgery
Abstract: Accurate localization of the SubThalamic Nucleus (STN) during Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) surgery is critical for therapeutic efficacy and is commonly supported by intraoperative MicroElectrode Recordings (MERs). While deep learning approaches have shown promising performance in automatic STN identification, their limited transparency hinders their clinical adoption. In this work, we present an interpretable deep learning pipeline for MERs classification coupled with a structured validation framework aimed at assessing the clinical relevance of the model reasoning. To this aim, the classification output from a patch-based convolutional neural network with self-attention is combined with Grad-CAM relevance maps. Alignment between relevance maps and manual annotations from 3 expert neurologists with 27, 20, and 11 years of experience was quantified using overlap-based metrics, while perceived transparency, usefulness, and trustworthiness were assessed through Likert-scale questionnaires. Results show competitive classification performance (0.92 ± 0.07 AUC) and consistent agreement between automatic explanations and expert reasoning, with a maximum Dice Score of 0.77 ± 0.11, alongside high clinician acceptance and perceived interpretability. These findings suggest that structured, expert-centred validation of XAI can provide a meaningful contribution toward trustworthy AI-assisted decision support systems in intraoperative neurosurgery. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Can Artificial Intelligence Literature Review Tools Provide Reliable Overviews?
Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) literature review tools like Elicit, consensus, and Scispace are gaining popularity among novice researchers, especially graduate and undergraduate students. Beyond retrieving a list of the most relevant research papers, these tools provide a synthesized overview of a research area. However, questions remain about the accuracy and reliability of AI-generated overviews. Therefore, this study compared the overviews produced by four user-friendly AI research assistants. I examined the citations used in the summaries based on three key criteria: (1) currency, (2) author expertise, and (3) diversity and bias. Additionally, I compared the content of the overviews based on their depth of analysis, supporting evidence, relevance, and language quality. Findings revealed several limitations in the effectiveness of AI research assistants for providing an overview of the research topic. The overviews were written based on the most recent publications (2009–2025). The AI research assistants often overlooked many seminal works in the field. Furthermore, the citations on the topic of teacher-written feedback were predominantly focused on university-based research and specific geographical regions. Most importantly, analysis demonstrated that AI-generated overviews lacked depth of analysis. Novice researchers wishing to use AI research assistants must be aware of the limitations of the AI-generated overviews. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Task-aware modality configuration in personalized health information systems: Evidence from multi-attribute task contexts
Abstract: This study investigates how multi-attribute health-related tasks shape users’ observed choices among single-modal and multimodal information combinations. It examines modality configuration as a task-triggered, micro-level instantiation of task–technology fit in personalized health information systems. Grounded in task facet classification theory, the study conceptualizes health tasks along three dimensions: task type, task complexity, and topic group. These effects are examined through a quasi-experimental design based on simulated work task scenarios. A total of 120 participants were recruited, yielding 25,000 valid health information records selected and saved in a researcher-supervised controlled live-web SWTS setting. Distributional differences in modality choices across task configurations are examined, and the findings are triangulated using descriptive odds ratios and multinomial logit models to assess the consistency of effect direction and relative strength in task–modality relationships. The results show that users’ observed modality choices are highly concentrated in a small number of dominant text-centered single-modal and multimodal formats, indicating a clear distributional concentration pattern rather than indiscriminate multimodal use. Systematic distributional differences are observed across task configurations in the selection proportions of key modality combinations, including text-only, text–voice, text–image, text–image–video, and text–video formats, suggesting that task attributes are associated with observed modality choices in multimodal information system use. By translating task attributes into implementable modality configuration logic, this study operationalizes modality configuration as a task-triggered, micro-level instantiation of task–technology fit and provides actionable principles for adaptive and risk-sensitive modality design in personalized and generative AI–enabled health information systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Building Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence Enabled Electronic Health Record Systems

Title: Who Gets the Gains? Technology, Productivity, and the Split Between Labor and Capital
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: Why has labor’s share of national income in the advanced economies drifted downward since the 1980s, and why has the drift been so uneven across countries with broadly similar technologies? This paper takes up that question not by offering a new econometric decomposition—it does not—but by weighing four intellectual traditions (classical, neoclassical, task-based, and institutional) against the causal evidence now available, with particular attention to cross-country variation and to the still-thin evidence on generative artificial intelligence. My reading of that evidence is that neither automation on its own nor institutional erosion on its own can carry the explanation. What fits best is an interactive account, in which technology-enabled market concentration and the weakening of worker bargaining power jointly shape how the gains from production are divided. That interaction, I argue, is not written into the technology: choices about the direction of AI development, the governance of data, competition policy, and labor-market institutions can move distributional outcomes appreciably. The paper closes with what these readings imply for future research and for policy. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Laghu: Localization of RL-Induced Reasoning in Small Language Models
Abstract: Small Language Models (SLMs) remain limited in mathematical reasoning despite their deployability advantages. Reinforcement learning based post-training methods have recently shown promising improvements in mathematical reasoning, yet very little is understood about how these methods modify the internal representation of the language models. In this work, we investigate how reinforcement learning fine-tuning alters reasoning behavior in small language models. Using Gemma-2-2B model fine-tuned with supervised learning and further trained with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), on the GSM8K benchmark, we observe reasoning accuracy improving from 24.3% to 51.3% on the GSM8K. To understand the source of these gains, we conduct a mechanistic investigation of reinforcement-induced reasoning improvements, which we refer to as Laghu (Localization of RL-Induced Reasoning in Small Language Models). By comparing representations and performing targeted analysis, we identify layers and attention heads that causally mediate reasoning improvements introduced by reinforcement learning. Our analysis suggests that RL fine-tuning induces localized computational changes in deeper layers of the model, concentrating reasoning behavior in a small subset of components. These findings provide new insight into how reinforcement learning modifies the internal reasoning mechanisms of small language models. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: A methodology to perform cross-ecosystems case-control security studies: Java/Maven vs Python/PyPI
Abstract: The choice of one’s programming language and relative ecosystem of libraries can affect the likelihood of encountering a critical vulnerability. Simply counting the vulnerabilities by mining a software repository is not enough, and case-control studies are a well-accepted methodology to determine relative risk. Yet, they require the ability to compare ‘equals with equals’ as a library for text processing is likely subject to less security scrutiny than a library for web applications. To compare libraries, we implemented a human-guided protocol to transfer classification categories from an ecosystem to libraries of another ecosystem. By building of this categorization, we performed a case-control study with the vulnerabilities available on Snyk and with status ’reviewed’ in the Github security Advisories till 2024. We mapped 76 Java/Maven libraries and 221 Python/PyPI packages as ’cases’ (libraries with vulnerabilities with a CVSS critical score) compared them against 58 Java/Maven and 166 Python/PyPI ’controls’ (Only with a high CVSS score). We found and overall the odds ratio of ending with a critical vulnerability is slightly higher when using a Java/Maven library in comparison to using a Python/PyPi package (1.13x). We refine the analysis to understand possible reasons for our result by using the CVSS vector metric. A possible explanation is that a vulnerability with low attack complexity has disproportionately higher chances to be critical in Java/Maven (38.9x) than in Python/PyPI (5.9x). Such results might be explained by the lack of past security interest in the Python ecosystem. By using the introduction of the OWASP dependency checker in 2023 for Python as possible indication of community interest, we found a risk reversal: after 2023 the risk of ending with a critical vulnerability (as opposed to just a high severity one) is significantly higher (2.4x) for a Python/PyPI package than for a Java/Maven library. To allow replication and updates, we make the dataset and the protocol individual steps available as open data. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Can LLMs Accurately Score Medical Diagnoses and Clinical Reasoning?
Abstract: Evaluating medical AI systems using expert clinician panels is costly and slow, motivating the use of large language models (LLMs) as alternative adjudicators. Here, we evaluate an LLM Jury, composed of three frontier AI models, for scoring 3333 diagnoses on 300 real-world low- and middle-income country (LMIC) hospital cases. Both LLM- and clinician-generated diagnoses are scored against expert panel diagnoses across four dimensions: diagnosis, differential diagnosis, clinical reasoning, and negative treatment risk. The LLM Jury scores are compared with expert and independent re-scoring panel scores, assessing error metrics, inter-rater agreement, severe risk errors, and the effect of post hoc calibration using isotonic regression. In our data, we find that: (i) the uncalibrated LLM Jury scores preserve ordinal agreement with the expert clinician panel scores, but are systematically lower; (ii) the probability of severe risk errors is lower for the LLM Jury than the human expert re-score panels; (iii) the LLM Jury combined with LLM diagnoses can be used to identify diagnoses at high risk of error, enabling targeted expert review and improved panel efficiency; (iv) the calibrated LLM Jury rankings of diagnosing agents show excellent agreement with primary expert panel rankings. Together, these results provide evidence that a calibrated, multi-model LLM jury is a trustworthy and reliable proxy for expert clinician evaluation in medical AI benchmarking. Confirming these findings in other clinical settings is an important direction for future work. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Combating label noise in sequential recommendation: A symmetric cross-entropy and contrastive denoising framework
Abstract: Significant progress has been made in sequential recommendation, which focuses on modeling users’ dynamic preferences through sequence-based approaches. Among these, contrastive learning (CL) methods effectively alleviate data sparsity. However, most CL methods typically overlook the presence of noisy labels in the original data and introduce new noise during the contrastive pair construction process. To address these dual challenges, we propose a Symmetric Cross-Entropy and Contrastive learning-based Denoise framework for sequential Recommendation (SCDRec). Within a meta-learning paradigm, our framework incorporates two technical components: a noise separation strategy and a perturbation attention mechanism. The separation strategy learns a correction term for potentially noisy supervision, guided by a robust symmetric cross-entropy objective. Concurrently, the perturbation attention mechanism generates robust feature representations for contrastive learning by injecting controlled parameter noise into attention modules, creating correlated and noise-resilient views. Extensive experiments conducted on Amazon Beauty, Amazon Sports, and Yelp datasets show that SCDRec improves ranking accuracy over competitive sequential and contrastive recommendation baselines. SCDRec obtains the best result on most evaluated metrics and remains competitive on the remaining metric. Additional controlled corruption experiments indicate that SCDRec maintains strong absolute performance under synthetic training-label corruption and inference-time perturbation, providing empirical support for its robustness while not treating these stress tests as a complete proxy for all naturally occurring behavioral noise. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Every Segment Remembered: Reliability-Tokenized MoE Adapters for Mismatch-Robust and Better-Calibrated Audio-Visual Learning
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: Audio-visual learning often assumes that the audio and visual streams in a video are semantically aligned. In real-world videos, however, this assumption can be fragile: background music, dubbing, narration, off-screen sounds, and temporal misalignment may cause cross-modal interaction to amplify unreliable evidence rather than improve recognition. This paper proposes ReliaCLIPAV, a reliability-aware audio-visual adaptation framework that learns when to encourage or suppress cross-modal interaction. Built on frozen pretrained audio and visual backbones, ReliaCLIPAV introduces two lightweight adapter paths: an interaction-safe expert that preserves modality-specific evidence, and an interaction-enabled expert that performs cross-modal refinement when the two modalities are likely to be consistent. A reliability gate, estimated from semantic agreement, uncertainty reduction, and temporal offset cues, dynamically routes each sample between the two experts. To make the gate sensitive to different degrees of audio-visual conflict, we further design reliability-oriented training objectives and mismatch-aware augmentation strategies. Experiments on AVE, VGGSound, and Kinetics-Sounds, together with dubbed and synthetic mismatch stress tests, show that ReliaCLIPAV improves robustness under modality inconsistency while maintaining competitive performance on clean samples. Beyond accuracy, the proposed method also yields better calibration and more reliable selective prediction, suggesting that modeling cross-modal reliability is important for practical audio-visual recognition. The framework achieves these gains with only a small increase in trainable parameters over lightweight adapter baselines. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: GIFT: Topological Locking for Long-Term Persona Memory in Conversational AI
Abstract: Long conversations require dialogue systems to preserve stable user facts while allowing short-lived context to lose influence. Standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) relies on semantic similarity, which allows recent but unstable turns to compete directly with persistent persona facts. We introduce GIFT (Gist-based Incremental Forgetting with Topological locking), a hierarchical memory architecture that assigns each memory a dynamic lock value tlock(τ) ∈ [0, 1]. Locked persona memories remain accessible, whereas ordinary context decays under an adaptive forgetting controller. GIFT achieves 93.2% Top-1 accuracy on PersonaChat versus 61.9% for Vanilla RAG, and 97.8% on BST versus 77.7%. In dialogues longer than 20 turns, GIFT maintains 90.6% accuracy while RAG drops to 40.0%. Ablations indicate that the lock mechanism is the main contributor, improving PersonaChat by 20.1 percentage points. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: Evaluation of Generative AI Tools for Process Modeling with Educational Purposes
Abstract: Process modeling is an important topic that has faced multiple advancements, as a result of its integration with artificial intelligence. Results showed that in-built editing options, friendly visual appearance, or code control are the top preferences of engineering students. Title: A Hyper-heuristic DQN Algorithm for the Lot-Sizing and Scheduling Problem in Distributed Heterogeneous Factories
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: Driven by economic globalization and intelligent manufacturing, distributed manufacturing has become a prevailing model in complex industries. This paper addresses the Distributed Heterogeneous Factory Lot-sizing and Scheduling Problem (DHFLSP), a core optimization challenge. A collaborative hyper-heuristic algorithm integrated with a Deep Q-Network (DQNHH) is proposed. Unlike existing single-agent reinforcement learning methods that struggle to decouple the hierarchical relationship between lot-sizing and shop-floor scheduling, the proposed method introduces a hierarchical decision architecture. This architecture utilizes a Batch-sizing Agent (BSA) for production-line-level lot-sizing and a Scheduling Optimization Agent (SOA) for operation-level sequencing. A multi-head attention mechanism enables cross-layer interactions. Furthermore, a low-level heuristic operation pool, combined with a dynamic reward mechanism and a Pareto non-dominated sorting strategy, is adopted to balance makespan and total tardiness. Experiments demonstrate that DQNHH significantly outperforms traditional optimization algorithms and classical hyper-heuristic methods in terms of solution quality. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: LLMs’ reshaping of people, processes, products, and society in software development: a qualitative exploration with early adopters
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly reshaping software development, but their impact across the full software development lifecycle is underexplored. Existing work tends to focus on isolated activities such as code generation or testing, leaving open questions about how LLMs affect developers, processes, products, and the broader software ecosystem. We address this gap through semi-structured interviews with sixteen early-adopter software professionals who integrated LLM-based tools into their day-to-day work in early to mid-2023. We treat these interviews as early empirical evidence and compare participants’ accounts with recent work on LLMs in software engineering, noting which early patterns persist or shift. Using thematic analysis, we organize our findings around four dimensions: people, process, product, and society. Developers reported substantial productivity gains from reducing mundane tasks, streamlining search, and accelerating debugging, but also described a productivity-quality paradox: they frequently discarded generated code and shifted effort from writing code to critically evaluating and integrating it. LLM use was highly phase-dependent, with strong uptake in implementation and debugging but limited influence on requirements gathering and collaborative work. Participants developed new competencies to use LLMs effectively, including prompt engineering strategies, multi-layered verification, and security-conscious integration to protect proprietary data. They also anticipated changes in hiring expectations, team practices, and computing education, while emphasizing that human judgment and foundational software engineering skills remain essential. Our findings, consistent with evidence from large-scale studies, offer actionable implications for developers, organizations, educators, and tool designers seeking to integrate LLMs responsibly into professional software practice. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: The Missing Evaluation Axis: What 10,000 Student Submissions Reveal About AI Tutor Effectiveness
Abstract: Current Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based tutoring systems (AI tutors) are primarily evaluated based on the pedagogical quality of their feedback messages. While important, pedagogy alone is insufficient because it ignores a critical question: what do students actually do with the feedback they receive? We argue that AI tutor evaluation should be extended with a behavioral dimension grounded in student interaction data, which complements pedagogical assessment. We propose an evaluation framework and apply it to 10,235 code submissions with corresponding AI tutor feedback from an introductory undergraduate programming course to measure whether students act on tutor feedback and whether those actions are applied correctly. Using this framework to compare two deployed AI tutors across different semesters in a large-scale introductory computer science course reveals substantial differences in student engagement patterns that are not captured by pedagogy-only evaluation. Title: CoTMind: A closed-loop framework for optimizing Chain-of-Thought reasoning in complex question answering
Abstract: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting has been shown to improve complex question answering, but existing methods often rely on implicit confidence scores from large language models (LLMs), which limits transparent evaluation and modular extension. To address these limitations, we propose CoTMind, a closed-loop framework that integrates candidate reasoning-step generation, multidimensional evaluation, and candidate-step selection policy optimization. In the generation stage, DeepSeek-LLM-67B decomposes complex questions into successive sub-questions and retrieves evidence via dual channels to form structured reasoning steps, each consisting of a sub-question, supporting evidence, and an answer. In the evaluation stage, hard labels derived from the REVEAL dataset (704 complex questions, 1002 reasoning chains, 3360 steps, and 1250 human annotations) and soft labels generated by DeepSeek-LLM-67B are used to train a lightweight student model, Qwen2.5-0.5B, producing a six-dimensional reward model (6T-DistillRM) that provides fine-grained scores for relevance, step type, correctness, evidence support, chain consistency, and attribution coverage. In the optimization stage, these scores serve as reward signals for Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), which optimizes a candidate-step selection policy over fixed generated candidates, rather than directly fine-tuning the backbone generator, to improve the overall quality of the resulting reasoning chains. On five complex QA benchmarks (500 sampled test questions each from HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue, Fermi Questions, and StrategyQA), CoTMind achieves F1 scores of 68.2, 70.8, 36.1, 42.5, and 83.4, respectively, outperforming CoT-Decoding by 6.4, 7.1, 3.7, 4.9, and 2.5 points. These results suggest that CoTMind offers a more structured reasoning framework and yields empirical gains across the evaluated benchmarks, especially on explicit multi-hop QA, with partial transfer to implicit reasoning tasks and more mixed evidence on highly compressed yes/no reasoning. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: An Attitude Paradox? Examining Ability Beliefs and Persistence Intentions in a Middle School Conversational AI Learning Experience

Title: Tranquiliza 360: An Immersive VR–AI Ecosystem for Cognitive, Emotional, and Motor Rehabilitation

Title: Griefbots—A New Virtual Reality for Our Youths?

Abstract: This cross-sectional study explores the Portuguese public’s perception of griefbots—AI systems that mediate grief by simulating deceased loved ones. Is this going to be a new reality in future years to come and for the youths of today? Based on a survey that yielded 276 valid responses from Portuguese residents aged 18 or older, the study analysed, through descriptive and inferential statistics, acceptability, perceived risks or concerns, and willingness to pay, framing the findings within a PESTEL strategic management analysis. Acceptance is hindered by a distrust in sharing personal data with AI across all generations. The descriptive results show high refusal to learn how to chat with griefbots among Gen Z, Millennials, and Gen X. Baby Boomers stand out as the only group with notable openness, which was confirmed by the Kruskal-Wallis test and the Mann-Whitney test, in inferential statistics. All cohorts showed caution toward griefbots. Key concerns include the fear of emotional dependence, denial, and prolonged grief. Ethical worries focus on recreating the deceased without consent and the commercialization of human suffering. Millennials and Gen Z strongly prefer simulation warnings, contrasting with Baby Boomer’s preference for realism. Regarding economic value, Millennials emerge as the most receptive cohort, showing a preference for a one-time payment model, while Gen Z favours the freemium model. Strategically, griefbots occupy a regulatory grey area concerning posthumous data rights and faces long-term sustainability threats due to the environmental impact of large—scale AI infrastructure. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Beyond Performance Metrics: Nurses’ Concerns and Comfort with Clinical AI Use in Canada
Abstract: Nurses represent frontline users of Artificial Intelligence (AI) enabled decision support, monitoring, and workflow systems, but their perspectives remain underrepresented in AI implementation research. This study examines the nature and level of concerns affecting nurses’ comfort with AI use in Canada. Secondary data from the 2023 Canada Health Infoway nurses’ survey (N = 1,907) were analyzed to examine the association between self-reported comfort (dependent variable) and concerns with AI use (independent variables). Multivariate ordinal logistic regression analyses assessed the relationship between comfort with AI use and nine concern items (4-point Likert Scale, 1 = very uncomfortable or concerning to 4 = very comfortable or not at all concerning) covering three concern areas (i.e. ethical/legal; human-relationship; workforce), while controlling for age and gender. Most respondents were female (91.5%) and [35–54] years old (53.7%). Median concern levels ranged from 1 to 2, with highest concerns related to data privacy and reduced human interaction (median = 1, respectively). Comfort with AI use was moderate (median = 2). Lower comfort was significantly associated with older age (τ = −0.066) and female gender (χ2 (2) = 6.18). Multivariate analyses showed that greater concerns with medical liability (β = 0.363), negative patient-provider relationship impact (β = 0.409), and mistrust in AI (β = 0.498) are significantly associated with lower comfort. Nurses’ comfort with AI use is associated with AI trust and accountability concerns. Future research should build on these findings and investigate how AI knowledge may affect this relationship. Designing AI tools requires in addition to algorithmic transparency and performance validation, liability frameworks, explainability, and clinician-centered interaction models that alleviate users’ concerns. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Scaling Socratic Dialogue with Generative AI: Understanding Implications for Student Engagement and Learning Outcomes
Abstract: This study examines Socratic Mind, a generative artificial intelligence (GenAI)-powered tool designed to scale adaptive Socratic dialogue and provide reasoning-focused practice that is difficult to deliver at scale in large courses. Implemented in an undergraduate computer science course, the study adopts a mixed-methods approach that integrates academic outcomes, behavioral indicators of tool use, sentiment analysis of student-AI dialogue transcripts, and students’ reflective responses about higher-order thinking. Behavioral traces and dialogue features suggest that productive engagement was characterized by sustained, elaborated interaction, including persistence across assignments and richer dialogic exchanges. Affective analyses indicate that students expressed more varied emotional tone during dialogue in AI-mediated learning. Students’ reflections further suggest that adaptive Socratic questioning supported cognitive engagement, especially among fully engaged students, by prompting them to articulate reasoning, confront misconceptions, and monitor their understanding. Overall, our findings provide actionable insight for designing pedagogically meaningful and engagement GenAI-assisted educational tools. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: The Critical Role of Model Selection in Causal Inference: A Comparative Analysis of Classification Models Within the InferBERT Framework for Pharmacovigilance
Abstract: Distinguishing true causal adverse drug events (ADEs) from spurious correlations is a core pharmacovigilance challenge. The InferBERT framework [12] combines a neural classifier with Judea Pearl’s Do-calculus to address this, but the pipeline depends critically on the classification model’s quality. We compare four models: XGBoost (a strong tabular baseline), ALBERT (the original InferBERT implementation), BioBERT (a biomedical-domain transformer), and Med-LLaMA (an 8-billion-parameter medical LLM) on two FAERS benchmarks: Analgesics-induced Acute Liver Failure (AILF) and Tramadol-related Mortalities (TRAM). We evaluate accuracy, calibration (ECE before/after isotonic regression), and Jaccard concordance with PRR, ROR, and EBGM signals using 5-fold CV over 20 runs with paired t-tests. BioBERT achieved significantly higher predictive accuracy than all other models on both datasets (p<0.0001). Domain-specific pre-training proved essential, whereas the much larger Med-LLaMA performed worst. Post-hoc calibration reduced ECE but had inconsistent effects on accuracy and causal discovery. These results demonstrate that domain-specific pre-training offers a clear practical advantage over both simpler models and larger LLMs in computational pharmacovigilance. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Automated Pulmonary Hypertension Subtype Discrimination from CTPA Scans
Abstract: Accurate differentiation between Arterial Pulmonary Hypertension (PAH) and Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension (CTEPH), two subtypes of Pulmonary Hypertension (PH), from CT Pulmonary Angiography (CTPA) scans may facilitate earlier diagnosis and improve patient prognosis. In this work, we reimplemented an existing framework originally developed for the identification of chronic thrombi in CTPA scans and adapted it to the differentiation between PAH and CTEPH. The original framework was based on generating Maximum Intensity Projections (MIP) of the CTPA scans from different spatial positions, which were then embedded and classified using a neural network architecture. Furthermore, we introduce a variant of the approach that allows ranking MIP projections and generating relevance maps in the original CT image space, thereby improving explainability. The two methods exhibited comparable classification performance. However, a preliminary radiologist assessment of the relevance maps generated by the proposed variant suggests an ability to focus on regions of abnormal pulmonary perfusion that are characteristic of thromboembolic disease. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Artificial Intelligence in HRM and Organizational Learning Culture: Impacts on Leadership and Teacher Performance
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: This study investigates the interplay between artificial intelligence–driven human resource management (AI-driven HRM), organizational learning culture, leadership effectiveness, and employee performance within the education sector in Johor, Malaysia. Drawing on the Ability–Motivation–Opportunity (AMO) framework, the research develops and tests a holistic model that integrates technological practices, relational leadership skills, and cultural preconditions. Data were collected through a cross-sectional survey of 131 teachers across Malaysian schools, analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Results demonstrate that AI-HRM and organizational learning culture significantly enhance leadership effectiveness, which in turn positively influences employee performance. Moreover, leadership effectiveness mediates the relationship between AI-HRM, organizational learning culture, and performance outcomes, underscoring its critical role as a bridging mechanism. The findings contribute to theory by addressing conceptual fragmentation in HRM research and highlighting the importance of organizational culture in technology adoption. Practically, the study emphasizes the need for school leaders to balance digital innovation with human-centered leadership to foster teacher engagement and performance. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Ethnic Capital in AHP-Driven Preference Elicitation and Public Policy Negotiation
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: The research concerns interstate negotiations. The perspective of negotiation theory is adopted and the AHP method is used to analyze the role of ethnic capital in this process. The example of peace negotiations between Ukraine and Russia illustrates the general argument. The resulting negotiation support system – a peace negotiation map – uses a formalized protocol for option generation, pair comparisons, concession rates, and mediation steps. The AHP method assists in aggregating the parties’ priorities in the areas of security, sovereignty, economics, procedural parameters, etc. Extended ethnic capital is introduced as a separate criterion influencing conditions for the compromise. The results of the analysis and simulation of negotiation procedures reveal the impact of the structure of the protocols on the outcome of the process. The presented proposals treat negotiations as a formalized analytical process with clearly defined procedures considering cultural background and communicative aspects. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: ProtoMix-SAM: Prototype-Vicinal Sharpness Minimization for Low-Shot Covariate-Shift Generalization
Abstract: Low-shot classifiers are brittle under covariate shift because small supports induce unstable class boundaries and sharp local minima. We propose ProtoMix-SAM, a two-step optimizer that couples prototype compactness with an inter-prototype margin, prototype-vicinal feature mixing, light perturbation consistency, and uncertainty-adaptive sharpness-aware updates. The method targets controlled low-shot covariate-shift benchmarks that isolate training dynamics from large-scale domain heterogeneity. Across three datasets (Digits, Wine, Iris), three shot regimes (5/10/20 per class), nine synthetic shifts, and five seeds, ProtoMix-SAM attains the best average robust accuracy (86.18%) and the best mean task rank (3.22), winning four of nine tasks. A Friedman test supports overall method differences (χ2 = 18.05, p = 0.0117), although pairwise Holm-corrected Wilcoxon tests are not significant because only nine tasks are available. The study also reveals a clear trade-off: prototype regularization helps accuracy most, whereas vanilla SAM and ASAM remain more calibrated on some Wine tasks. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: Benchmarking Local XAI Against TreeSHAP for Explainable Diabetes Prediction
Abstract: Accurate diabetes risk prediction models are increasingly adopted in clinical decision support. Yet, their practical value depends on how well model decisions can be explained at both global and patient-specific levels. This paper presents an end-to-end framework to compare global and local explainable AI (XAI) methods for tabular diabetes prediction. A diabetes health-indicators dataset (100,000 records with 35+ features) has been trained and evaluated by ten machine learning classifiers to select the best-performing model based on test-set metrics. Then, the global feature importance is computed using TreeSHAP on the entire test set, and three local explanation approaches are benchmarked: Feature Occlusion, BreakDown (DALEX), and LIME on a representative subsample. To determine agreement between global and local explanations, Top-K overlap and rank correlation are measured, and explanation quality is further assessed in terms of faithfulness, stability, complexity, and sparsity. Results show that clinically meaningful biomarkers, such as HbA1c and fasting glucose, consistently dominate both global and local explanations, while BreakDown and Occlusion achieve the highest alignment with global SHAP among local methods. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: Modularization of Domain Ontology Based on DIS
Abstract: Large-scale ontologies often contain excess concepts for specific applications, making ontology reuse and maintenance more difficult. While modularization can extract relevant subsets, existing methods for domain ontologies of Domain Information System (DIS) are limited to the Boolean lattice, lacking fine-grained rooted graph support and automated reduction tools. This paper addresses these gaps by (1) proposing two fine-grained modularization approaches for DIS rooted graphs, (2) developing the DIS Platform, a tool supporting multiple modularization functions and domain adequacy, and (3) constructing the HeartStatus Ontology for validation. Our case studies demonstrate that the tool automates module extraction, minimizing manual intervention and enhancing efficiency. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.
