Authors: Plevnik M.; Jereb B.
Author full names: Plevnik, Mihael (54394059300); Jereb, Borut (24597043000)
Title: Evaluating logistics software quality: A systematic review and research agenda for ISO/IEC 25010 across supply chain digitalization research
Abstract: Logistics organizations depend on software whose quality determines whether digital transformation delivers its operational benefits, yet formal quality evaluation against internationally standardized frameworks is systematically absent in both research and practice. Three interconnected gaps define this research problem: logistics IS practice focuses on functional capabilities rather than quality characteristics; ISO/IEC 25010:2023, the authoritative international standard for software product quality, has never been comprehensively applied to logistics software; and security evaluation remains insufficiently addressed despite mandatory requirements introduced by the EU Cyber Resilience Act. This study addresses these gaps through a systematic literature review conducted under PRISMA 2020 guidelines, encompassing 224 articles from 554 raw records identified across six bibliographic databases — 63% published between 2019 and 2026 — organized into eight thematic groups: blockchain, IoT, Industry 4.0, IT platforms, service quality, cybersecurity, software quality standards, and supply chain digitalization. Of these, only 11 explicitly reference ISO/IEC 25010, and only five apply it directly to logistics software. The review establishes a consistent hierarchy of quality imperatives: compatibility and functional suitability appear in 60% of articles each, reliability in 46%, maintainability in 45%, and interaction capability in 36%, while security appears in only 21% despite its cross-cutting regulatory relevance. These findings provide logistics organizations with an evidence-based quality checklist for software evaluation; developers with design guidance calibrated to logistics demands; and regulators with the empirical foundation for domain-adapted evaluation instruments under the EU Cyber Resilience Act. The study contributes the first systematic literature review explicitly applying a dual logistics-domain and ISO/IEC 25010:2023 lens. On this basis, it proposes a preliminary logistics software quality profile that prioritizes the ISO/IEC 25010 characteristics and links them to logistics indicators, candidate metrics, and evidence types across the principal logistics system types. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Feature-space statistical multi-center modeling for open-set recognition of LPI radar signals
Abstract: Open-set recognition (OSR) of low-probability-of-interception (LPI) radar signals is challenging in non-cooperative environments. Due to parameter variations and low signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), LPI radar features often exhibit multimodal structures. This limits conventional single-center representations, leading to loose acceptance regions and increased false acceptance of unknown samples. To address this issue, this paper devises a feature-space multi-center framework for OSR of LPI radar signals. It represents each known class with multiple local prototypes and a shared within-class covariance matrix to capture complex intra-class distributions. A consistency-driven filtering mechanism calibrates the rejection boundary using validation data, while a class-level prototype configuration strategy adapts model complexity to heterogeneous class structures. Experiments on a simulated LPI radar signal dataset across a wide SNR range show that our solution outperforms several representative baseline approaches in terms of the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and the false positive rate at a 95% true positive rate (FPR@95%TPR). At an SNR of (Formula presented) dB, the proposed method achieves an FPR@95%TPR of 19.09% and an AUROC of 92.11%, indicating effective discrimination under noise-dominated conditions. These results indicate the potential of the proposed method for handling complex intra-class structures in OSR of LPI radar signals under simulated non-cooperative conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: When Words Move Markets: Interpretable Behavioural and Robustness Analysis of LLMs for Financial Sentiment Reasoning via Local Perturbation Explanations
Abstract: Sentiment analysis plays an integral role in the financial sector towards identifying ongoing and emerging market trends. Whilst LLMs perform efficiently in tasks like sentiment prediction, the token-level and contextual understanding behind their decisions remains under-explored. This thereby limits their adoption in regulated domains. This study aims to decipher the reasoning behind how LLMs judge sentiments by taking predictive stability, token-level evidence and contextual cues into account. We apply Generative Statistical Model-Agnostic Interpretability (GSMILE) technique, to examine how a given sentence influences the model output distributions at the local level. We fine-tuned three open-source models to compare their behaviour in this study – Gemma-3-270M by Google, Mistral-7B-Instructv0.1 and Qwen-2.5-0.5B-Instruct. Our analysis shows that LLM sentiment prediction is shaped by how importance is distributed across tokens and their interactions in a sentence. Moreover, the model predictions are driven more by contextual cues than by lexical sentiment cues. These findings suggest that high efficiency alone is insufficient to enable trust in LLM-based predictions, underscoring the importance of interpretability and transparency when using LLMs in financial analytics. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Using LLMs to Score Mathematics Lessons for Instructional Quality with the UTOP
Abstract: Validated classroom observation protocols are useful tools in educational research, but are expensive and invasive to implement. This study sought to investigate the use of AI to reliably score classroom recordings using a validated classroom observation protocol. The UTeach Observation Protocol (UTOP) was designed to assess active and inquiry-based teaching and learning in K-12 STEM classrooms, focusing on more complex and high-inference elements of instruction. We trained 4 experts in STEM education to rate lessons with the UTOP, drawing on a sample of mathematics lesson transcripts from classroom audio recordings. We then had the trained experts each rate 5 new lessons (grades 8-11 mathematics) using the UTOP, and compared their ratings to those generated by GPT-4.1-mini using two prompt-tuned approaches: a rubric-aligned rationale-generation approach and a quote-anchored evidence approach. We found that the reliability of two human raters surpassed the reliability of one human teamed with one AI. However, the AI ratings were substantially above chance in their agreement with human ratings and were moderately correlated to human ratings. The AI models did better on individual indicator ratings than synthesis ratings, and better at rating lesson structure and content than classroom environment or implementation. Using a g-theory approach, we found that having an AI rater to complement a human rater can increase consistency of ratings, particularly for assessing mathematics content. Implications for human-AI teaming to evaluate K-12 instructional quality are given. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Safeguards for Speech2Speech LLM-Assistants: A Case Study in Automotive Applications
Abstract: Recent advances have introduced speech-to-speech (S2S) conversational assistants capable of producing natural-sounding interactions, including non-verbal cues like tonality and mood. In the automotive domain, this enables intuitive and humanlike in-car dialogue experiences. However, integrating these end-to-end assistants limits architectural options for programmable domain-specific safeguards. This paper discusses two implementation approaches for S2S guardrails: transcript-based and tool-based. Through an empirical evaluation, we demonstrate that both strategies are insufficient for industrial deployment in most cases due to prohibitive latency (delaying each answer by 0 to 1.4 s even for computationally cheap checks) and technical impediments (like potentially non-deterministic tool call behavior). Finally, we outline open challenges for S2S guardrails in the automotive context. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: He X.; Zeng J.; Tang H.; Wen J.; Gao M.
Title: Temporal modulation with anchor routing for heterogeneous federated POI recommendation
Abstract: Point-of-interest (POI) recommendation plays a crucial role in location-based services by predicting users’ next visiting locations from historical check-in data. In real-world scenarios, user behaviors exhibit significant temporal heterogeneity, referring to the distribution mismatch of preferences across different time contexts, which is further exacerbated in federated learning due to decentralized and non-IID data. To address this issue, we propose FedTAAR, a federated POI recommendation framework that models temporal heterogeneity at multiple levels. Specifically, to capture dynamic time-aware preferences, we design a temporal decoupled adapter for flexible temporal feature modulation. To mitigate noisy and entangled signals in user sequences, we introduce a semantic anchor routing module that learns stable high-level behavioral patterns. Furthermore, to alleviate parameter conflicts across heterogeneous clients, we develop an anchor-aware aggregation strategy that adaptively adjusts client contributions. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that FedTAAR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods and effectively improves recommendation performance under heterogeneous federated settings. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Classification of Dynamic Libras Signs Related to the Hospital Context Using Recurrent Neural Networks
Abstract: Communication between Brazilian healthcare professionals and Deaf individuals remains a significant challenge in hospital environments, especially due to the scarcity of professionals fluent in Brazilian Sign Language (Libras). In this context, sign recognition systems emerge as a promising alternative to reduce communication barriers. This work proposes the construction of a dataset composed of ten dynamic Libras signs related to hospital triage, as well as the development of recurrent neural network–based models for their classification. The signs are represented by three-dimensional landmarks extracted using MediaPipe Holistic, capturing spatial and temporal information of the movements, which are classified by LSTM networks. Initially, we investigated the 10-class classification problem, achieving an average accuracy of 83.83% and revealing frequent confusions between pairs of semantically similar signs. To address this limitation, we proposed a hierarchical strategy based on expert models, consisting of a general 7-class classifier combined with dedicated models for distinguishing frequently confused signs. This approach resulted in a significant improvement in overall performance, increasing the average accuracy to 92.44% and substantially reducing confusion errors between classes. Additional experiments conducted on an external subject, under less controlled acquisition conditions, achieved an average accuracy of 98.17%, further supporting the generalization capability of the proposed approach. These results indicate the potential of the method for communication support applications in healthcare environments. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Zhou Y.; Dai W.
Title: Proximal dogleg opportunistic majorization for nonconvex and nonsmooth optimization
Abstract: This paper studies a quadratically penalized consensus problem whose objective function consists of a sum of proximable functions and a quadratic penalty term that enforces consistency among variables. Many problems in signal processing and machine learning admit this form, but they become challenging to solve when the proximable terms are both nonconvex and nonsmooth. Existing methods often suffer from slow convergence, complicated implementation, or both. To address these limitations, we propose a fast, easy-to-implement second-order proximal algorithm with provable convergence guarantees. The main idea is to combine a dogleg Newton search with an opportunistic majorization strategy, so that no numerical Hessian approximation is required for the possibly nondifferentiable objective. The surrogate is designed to majorize the quadratic penalty term on the first segment of the dogleg path and preserve this relation on the second segment after restriction to the search path. We prove that the proposed algorithm globally converges to a critical point and establish its local convergence rate under the Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz property. Numerical experiments show that the proposed algorithm converges faster than benchmark methods and consistently attains solutions with lower objective values. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Sequential Counterfactual Inference for Temporal Clinical Data: Addressing the Time Traveler Dilemma
Abstract: Counterfactual inference enables clinicians to ask “what if” questions about patient outcomes, but standard methods assume feature independence and simultaneous modifiability, which could violate the assumptions of longitudinal clinical data. We introduce the Sequential Counterfactual Framework, which respects temporal dependencies in electronic health records by distinguishing immutable features (chronic diagnoses) from controllable features (lab values) and modeling how interventions propagate through time. Applied to 2,723 COVID-19 patients (383 Long COVID heart failure cases, 2,340 matched controls), we demonstrate that 38–67% of patients with chronic conditions would require biologically impossible counterfactuals under naive methods. We identify a cardiorenal cascade (CKD → AKI → HF) with relative risks of 2.27 and 1.19 at each step, illustrating temporal propagation that sequential but not naive counterfactuals can capture. Our framework transforms counterfactual explanation from “what if this feature were different?” to “what if we had intervened earlier, and how would that propagate forward?”, yielding clinically actionable insights grounded in biological plausibility. Title: Impact of Multimodal and Conversational AI on Learning Outcomes and Experience
Abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) offer an opportunity to support multimedia learning through conversational systems grounded in educational content. However, while conversational AI is known to boost engagement, its impact on learning in visually-rich STEM domains remains under-explored. Moreover, there is limited understanding of how multimodality and conversationality jointly influence learning in generative AI systems. This work reports findings from a randomized controlled online study (N=124) comparing three approaches to learning biology from textbook content: (1) a document-grounded conversational AI with interleaved text-and-image responses (MuDoC), (2) a document-grounded conversational AI with text-only responses (TexDoC), and (3) a textbook interface with semantic search and highlighting (DocSearch). Learners using MuDoC achieved the highest post-test scores and reported the most positive learning experience. Notably, while TexDoC was rated as significantly more engaging and easier to use than DocSearch, it led to the lowest post-test scores, revealing a disconnect between student perceptions and learning outcomes. Interpreted through the lens of the Cognitive Load Theory, these findings suggest that conversationality reduces extraneous load, while visual-verbal integration induced by multimodality increases germane load, leading to better learning outcomes. When conversationality is not complemented by multimodality, reduced cognitive effort may instead inflate perceived understanding without improving learning outcomes. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: SmartBrew Advisor: A Hybrid Conversational Recommender System for Brewing Product Guidance
Abstract: Conversational Recommender Systems (CRSs) are emerging as a transformative paradigm in human-AI interaction, enabling users to express preferences, refine recommendations, and receive explanations in natural language. However, generic models often struggle with domain-specific accuracy and hallucinations. This article presents the design and validation of a Hybrid Conversational Recommender System (H-CRS) applied to the brewing domain. The proposed architecture integrates Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to ensure factual grounding and avoid hallucinations, the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for standardized integration of tools and memory, and Large Language Models (LLMs) orchestrated via chain-of-thought frameworks and vector stores. To assess the system’s efficacy, we employed a comprehensive dual-validation strategy. First, we compared the H-CRS with a standard ChatGPT baseline on six experimental topics designed to simulate realistic customer interactions. Second, we conducted a human-centered evaluation using structured feedback to assess clarity, relevance, and naturalness. The results demonstrate that while generic models perform adequately in casual dialog, the proposed H-CRS delivers superior accuracy, catalog-specific grounding, and conversational stability. Furthermore, user feedback indicates that combining domain knowledge with conversational intelligence meaningfully enhances decision support and user engagement. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Beyond the Gold Standard: Reliability Estimation of Human and GenAI Scoring
Abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) has advanced rapidly, yet current evaluations of GenAI-based automated scoring continue to rely on traditional metrics that assume human scores represent the gold standard. However, human scoring is inherently prone to subjectivity and rater variability. To address these limitations, this study applied the Linguistic-integrated Reliability Audit (LiRA) framework, which automatically generates data-driven benchmark scores. We estimated and compared the reliability of human and GenAI scoring for six constructed response items from PIRLS across all participating countries. Results demonstrated that GenAI scoring achieved consistently higher reliability (97.21%) than human scoring (95.23%) across items and countries. These findings challenge the conventional reliance on human scores as the gold standard and support a paradigm shift toward automated, reproducible reliability estimation. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Application of Artificial Intelligence Tools in Modern Auditing
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: Modern auditing is being transformed and taking on new dimensions with the development of artificial intelligence (AI). Globally, practices that apply AI tools in control testing, detection of irregularities, and processing of unstructured data have already been developed and proven highly successful, indicating both the need and significant potential for introducing such practices in audit firms in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The advantages of using AI tools in auditing are reflected in increased accuracy in data verification necessary for forming an audit opinion, faster generation of reports, more efficient analysis of large datasets, automation of routine tasks, and quicker identification of irregularities that indicate business areas requiring more detailed examination. This paper presents primary research conducted on a sample of audit professionals with the aim of examining their perceptions regarding the use of AI. The defined sample consists of 126 respondents who answered 40 survey questions. In addition to professionals from Bosnia and Herzegovina, the research also includes, to a lesser extent, professionals from Serbia and Slovenia, enabling a clearer overview of both the current situation and the potential for the application of AI in auditing. The research conclusions were drawn using appropriate statistical methodologies applied to primary descriptive scales, which enable the measurement of the impact and interrelationships of respondents’ attitudes, thereby ensuring an adequate assessment of perceptions regarding the methods and effects of AI usage in auditing. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Bridging AI and Cooperative Learning: A Jigsaw-Based Instructional Model for Embedded Systems
Abstract: This study investigates the effects of integrating Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) and Jigsaw Cooperative Learning in an embedded systems course on undergraduate students’ learning outcomes. Embedded systems courses are highly practical and complex, requiring students to possess strong computational thinking and problem-solving skills. However, traditional teaching methods often fail to effectively enhance learning outcomes and depth of understanding. To address this issue, this study incorporates a GAI-assisted learning mechanism that provides real-time feedback and learning support, combined with the Jigsaw cooperative learning strategy to promote knowledge construction and interactive learning among students. A quasi-experimental design was adopted, with undergraduate students as participants. The students were divided into an experimental group and a control group. The experimental group received instruction through a GAI-supported Jigsaw cooperative learning approach, while the control group was taught using traditional instructional methods. Learning outcomes were evaluated through pre-test and post-test scores. The results indicate that the GAI-supported Jigsaw cooperative learning approach significantly improves students’ learning outcomes and outperforms traditional teaching methods. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Towards Predicting Sedation Depth in Endoscopy with Large Clinically Annotated EEG Data of Continuous Propofol Sedation
Abstract: Brain function monitors are a widely used tool in general anesthesia. For monitoring drug effects in procedural sedation, however, no objective device is currently available. While available monitors offer no clinically significant benefit in sedation, the reasons are not well understood and labeled data lacking. To enable a data-driven approach for sedation depth prediction, we collected 2-channel fronto-temporal EEG signals enhanced with additional biosignals during Propofol sedation for gastrointestinal and bronchoscopic endoscopies. A total of 171 recordings were annotated in real-time with clinical events and the State of Consciousness (SoC) as well as clinical Sedation Depth. Overall, 78.5 h of multimodal biosignal data with 1129 transitions of the SoC and 7328 sedation depth data points measured on the MOAA/S scale have been collected. Applying advanced feature engineering and basic machine learning, we demonstrate that this data is suitable for predicting SoC and provides a sound foundation for research towards a reliable prediction of sedation depth. Notably, we introduce the underlying DOSE-I dataset as the first public large-scale EEG-based multimodal dataset in routine procedural sedation with rich clinical labeling. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Bridging the Gap Between Validated Cognitive Screening and Clinical Practice: A Stylus-Driven Digital Use Case for the SAGE Test
Abstract: Early detection of cognitive decline can improve outcomes. The SAGE is a cognitive assessment test and is currently one of the standard tools used in medicine for the early diagnosis of Alzheimer’s and dementia. The aim of this work is to propose a software framework for the test, with the objective of retaining the original structure whilst bringing the benefits of digitisation, such as reducing the amount of paper documentation to be stored, speeding up the calculation of scores and the generation of reports, and enabling data to be archived in digital format for future comparison. The proposed system is a single-page web application accessible via a tablet and supporting stylus input. The system collects the user-entered data on the web page, presents the exercises and various tasks included in the test, then automatically organises them into a data structure and provides a report with a partial score to healthcare staff. The partial score is based on exercises with pre-set scores, which helps to speed up the work of the staff. The resulting code is finally released under an open-source licence. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: An Agentic AI-Based Prototype to Support Teaching-Learning Processes
Abstract: Current educational systems face increasing demands for pedagogical innovation, particularly in higher education (HE), where the need for personalized support and timely feedback often exceeds the capacity of traditional methods to meet these needs. This paper presents a prototype based on agentic AI to support two main teaching and learning processes in HE. The prototype, built with a flexible design, aims to use the advanced abilities of large language models to provide better, more relevant information and help everyone involved in teaching and learning. The system employs traceable agents and tools that enable students to access contextualized responses to solve problems and support teachers in creating structured lesson plans based on the ADDIE model and the analysis of real-world needs. Title: Agnoagentia: The Illusion of Agency in AI-Assisted Learning
Abstract: This study examines learners’ perceived and enacted agency when interacting with different AI systems during collaborative writing tasks. A total of 52 university students, randomly grouped into 26 dyads consecutively completed three collaborative writing tasks under three conditions: (a) “Baseline” collaboration via chat and collaborative text editor, (b) “Clair”, same as the Baseline, but with a pedagogically structured collaborative conversational agent (Clair) supporting student discussions, and (c) “ChatGPT”, same as Baseline, but students had additionally individual access to ChatGPT (using GPT-5). Perceived agency was assessed by self-reported measures based on the Sense of Agency Scale. Enacted agency was evaluated through coding dyad dialogues using Bandura’s four core properties: forethought, self-reactiveness, intentionality, self-reflectiveness. Whereas Clair had some positive impact on self-reflectiveness, ChatGPT significantly reduced the communication volume, while increasing offloading behaviour, i.e., delegating the task to ChatGPT. Results revealed a paradox: ChatGPT-assisted students reported high perceived agency, while demonstrating low enacted agency. We term this phenomenon agnoagentia, the illusory perception of agency that emerges when learners interact with GenAI tools, unaware that their enacted agency has been displaced. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: KRAG: Refining Knowledge for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Through Kahneman-Tversky Optimization
Abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) improves the factuality of large language models by incorporating external documents, but its performance can degrade when retrieved passages are irrelevant, redundant, or misleading. To overcome the limitations of retrieval noise, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) incorporates external knowledge sources to enhance response reliability; however, its efficacy is heavily limited by (i) the relevance and quality of retrieved documents and (ii) the model’s capacity to utilize such information effectively. Noisy or redundant retrieval results can introduce distractions and compromise output integrity. In response to the factual inaccuracies, we propose Knowledge-Refined RAG (KRAG), a knowledge refinement method that repurposes the LLM as an active knowledge refiner. Under this approach, each retrieved text passage is first condensed into a concise chain-of-thought rationale that captures its potential relevance to the query. These rationales are then evaluated by a lightweight, trainable evaluator, which outputs binary (good/bad) feedback to construct positive and negative samples for fine-tuning the LLM, thus enabling it to learn to generate higher-quality refined rationales among these candidate outputs based on all retrieved documents. Experimental results show that KRAG improves the average score over RankCoT by 1.68, 1.39, and 1.35 points on Llama3-8B-Instruct, MiniCPM3-4B, and Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, respectively. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Authors: Hou Z.; Zhang J.; Liu Y.; Li Q.; Hu L.
Title: A Coarse-to-Fine Spectral Alignment Framework for Traffic Signal Optimization
Abstract: Finding the right signal offsets along a corridor—so that platoons hit green lights instead of red ones—depends on how well we can match upstream departures to downstream arrivals. Grid search checks every integer lag, which costs ON2 and misses fractional shifts entirely; evolutionary solvers like PSO and CMA-ES do explore continuous offsets, but they tend to converge slowly and sometimes get trapped in poor local optima. We propose HCCR-E2 to deal with both problems at once. The idea is a two-phase pipeline. Phase 1 uses FFT cross-correlation (ONlogN) for a rough integer alignment, then zooms in with the Chirp-Z Transform (CZT) to pin down a sub-sample shift; we also swap in cubic spline interpolation before the correlation step, which we find noticeably sharpens the peak and cuts phase distortion. Phase 2 takes those per-movement shifts as a starting point and runs coordinate descent with a cell-transmission-model simulation as the loss function, so the offsets get tuned jointly at the corridor level. We tested HCCR-E2 on a 6-intersection corridor built from real GM trajectory data. Compared with the Phase 1 baseline, total delay drops by 8.28% and total stops by 7.66%, beating all nine comparison methods. The same ranking holds on the NGSIM Peachtree Street corridor (p < 0.01, Wilcoxon). © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: A Comparative Study of Expert-Novice Design Thinking Processes Using NotebookLM
Abstract: This study explores cognitive processes of novice learners and an external expert reference case during AI-assisted design thinking activities supported by Lovable AI. An exploratory qualitative case study design was employed to examine differences in cognitive structuring in a small-scale, task-based AI-assisted design task. Data were collected through think-aloud protocols and semi-structured interviews during website landing page design tasks. The analysis combined thematic coding and SOLO Taxonomy to identify variations in cognitive complexity across participants, supported by MAXQDA and NotebookLM for data organization and visualization during the analytical process. Findings indicate that novice learners tended to engage in exploratory and reactive, trial-based reasoning characterized by fragmented design structuring and strong reliance on AI-generated outputs. In contrast, the expert reference case demonstrated more structured, goal-oriented, and reflective cognitive processes involving planning, evaluation, and coherent integration of design elements. These differences suggest that AI-assisted design environments may amplify existing variations in cognitive organization rather than standardize learner performance. NotebookLM functioned as an analytical support tool for structuring think-aloud data prior to formal coding. Overall, the study provides preliminary insights into how AI-supported design tools interact with learner cognition and how AI-assisted qualitative analysis tools can support exploratory research in educational contexts. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: From Ethical Discourse to Empirical Evidence: How Ethical Concerns are Operationalized in Studies on Generative AI in Higher Education
Abstract: The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in higher education has raised widespread ethical concerns, particularly in computer science (CS) education. While issues such as academic integrity, fairness, bias, and responsibility are frequently discussed, it remains unclear how these concerns are empirically examined in existing research. This paper presents a systematic analysis of how ethically relevant concerns are addressed in peer-reviewed empirical studies on GenAI use in higher CS education. Using a structured selection protocol, we analyze a corpus of empirical studies published since the public release of large language models, focusing on how concerns such as academic integrity, fairness, bias, responsibility and student autonomy are defined, studied, and methodologically grounded. Our analysis reveals a substantial gap between ethical discourse and empirical practice: although ethics is often mentioned, only a small subset of studies integrates ethically relevant concerns as a core analytical dimension with explicit empirical grounding. Most studies rely on indirect proxies or address ethics implicitly, without clear operational definitions or evaluative frameworks. Based on these findings, we propose an empirically grounded categorization of ethical concerns as addressed in current research and outline methodological directions for more robust integration of ethics into future empirical studies on GenAI-supported CS education. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Ran R.; Gai K.; Yu J.
Title: EATER: Entropy-Aware Multi-bit Watermarking for Large Language Models
Abstract: The extensive generative capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) are causing the potential to increase abuse and misuse of AI-generated contents, which makes annotation and detection be critical tasks. Embedding watermarks into models is considered an effective approach that is imperceptible to humans but can be easily detected using specific algorithms. However, compared to the image and audio domains, the text domain possesses relatively limited redundancy. Most existing watermarking methods struggle to be effectively applied in scenarios requiring substantial embedding space, including low-entropy generation tasks and when it is necessary to embed multi-bit watermarks for advanced traceability. To address this challenge, in this work we propose a novel entropy-aware multi-bit watermarking framework. Specifically, by developing an entropy-aware filtering module, we estimate context entropy in real time to filter out invalid watermark spaces. Simultaneously, we integrate a multi-bit position allocation strategy to efficiently utilize the remaining space, thereby enabling trustworthy traceability of multi-bit watermark information in diverse generation scenarios. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that our scheme improves text quality across various generation scenarios while maintaining high multi-bit decoding accuracy, providing a practical solution for the trustworthy traceability of LLMs. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: A Variational Quantum Classifier Applied to Romanian Financial Data: Insights into Energy-Pharmaceutical Sector Relations
Abstract: Variational Quantum Classifiers (VQCs) are hybrid algorithms that combine classical machine learning with quantum computing techniques, aiming to improve upon traditional classification approaches. In this paper, we test the hypothesis that daily price variations in selected Romanian energy-sector stocks contain predictive information about the daily direction of price variation in a major Romanian pharmaceutical stock. We further examine whether a shallow variational quantum classifier can model these cross-sector nonlinear dependencies more effectively than standard classical classifiers. Our expectation is not a provable computational quantum advantage, but a possible empirical modeling benefit arising from quantum feature embedding and entangling layers in a low-dimensional classification setting. Title: Neural network-based design of variable fractional-delay FIR filters with controllable cutoff frequency
Abstract: Variable fractional-delay (VFD) finite impulse response (FIR) filters with controllable cutoff frequencies play an important role in practical bandlimited signal applications. The Farrow structure has long been a standard structure for VFD filter design, offering real-time fractional delay adjustment through multiple subfilters. However, the coefficients of fixed subfilters require complete redesign when cutoff frequencies change. To solve the coefficients redesign problem, this paper proposes a deep learning (DL)-based framework for the design of VFD FIR filters with controllable cutoff frequencies, which redefines the VFD filter design as an end-to-end mapping from design parameters (low cutoff frequency, high cutoff frequency, and fractional delay) directly to filter coefficients, offering a higher degree of freedom in the design process. Title: A Novel Two-Stage Machine Learning Framework for Physician Churn Prediction and Promotion Period Estimation in Family Health Information Systems: A Hybrid Feature Selection and Multi-Model Approach with Statistical Validation
Abstract: Family Health Information System (FHIS) vendors in Türkiye operate in a market of approximately twenty competitors, where annual physician attrition rates of 8–10% create significant revenue erosion. This paper proposes the first domain-specific two-stage machine learning framework for FHIS physician churn, addressing both at-risk physician identification and optimal promotion period estimation. Stage 1 evaluates Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), Logistic Regression, and Support Vector Machine (SVM, four kernels) for binary churn classification on 4,229 physician records (churn rate 24.5%); Stage 2 evaluates LightGBM, XGBoost, and a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) for promotion-duration regression (0–6 months) on 3,195 records. Title: Ethical Integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education: Student Practices, Risks, and Institutional Governance

Abstract: Generative AI is already reshaping higher education. Title: What Children’s AI Literacy Books Teach: A Content Analysis Using the AI4K12 Framework
Abstract: Although many books introducing artificial intelligence (AI) to young children are now available, their quality and educational value have not been systematically or empirically examined. This study addresses this gap by analyzing how AI literacy books conceptualize and communicate foundational AI ideas, practices, and values to young learners. Guided by the AI4K12 “Five Big Ideas in AI” framework, we conducted a mixed-methods content analysis of 57 English-language AI literacy books for children ages 5–8. Results revealed an uneven distribution of AI Big Ideas introduced by these books. Societal Impact, Learning, and Natural Interaction were emphasized, whereas Perception, Representation and Reasoning, which capture foundational technical mechanisms, were comparatively underrepresented. To examine the variation across books, we calculated per-book relative frequencies and conducted a cluster analysis, which revealed five recurring book profiles dominated by different combinations of Big Ideas. Title: Evaluating AI as Part of Social Mechanisms
Abstract: This article proposes a methodology for evaluating AI systems as components of social mechanisms rather than isolated artefacts. The research question we answer in the paper is: How can an AI system’s contribution to a human–agent mechanism be assessed with respect to collective outcomes, welfare, norms, and risks? Combining mechanism design with analytical sociology, we propose the Star–Durkheim test as a diagnostic instrument for asking which collective goal is implemented, how welfare and fairness are affected, and which causal social dynamics may emerge. The test does not ask whether an AI appears human as done in the well-known Turing test, but investigates whether it contributes to, distorts, or endangers a socially situated mechanism. Title: Spatio-Temporal Decoupling Network with Frequency Domain Enhancement for Traffic Forecasting
Abstract: A major challenge in traffic forecasting lies in the coupled modeling of spatial relationships and temporal evolution, which limits the effectiveness of existing approaches. Motivated by this challenge, we propose a Spatio-Temporal Tensor Fusion Network (STTFN), a decoupling framework with frequency-domain enhancement. Specifically, STTFN factorizes the forecasting task into independent temporal and spatial hyper-planes. First, a temporal branch incorporates an Auto-Correlation mechanism to capture and model long-range periodicity in recurring traffic patterns. Then, a spatial branch integrates multi-view graph convolutions with a Frequency Domain Block for robust spatial relation learning, balancing topological feature extraction with global structural enhancement. Finally, a Hadamard-based tensor fusion module aggregates the decoupled representations. Experiments on PeMS04 and PeMS08 datasets demonstrate that STTFN outperforms representative baselines. Title: CatalogAgent: A Supervisor-Mediated Self-Learning System Enabling Context Engineering for GenAI Models
Abstract: Product catalogs are the backbone of e-commerce sites, yet a large number of structured attributes (SAs)—such as material, color, and shape often have missing values. Typically, SA values are extracted from product information, including titles and descriptions. While LLM-based generator-evaluator frameworks have demonstrated effectiveness for SA prediction—where an LLM generates SA values and another evaluates them—they face challenges when the Generator and Evaluator produce conflicting outputs, as either component can make mistakes. We introduce CatalogAgent, a novel agentic system that continuously improves Generator and Evaluator models for e-commerce catalog enrichment. When disagreements arise from (1) internal conflicts between the LLM-based Generator and Evaluator, or (2) external feedback from sellers on LLM outputs, a Supervisor Agent intervenes to mediate these conflicts and make final decisions. The system also incorporates a Memory Base and a Memory Summarizer that stores Supervisor Agent activities from individual cases and aggregates patterns into learnings. These learnings are fed back to the worker Generator and Evaluator LLMs, enabling self-improvement without human intervention. Through context engineering—injecting learnings and insights into worker LLMs’ contexts—the system successfully transfers the Supervisor’s capabilities to the Generator and Evaluator, improving their performance by 15.24% and 13.98%, respectively. Title: From Swipes to Subscriptions: Consumers’ Attitudes on Dating Apps
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: Mobile dating applications rely predominantly on a subscription-based revenue model, requiring users to pay a premium price to access enhanced features and functionalities. Nevertheless, while the freemium-to-premium conversion is essential for profitability, converting a substantial portion of users into paying customers remains difficult. Through the development of a conceptual model that integrates two dominant consumer behaviour frameworks, namely the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) Theory and the extended Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), this study explores the factors influencing users’ purchase intentions within dating applications by focusing on the intrapersonal motivations, perceived value, and attitudes toward the platforms. Qualitative and quantitative methods were employed in this research, including an online questionnaire and semi-structured interviews. The findings from these methodologies suggest that while hedonic and utilitarian motivations influence dating application users’ initial engagement with the platforms, these factors primarily shape their perceived value rather than directly drive in-app purchase intentions. Additionally, consumer attitudes toward dating applications are crucial in shaping purchasing decisions. However, dissatisfaction with the applications and stigma often leads to low conversion rates from freemium to premium services. The study offers theoretical contributions to research on consumer behaviour on digital platforms. It provides practical recommendations for dating app developers and communication strategists seeking to enhance user engagement and monetization strategies. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Scalable and Explainable Learner-Video Interaction Prediction Using Multimodal Large Language Models
Abstract: Learners’ use of video controls in educational videos provides implicit signals of cognitive processing and instructional design quality, yet the lack of scalable and explainable predictive models limits instructors’ ability to anticipate such behavior before deployment. Our approach leverages multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to compute embeddings of short video segments and trains a neural classifier to identify temporally fine-grained interaction peaks. Drawing from multimedia learning theory on instructional design for optimal cognitive load, we code features of the video segments using GPT-5 and employ them as a basis for interpreting model predictions via concept activation vectors. We evaluate our pipeline on 77 million video control events from 66 online courses. Our findings demonstrate that classifiers based on MLLM embeddings reliably predict interaction peaks, generalize to unseen academic fields, and encode interpretable, theory-relevant instructional concepts. Title: An empirical study on method-level performance evolution in open-source Java projects
Abstract: Performance is a critical quality attribute in software development, yet the impact of method-level code changes on performance evolution remains poorly understood. While developers often make intuitive assumptions about which types of modifications are likely to cause performance regressions or improvements, these beliefs lack empirical validation at a fine-grained level. We conducted a large-scale empirical study analyzing performance evolution in 15 mature open-source Java projects hosted on GitHub. Our analysis encompassed 739 commits containing 1,499 method-level code changes, using Java Microbenchmark Harness (JMH) to benchmark the performance of these methods before and after the changes, thereafter measuring the significance and magnitude of the performance variations. We employed bytecode instrumentation to capture method-specific execution metrics and systematically analyzed four key aspects: the performance change patterns, the impact of code change types, the developer and complexity factors, as well as the impact of project domain and size. Our findings reveal that 32.7% of method-level changes result in measurable performance impacts, with regressions occurring 1.3 times more frequently than improvements (18.5% vs 14.2%). We also observe that certain code change types, such as algorithmic changes, demonstrate a higher chance of performance improvement, but also carry substantial regression risks. While senior developers produce more stable changes, junior developers are more likely to be associated with aggressive performance changes; besides, we observe an increasing trend of performance regressions associated with more complex code. Finally, our findings show that different project domains and scales exhibit distinct performance characteristics, which suggest the need for domain-specific performance management strategies that account for the project scales. Title: OWseg-WE: An effective method for open-world semantic segmentation of ginkgo biloba pests and diseases

Title: Beyond Generic Answers and Empty Praise: The Differential Impact of AI Companionship Roles on Social-Emotional Learning in University Student Intervention

Title: Prompt-Guided Feature Calibration for Multi-modal Object Re-identification with Missing Modalities

Title: Valuation of Science and Technology Innovation Enterprises Using a GA-XGBoost-SHAP Model
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: Science and technology innovation enterprises are characterized by high technological barriers, intensive R&D investment, and substantial uncertainty in future growth, which pose challenges to traditional valuation approaches. This study develops an integrated valuation framework combining Genetic Algorithm (GA), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Using data from high-tech firms listed on China’s Science and Technology Innovation Board and the Growth Enterprise Market during 2021–2023, we refine an initial set of 55 indicators to 33 through Spearman correlation analysis. The GA is employed to optimize XGBoost hyperparameters, while SHAP is used to explain feature contributions and improve model interpretability. Empirical results indicate that our proposed framework exhibits better predictive accuracy and robustness compared with benchmark models. Moreover, it effectively captures the joint effects of growth potential and intangible assets, providing interpretable insights at the feature level. The contributions of this study to the literature are twofold. First, it develops a relatively comprehensive and optimized indicator system for valuing innovation-driven enterprises. Second, it proposes an accurate and interpretable machine learning framework for enterprise valuation. Title: Cyber Resilience Through LLM-Enhanced Vulnerability Reports
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: Decentralized, heterogeneous, and self-administered IT infrastructures pose major challenges to cyber resilience. For example, in academia and research institutions, each research group requires its own set of IT systems. Frequently, those systems are managed part-time by local system administrators (LSAs) without formal IT security education. A common option to increase cyber resilience in such scenarios is to perform vulnerability scans on the institution’s IP address range. However, LSAs are often overwhelmed by the technical depth of the scan reports. A promising solution is to have a large language model (LLM) translate the reports into a less demanding, more actionable form. In this paper, we present a mixed-method study (n = 21) with LSAs from Leipzig University. Our study investigates how LLM-enhanced vulnerability scan reports affect the LSAs’ remediation capabilities. Our findings reveal that LSAs’ backgrounds are even more diverse than one might think, with varying levels of technical understanding. LLM-translated reports allow them to fix common vulnerabilities much faster, without requiring central IT support. However, complex issues still require expert support and knowledge. Our results help design vulnerability communication approaches that strengthen cyber resilience in heterogeneous environments. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Damocles: Relational Event Modeling on Heterogeneous Temporal Graphs for Window-Level Anomaly Detection
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: System audit logs provide fine-grained behavioral evidence for anomaly detection and can be naturally represented as heterogeneous temporal graphs. However, existing temporal graph methods often underexploit heterogeneous relation semantics and short-term pairwise interaction context, leading to less discriminative reconstruction errors for window-level detection. We propose Damocles, a relation-aware event modeling framework built on a dynamic graph backbone. Damocles introduces a Heterogeneous Dynamic Graph Attention module to jointly capture structural dependencies, typed relation semantics, and local temporal context, a pair-state-aware event decoder to improve event-type reconstruction, and an IDF-aware decoupled scoring mechanism for window-level anomaly detection. Experiments on three DARPA Transparent Computing datasets show that Damocles consistently improves event reconstruction over Kairos and yields more precise window-level detection. Title: What Do AI Agents Actually Change? An Empirical Taxonomy of Mutation Patterns in Performance-Improving Pull Requests
Abstract: AI coding agents are black boxes: we cannot inspect how they generate code, but we can inspect what they change. This distinction matters for search-based software engineering (SBSE), where techniques such as genetic improvement—in the performance-optimisation application we study—depend on mutation operators that reflect how code is actually transformed. Fewer than 1% of the 33,596 agent PRs in AIDev-pop target performance, making each case a rare window into otherwise opaque agent behaviour. We classify 1,254 performance-relevant diff hunks from 216 of these PRs, spanning five agent systems, against the 18-category syntactic mutation taxonomy of Even-Mendoza et al. (2025) using a dual-LLM intersection pipeline. Three categories dominate: name_modification (37.0%), object_creation (26.4%), and type_change (22.7%), a profile markedly different from prior GI corpora where no_change accounted for 84%. Each agent’s deployed system commits to a distinctive mutation vocabulary, and each performance strategy activates a largely disjoint category subset. Agent identity and target strategy are therefore informative priors that narrow the effective SBSE operator space. Title: TabRLLM: Tabular Data Generation via Local-to-Global Rule Extraction in Low-Data Regimes
Abstract: Machine learning on tabular data is often constrained by data scarcity, especially in domains where data collection is expensive or highly sensitive. Although data generation is widely adopted to alleviate this problem, existing approaches frequently fail to capture complex cross-feature dependencies and implicit business rules. To address these challenges in low-data regimes, we propose TabRLLM, which leverages large language models for semantic feature grouping. It extracts partial-table integrity rules and integrates them into full-table constraints. TabRLLM further combines these rules with statistical constraints, including marginal distributions and feature correlations, and converts them into prompts to guide data generation. Title: Can LLMs Mimic Experienced Neurosurgeons in Real-World Spine Surgery Triage?
Abstract: Low back and neck pain are leading causes of disability, and some patients require surgical intervention to prevent long-term complications. Current triage workflows rely on MRI reports, questionnaires, and in-person assessment. However, many referred patients are ultimately managed non-surgically, contributing to long wait times and inefficient use of specialist resources. Automated decision support that distinguishes surgical from non-surgical cases could improve prioritization and care pathways. This study investigates large language models (LLMs) for surgical triage using real-world data from the Spine Assessment Clinic in Edmonton, Canada. The dataset includes MRI reports and patient questionnaires, reflecting routine clinical inputs. We first evaluate conventional machine learning methods and find that these approaches perform poorly due to class imbalance, limited labelled data, and the complexity of radiology narratives. We then explore prompt-based use of open-source LLMs as an alternative to gradient-based training. LLMs outperform conventional models in this low-resource setting, particularly in unambiguous cases. Ablation analyses indicate that neither data modality alone is sufficient, but their combination yields the most reliable triage performance. To the best of our knowledge, this work presents the first evaluation of LLMs for spine surgery triage on real-world clinical data. We benchmark multiple methods, examine multimodal integration strategies, and assess agreement with expert labels, highlighting both the promise and limitations of LLM-based clinical decision support. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Physics-Informed Gaussian Process with Sequential Virtual Point Selection for Constrained Regression
Abstract: To address the drawbacks of poor physical consistency and weak generalization in traditional purely data-driven modeling, physics-informed Gaussian process can incorporate constraints such as boundedness and monotonicity. By leveraging virtual points, global constraints are transformed into constraints imposed on a finite set of virtual points. In this paper, a novel sequential virtual point selection strategy is proposed. On the basis of the constraint violation probability criterion, a distance penalty term is introduced to enhance the diversity of virtual points, which not only avoids computational difficulties in matrix operations caused by point aggregation but also significantly reduces the computational burden arising from virtual point searching. Compared with unconstrained Gaussian processes and other existing methods, the proposed approach yields predictions with higher physical consistency and lower generalization errors. Title: A Systematic Review of Computer Vision-Based Approaches in Educational Contexts
Abstract: Computer vision has emerged as an important artificial intelligence technology in educational research, enabling the automated analysis of visual learning data such as student behavior, movement, engagement, and interaction. Although an increasing number of empirical studies have explored its educational applications, existing research remains fragmented and insufficiently synthesized. To address this gap, this systematic review examines how computer vision technologies have been implemented across educational contexts. Guided by the PRISMA framework, empirical studies published between 2021 and 2025 were identified through searches of Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar. Following a multi-stage screening and eligibility process, thirty studies were selected for in-depth analysis. The studies were coded according to technology type, educational domain, instructional tasks, learning outcomes, methodological design, advantages, and limitations. The findings show that deep learning-based computer vision models and pose estimation technologies are the most frequently used approaches, primarily supporting automated monitoring of student behavior and engagement, performance assessment, and classroom analytics. Applications were most common in higher education, STEM disciplines, physical education, and performance-based learning contexts. Learning outcomes predominantly focused on engagement, behavioral regulation, and motor skill development, while cognitive outcomes were reported less consistently. Despite clear advantages such as objective assessment, real-time feedback, and reduced teacher workload, challenges related to technical robustness, scalability, ethical concerns, and limited pedagogical integration were widely reported. The review highlights the need for theory-informed, pedagogy-driven, and ethically grounded research to advance the meaningful integration of computer vision in education. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: What To Transfer: Refined Transfer Framework for Universal Cross-Domain Recommendation
Abstract: Cross-domain recommendation (CDR) improves target-domain recommendation by leveraging behavioral signals from auxiliary domains, alleviating data sparsity and cold-start issues. Universal cross-domain recommendation (UniCDR) further learns a single model to unify multi-domain preferences and support both dual-domain and multi-domain scenarios. However, incorporating source-domain information can even hurt target-domain performance, a phenomenon known as negative transfer. This is because cross-domain signals are not uniformly beneficial: representation learning may capture shortcut cues that break under domain shift, and static fusion may further propagate such unreliable components into the target representation. To explicitly address what to transfer, we propose the Refined Transfer Framework (RTF), an end-to-end architecture that decouples robust representation learning from selective cross-domain fusion. At the representation layer, RTF employs a temperature-scaled attention encoder over the source history and the global history, together with popularity down-weighting to suppress shortcut cues. At the fusion layer, we introduce a domain-routed decoder that aligns multi-source representations in a shared space and selectively fuses auxiliary signals with a global fallback. Finally, we optimize RTF with recommendation supervision and dual contrastive objectives to enhance intra-view robustness and cross-view consistency. Extensive experiments on Amazon benchmarks across four UniCDR scenarios demonstrate that RTF yields competitive and stable improvements over strong baselines. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: ACTMNet: Adaptive channel-temporal mixing net for multivariate time series forecasting
Abstract: Multivariate time series forecasting requires simultaneously capturing temporal dynamics and inter-channel dependencies. Current channel-independent (CI) methods neglect inter-channel correlations, whereas channel-dependent (CD) approaches can introduce noise when those correlations are weak. To exploit the CD strategy’s ability to model cross-channel dependencies while preserving each channel’s private characteristics and mitigating noise from weakly related channels, we propose the Adaptive Channel-Temporal Mixing Net (ACTMNet). ACTMNet introduces an Adaptive Channel-Temporal Feature Coupling (ACTFC) module that adaptively disentangles and fuses private and shared features, followed by a Temporal Feature Modeling (TFM) module that integrates the resulting global representations with the original sequences to explicitly model temporal dynamics. We evaluate ACTMNet on seven benchmark datasets: the cross-dataset average MSE and MAE are 0.340 and 0.344, respectively. Title: Regenerating Historical, Landscape, and Environmental Heritage Through the Municipal Territorial Plan in Lombardy
Abstract: Heritage-induced urban and landscape regenerations are imperative in highly urbanised territories. Integrated spatio-temporal historical knowledge needs to directly inform the legal documentation of municipal planning. Title: The Current State of AI for Conversion of Mathematics to and from Braille
Abstract: There are many different braille codes for mathematics around the world. Most have limited or no support for reading online mathematical content or for entry and conversion from those codes to math notation. Meanwhile, AI has had tremendous success with language translation. We investigate the use of AI to translate to and from two of the most widely used braille codes, testing several different techniques across leading commercial and open-weight large language models. In our best configuration, accuracy reached 92% for both Nemeth-to-MathML and MathML-to-Nemeth conversion using thousands of examples. By contrast, results for translating to and from UEB were lower. Although there are some caveats to these numbers, it appears that translation of technical braille is nearing viability. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Di S.; Li Z.; Chen F.; Liang B.
Title: TAPE: Trend-Aware Perturbation Enhancement for Sparse Stepwise Non-stationary Time Series
Abstract: Sparse Stepwise Non-Stationary Time-Series (SSNT) arise in many real-world domains, where long plateaus and abrupt regime shifts yield discontinuous supervision and sparse gradients. This violates the smooth-dynamics assumption underlying most deep forecasters, leading to overfitting on stationary segments and weak modelling of transition dynamics. We introduce TAPE (Trend-Aware Perturbation Enhancement), a purely data-centric and model-agnostic framework that improves transition sensitivity without modifying backbone architectures. TAPE identifies volatile regions, extracts multi-scale trend cues, and synthesizes structured perturbations to enrich supervision signals in flat segments while preserving stepwise semantics. Across real estate and financial datasets, TAPE improves forecasting performance across all evaluated metrics and architectures (recurrent and attention-based), with no observed degradation in any experiment, demonstrating that trend-aware perturbation is an effective mechanism for enhancing robustness under sparse or discontinuous temporal dynamics. Additional validation on a quasi-periodic medical dataset further confirms that the benefit of injecting trend-aware signals generalises beyond stepwise regimes. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Authors: Lou Z.; Wang Y.; Xin Y.; Qin B.; Ye W.
Title: NutMuse: Inspiring Creative Ideation for Nut Carving with GenAI
Abstract: Nut carving is a traditional Chinese micro-carving craft that imposes strict constraints on creative ideation due to the irregular shapes, textures, and structural limitations of the raw materials. Although generative AI has shown promise in supporting creative exploration, generic image-generation tools remain insufficient for nut carving, where artisans must reason not only about visual style but also about craft-specific terminology and material characteristics. To better understand these needs, we conducted a formative study with five expert nut carving artisans and identified four key factors shaping ideation: raw materials, carving styles, material combinations, and derivatives. Based on these findings, we constructed a domain-specific annotation framework that translates traditional nut carving knowledge into structured representations for dataset annotation and prompt recommendation, and developed NutMuse, a generative ideation system built on a fine-tuned LoRA model and interactive generation workflows. An exploratory study with six expert artisans suggests that NutMuse can improve ideation efficiency, support creative exploration, and help artisans expand design directions while remaining attentive to material and craft characteristics. Rather than guaranteeing physical feasibility, NutMuse is intended to support early-stage, craft-informed ideation within this highly constrained traditional-craft domain. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: Enhancing Model Generalization in Index Futures Markets via Evolutionary Optimization and Data Leakage-Free Feature Engineering
Abstract: This study investigates the directional prediction of the Mini Bovespa Index Futures (WIN), which are short-term derivative contracts based on Brazil’s main stock index that traders use to speculate or hedge utilizing rapid intraday price movements. A major hurdle in this domain is the tendency of machine learning models to overfit to market noise. To mitigate this, we propose an optimization pipeline that integrates Sequential Forward Selection (SFS) and evolutionary hyperparameter optimization via Genetic Algorithms (GA). The evaluation focused on how the XGBoost and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) architectures respond to evolutionary tuning. It was observed that the need for GA optimization depends on the stability of the model. For example, the XGBoost baseline (default hyperparameters) presented a generalization gap, which the GA-based regularization wrapper managed to reduce to 0.0179, giving it an F1-score of 0.7220. Additionally, the GA demonstrated superior computational efficiency over Random Search, by navigating the hyperparameter space through a directed search that minimizes the evaluation of suboptimal architectures. On the other hand, MLP already demonstrated stability with default settings, although GA brought its gap to near-zero indices and guaranteed it an F1-score of 0.7182, yielding marginal improvements. These results suggest that evolutionary algorithms are important for controlling variance models like XGBoost but serve as a refinement step for robust structures like MLP. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Clinical Deployability: A Socio-technical Construct for Evaluating Real-World Readiness of Medical AI
Abstract: Medical AI evaluation still largely emphasizes model performance under controlled conditions. However, whether an AI-enabled clinical capability can be introduced, used safely and appropriately, and sustained in routine care depends on additional socio-technical conditions. We propose clinical deployability as a second-order, multi-level construct capturing this readiness for real-world clinical work. Deployability integrates three coordinated domains: (A) task usability and safety-in-use; (B) implementation workability (embedding, routinization, sustainment); and, (C) accountability (in-use decision performance and risk governability). We outline operational criteria and a pragmatic measurement strategy based on a deployability dashboard rather than a single scalar score. This paper presents an ongoing research program; future work will apply the framework in real-world implementation case studies to produce comparative deployability assessments and refine the indicator set. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: A Multimodal-Based Framework for Smart ECG Report Generation
Abstract: An electrocardiogram (ECG) is a vital instrument for heart-related disease diagnosis through wearable devices for early treatment. Despite the recent rapid advancement in the development of large language models (LLMs), they are not widely adopted and utilized. In this work, we propose a multimodal framework for ECG signal processing and interpretation based on LLMs and vision-based language models (VLMs). By aligning the ECG time series features, text-based clinical ECG report, and visualized ECG signal through a trainable attention module, our framework provides accurate physiological analysis. Our findings demonstrate that by leveraging pre-trained LLMs and with the addition of the visual domain, which is rarely used in ECG diagnosis, we can enhance medical text interpretation without a heavy retraining computational load. This work contributes toward a more efficient and accurate physiological diagnosis, which enables smart AI healthcare applications and a potential multi-task medical assistant in the future. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Tay D.B.
Title: Nonlinear graph wavelet image compression
Abstract: A still image compression system that is based on a nonlinear graph signal transform is developed in this work. The transform nonlinearity stems from the use of median operators in a lifting structure. The transform generates a multiresolution subband structure and the subband coefficients are encoded using the SPIHT (Set Partitioning in Hierarchical Trees) algorithm. An efficient in-place algorithm is developed for implementing the transform for images, where the use of adjacency matrices is not needed. Extensive performance evaluation is presented and comparisons are made with the classical wavelet compression method. It will be shown that for some types of images, with edges as the primary feature, the nonlinear transform can give a lower bit-rate, for a similar perceptual quality as measured by the SSIM (Structural Similarity Index Measure). © 2026 The Author(s). Title: Redefining Cardiac Arrhythmia Detection and Monitoring in Athletes Using Artificial Intelligence: A Systematic Review
Abstract: Given the limited understanding of the clinical validity and impact of artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled tools in sports cardiology, this research presents a systematic review that synthesizes the evidence on AI-based detection / monitoring of arrhythmias in athletes. Following the PRISMA guidelines, we searched five databases (Embase, Medline, CINAHL, Scopus, SportDiscus) using terms related to AI, athletes, and arrhythmias. English-studies, assessing AI for arrhythmias detection/monitoring in athletes were included. Two researchers independently extracted the data (89% agreement); discrepancies were resolved by consensus. Twelve studies (2015–2025) were identified, collectively reflecting relatively low evidence level (8/12 non-randomized, non-comparative designs). Sample sizes ranged from 6 to 535 with ages 7–60 years. All studies assessed arrhythmias using electrocardiograms. The studies focused primarily on endurance athletes, with limited reporting on training intensity, exercise duration, and comorbidity data. Machine learning (5 studies) and deep learning (4 studies) models were mostly used; 66% did not describe model training/validation. 10 studies (83%) reported improved diagnostic performance (e.g. higher detection accuracy), and 2 studies (17%) indicated workflow benefits (e.g., less time consuming, remote data view), but none reported statistical significance. Evidence on AI-enabled arrhythmias detection in athletes remains early-stage and heterogeneous, limited by non-comparative designs and incomplete reporting of participants and models development/validation. Future studies should employ rigorous designs and assess clinical/statistical significance, patient-centered outcomes, and real-world implementation. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: From Intention to Text: AI-Supported Goal Setting in Academic Writing
Abstract: This study presents WriteFlow, an AI voice-based writing assistant designed to support reflective academic writing through goal-oriented interaction. Academic writing involves iterative reflection and evolving goal regulation, yet prior research and a formative study with 17 participants show that writers often struggle to articulate and manage changing goals. While commonly used AI writing tools emphasize efficiency, they offer limited support for metacognition and writer agency. WriteFlow frames AI interaction as a dialogic space for ongoing goal articulation, monitoring, and negotiation grounded in writers’ intentions. Findings from a Wizard-of-Oz study with 12 expert users show that WriteFlow scaffolds metacognitive regulation and reflection-in-action by supporting iterative goal refinement, maintaining goal–text alignment during drafting, and prompting evaluation of goal fulfillment. We discuss design implications for AI writing systems that prioritize reflective dialogue, flexible goal structures, and multi-perspective feedback to support intentional and agentic writing. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection of Acute Health Events in Older Adults Using Longitudinal Wearable Sensor Data
Abstract: Monitoring the overall health status of independently living older adults is essential for ensuring their well-being and enabling the timely detection of acute incidents. A commonly used approach is remote health monitoring (telecare), which relies on wearable wristbands to continuously collect physiological and activity data. However, the frequent scarcity of event labels in such datasets significantly limits the effectiveness of supervised machine learning to predict health events. To address this challenge, we present an unsupervised Long Short-Term Memory Variational Autoencoder (LSTM-VAE), and we conduct a feasibility study applying it to real-world telecare data from 8,267 older adults monitored over 30 days. Training exclusively on 1.3 million windows of normal physiological patterns, the model achieved AUROC 0.68 (95% CI: 0.65–0.71) for detecting acute events on held-out test data. Comparison with a non-temporal Standard Autoencoder (AUROC 0.67, 95% CI: 0.64–0.71) revealed no statistically significant difference, indicating that the present model family provides a feasible baseline for unsupervised telecare monitoring rather than a production-ready detector. This work demonstrates the feasibility of unsupervised anomaly detection for telecare monitoring and provides a realistic performance baseline for future validation. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Author full names: Jusufbegovic, Merim (57211159423); Hasic, Vahidin (59214178300); Sehic, Kenan (57211117248)
Title: Enhancing Hematology Interpretation with RAG: A Preliminary Study on AI-Guided Clinical Decision Support
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: Manual interpretation of hematology panels is slow and susceptible to inter-observer variability. While Large Language Models (LLMs) can rapidly draft reports, their tendency for clinically hazardous hallucinations poses a major barrier to adoption. This work investigates whether Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) can mitigate these risks. We conducted a preliminary, proof-of-concept study comparing responses generated from 50 hematology cases using a baseline GPT-4 model with those from a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline, which was grounded in 25 authoritative hematology sources. Two certified medical laboratory scientists independently rated each report’s quality on a five-point Likert scale. Although only two certified medical laboratory scientists participated in the evaluation, RAG demonstrated modest yet meaningful improvements: it reduced the proportion of “poor/fair” reports from 26% to 18% and significantly enhanced inter-rater reliability, increasing Cohen’s κ from −0.13 (indicating disagreement) to 0.25 (fair agreement). While one reviewer’s mean score improved (3.30 to 3.56), the other’s was unchanged, underscoring remaining inconsistencies. Our findings suggest that while ungrounded LLMs pose unacceptable clinical risks, domainspecific retrieval offers a measurable, though insufficient, step towards safety and reliability. We conclude that current LLMs act as probabilistic aids rather than autonomous diagnostic tools. While our preliminary results are encouraging, they underscore the need for more comprehensive studies involving a larger number of laboratory scientists, as well as substantial fine-tuning and rigorous validation before any clinical deployment can be considered.
