Title: From fuzzy intent to executable visual workflows: A multi-model orchestration approach
Abstract: Users often express visual tasks using ambiguous natural language, whereas system execution requires explicit and structured processing pipelines, resulting in a significant gap between fuzzy intent and executable workflows. To address this issue, this paper proposes an intent-driven multi-model orchestration framework for medium-compute devices. Rather than introducing new foundation models, the proposed approach adopts a system-level perspective by abstracting visual capabilities such as detection, segmentation, tracking, and change detection into Minimal Functional Units (MFUs). A large language model performs intent parsing and task decomposition, while explicit task graphs enable the organization, scheduling, and execution of heterogeneous models. The proposed method does not require end-to-end training and supports plug-and-play integration, lightweight design, and flexible deployment, enabling effective execution of fuzzy visual tasks. Experiments are conducted under varying conditions of visual-semantic uncertainty. The results indicate that the proposed method achieves competitive performance in task success rate, inference efficiency, and system interpretability, while remaining suitable for lightweight deployment and cross-scenario transferability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: An explainable deep learning framework for intelligent resume screening using semantic embeddings and attention-based candidate ranking
Abstract: Today, artificial intelligence (AI) has become increasingly prevalent to ensure faster and efficient recruitment processes. But most of the AI systems operate as a black box, and it is hard to know how they make decisions. This poses difficulties with regard to equity, confidence, and integrity during job recruitment. This paper presents an Explainable Deep Learning system to intelligent resume screening, as shown in Fig. 1. The system uses sentence-BERT (SBERT) methodology to understand resumes and job descriptions. A deep neural network can be used to candidates the resumes by job, whereas FAISS can be used to find the most relevant candidates within seconds. Attention-based ranking model is also an advancement in matching as it pays attention to significant skills. The key novelty of the proposed framework is the integration of the semantic embedding-based candidate representation, deep learning-based job classification, attention-guided candidate ranking, efficient retrieval using FAISS, and dual explainability mechanisms (SHAP and LIME) in a single end-to-end recruitment pipeline. This is in contrast to the existing systems which are isolated and focused on individual components that have only automated screening capabilities, but cannot provide the necessary transparency in the decision-making process. To explain why a candidate was selected or to explain why a candidate rated him highly, SHAP and LIME are used to bring transparency to the system. Such explainable approaches can assist the HR specialists in knowing how the model makes its decisions and help in building greater trust in automated hiring systems. In addition, the system supports fair and data-driven recruitment by reducing manual effort and improving decision consistency. The framework encourages explainable AI methodologies to facilitate the transparency and informed decision-making, however, a complete fairness assessment with tools like measuring for demographic parity, measuring for equal opportunity, bias auditing, and disparate impact is not part of this current study and is recognized as an important area for future research. The results prove that the system is correct in resumes and categorizing resume besides being transparent. Authors: Wang Y.; Zhang L.; Zhang Y.
Title: Global-regional anti-noise network for cross-subject EEG emotion recognition
Abstract: Emotion recognition based on electroencephalogram (EEG) signals has gained interest owing to its potential in affective computing. In practice, EEG signal acquisition is highly prone to noise interference from electrooculography (EOG) and electromyography (EMG) signals, severely impacting the cross-subject emotion recognition performance of models in real-world scenarios. Although learning-based denoising approaches have been developed to address this issue, they rely on standalone autoencoders for reconstruction, resulting in weak integration with downstream tasks. This study proposes a novel global-regional anti-noise network (GRANet) that is specifically designed for robust cross-subject emotion recognition from noisy EEG data. During modeling, GRANet adopts a novel noising training strategy and similarity-based noise-robust (NR) loss function. According to the noising training strategy, GRANet can extract anti-noise features from noisy EEG data using the NR loss. Moreover, GRANet comprises a three-dimensional global convolutional neural network (3D-GCNN) and a three-dimensional regional convolutional neural network (3D-RCNN). These networks aim to separately extract global and regional anti-noise features from noisy EEG data by applying the noising training strategy. We validate the effectiveness of GRANet by comparing it with state-of-the-art (SOTA) cross-subject methods on four benchmark datasets (SEED, SEED-IV, SEED-V, and DEAP). Findings demonstrate that GRANet has superior performance on these datasets, particularly improving average accuracy by 20.97% on SEED-V from the best baseline. In a nutshell, GRANet can robustly handle real-world EEG noise challenges while maintaining high recognition accuracy, establishing it as a promising solution for practical emotion recognition applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: From Speculation to Evaluation: Exploring Values in Design Fictions About AI-Enhanced Education
Abstract: Design fiction has become an established speculative method for exploring possible futures of Artificial Intelligence in Education, enabling critical reflection on emerging technologies. While it often surfaces ethical, social, and educational values, existing evaluation approaches – such as those focusing on plausibility, coherence, or provocation – primarily assess the quality of the narrative itself, and therefore offer limited support for the systematically analyzing value assumptions and tensions, despite their importance for responsible and equitable AIED research. This paper presents a value-driven evaluation framework for analyzing design fictions depicting AI-enhanced futures of higher education, enabling structured reflection on value assumptions and tensions. Grounded in value-sensitive design and educational research, the framework was developed and iteratively refined through a multi-phase mixed-methods approach. A literature review informed initial value dimensions, which were examined through deductive thematic analysis of human-authored and AI-generated design fiction narratives, and further refined through a participatory student workshop and expert interviews with higher education stakeholders. The resulting framework supports structured reflection on values across individual, institutional, and societal levels, addressing issues such as equity, inclusion, responsibility, and autonomy. For AIED research and practice, it provides a systematic tool to critically examine AI-enhanced educational futures and inform responsible research, policy, and design decisions. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Evaluating the interpretability of clinical speech AI models: Lessons from two user studies
Abstract: The deployment of Artificial intelligence (AI) in clinical speech applications has been limited in large part by the lack of interpretability, which is essential for establishing clinician trust and enabling effective decision support. Although methods such as SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) aim to improve transparency in many clinical domains, their applicability to clinical speech-language pathology practice is uncertain. Since these methods rely on data modalities like acoustic signal features and spectrograms, which are unfamiliar to clinicians and misaligned with clinical workflows, the resulting interpretations may introduce additional burden and bias rather than provide clinically meaningful insight. To better understand this challenge, we conducted two consecutive user studies to systematically evaluate a commonly used SHAP-based interpretation design (a bar chart showing the influence of acoustic features on AI decisions) in dysarthria detection. Building on our prior works, eight factors were examined: faithfulness, computational efficiency, cognitive load, human–AI task performance, mental model, user trust, clinical understandability, and decision relevance. The results reveal a previously unrecognized risk in current interpretation practices. The seemingly intuitive bar-chart design frequently misled participating speech-language pathology (SLP) students to interpret feature influence as an indicator of clinical severity. Other findings include difficulty understanding AI mechanisms, discrepancies between human and model reasoning, and the limited ability of interpretations to address clinical questions. Through this work, we highlight the need for interpretation designs that are more closely aligned with clinical reasoning patterns and suggest practical considerations for developing speech-based AI systems that can be meaningfully integrated into clinical practice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Fostering Scientific Literacy via Vicarious Learning: The Impact of AI-Generated Dialogue Versus Monologue on Psychological Mechanisms
Abstract: This pilot study examines the effects of AI-generated dialogue and monologue audio on learning-related cognitive processes in an audio-only learning environment. Ten participants were randomly assigned to either a single-speaker monologue or dual-speaker dialogue condition and learned about CRISPR-Cas9 through audio. Results showed preliminary trends suggesting that dialogue audio was associated with higher interest/enjoyment and lower mind wandering, but also higher extraneous cognitive load. No significant difference was found in objective learning outcomes. These findings suggest a possible engagement trap in AI-generated audio learning, where greater subjective engagement does not necessarily lead to better learning performance. Title: Evaluating the Multi-dimensional Impacts of the 10% Biodiversity Net Gain Requirement: A Methodological Proposal for Public Administrations
Abstract: Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG) has been introduced in England as a mandatory planning requirement to reverse biodiversity loss and mobilize private investment in nature recovery. From February 2024, most new developments are required to deliver a measurable improvement of at least 10% in biodiversity value. With the start of BNG implementation, positive and negative externalities are emerging and since it is still in its early implementation phase, no widely validated academic framework currently exists that comprehensively evaluates its multi-dimensional impacts. In this context, we propose using the COSIMA (Composite SIgnificance and Multicriteria Assessment) framework as a tool for a holistic ex-ante evaluation of BNG projects. COSIMA integrates traditional cost-benefit analysis (CBA) with multicriteria decision analysis (MCDA) to generate a composite index called the Total Rate of Return (TRR). In this context, this framework ensures that the priorities of developers, government agencies, and local communities are reflected in the final evaluation by including a variety of criteria, both monetizable and non-monetizable. The framework was developed through a structured three-phase methodology combining an exploratory and a systematic scoping review, a stakeholder analysis, and a structured expert validation procedure involving multi-domain specialists to finalize a set of impact indicators spanning environmental, economic, social, and governance dimensions. COSIMA enables transparent, evidence-based comparison of alternative scenarios and provides public administrators and policymakers with a flexible tool to support stakeholder dialogue and optimize the BNG policy. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Yang Y.; Wang Z.; Li L.; Zeng D.
Title: SARE: Soft Alignment Reward for Reinforcement Learning in Generative Recommendation
Abstract: Generative recommendation has recently emerged as a promising paradigm with the adoption of large language models, enabling recommender systems to directly generate items based on users’ historical behaviors. However, unlike classification or retrieval tasks, recommendation is inherently a multi-answer problem, where multiple items can reasonably satisfy a user’s preference. Existing generative recommendation approaches typically rely on strict exact-match alignment, which implicitly assumes a single correct answer and leads to severe reward sparsity in large-scale item spaces. In this paper, we propose SARE (Soft Alignment REward), a simple yet effective reward mechanism that extends exact-match supervision to group-level alignment. Instead of assigning rewards only to the target item, SARE provides partial rewards to items within a predefined group of reasonable alternatives, offering informative learning signals even when exact matches are rare. We further explore three complementary strategies for group construction, capturing temporal continuity, structural relationships, and collaborative similarity among items, respectively. Extensive experiments on real-world recommendation benchmarks demonstrate that SARE consistently outperforms hard exact-match alignment and state-of-the-art generative recommendation baselines. Additional analyses show that SARE generalizes well across different backbone models and maintains stable alignment between optimization signals and recommendation quality. These results highlight the necessity of soft, group-level alignment for generative recommendation tasks with inherently multiple valid solutions. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: An adaptive three-stage recovery framework for sparse identification of nonlinear dynamical systems
Abstract: Sparse identification of nonlinear dynamical systems provides a powerful framework for signal processing when governing equations remain unknown. Feature-selection-based methods must balance parsimony with accurate representation. However, existing methods typically perform selection in a single pass and permanently exclude candidates without reconsideration, which is problematic when measurement noise or weak signal strength causes true governing terms to be incorrectly pruned. To address this issue, we introduce an adaptive three-stage framework with an integrated recovery mechanism. First, an adaptive thresholding stage reduces the candidate feature library while preserving potential governing terms. Second, a forward-backward stepwise selection guided by the Bayesian information criterion provides a theoretically grounded model selection mechanism without requiring specification of regularization parameters. Third, a residual-based post-audit examines residual correlations to identify potentially missed features, and bootstrap resampling removes terms with unreliable coefficient estimates. Extensive experiments on synthetic systems, partial differential equations and real-world applications are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: GCBiMamba-DPS: A Gated ConBiMamba Modeling Approach with Dynamic Permutation Strategy for Session-Based Recommendation
Abstract: Session-based recommendation systems (SBRS) often suffer from recommendation bias due to their neglect of the influence of outer-session causes (OSCs) on user behavior. Existing approaches address the spurious correlation issue caused by OSCs by constructing counterfactual collaboration frameworks. However, they struggle to handle random noise interference in long session scenarios due to limitations in attention networks and pseudo-label generation. To overcome this, we propose GCBiMamba-DPS, a robust modeling approach integrating a gated ConBiMamba architecture with a dynamic permutation strategy for SBRS. First, we introduce a frequency-weighted pseudo-label generation mechanism and a multitask self-supervised learning paradigm for pre-training the base recommendation model (BRM). Second, instead of relying on heavy explicit causal decoupling, we adopt a dynamic permutation strategy as a structural augmentation alongside the GCBiMamba module to effectively isolate sequence noise from authentic preferences. Finally, a lightweight meta-network dynamically adjusts the fusion weights of in-session and outer-session context. Extensive experiments on three real-world datasets demonstrate that GCBiMamba-DPS exhibits strong noise robustness and scenario adaptability. Notably, it achieves a 55.2% improvement in NDCG@20 over COCO-SBRS on the Delicious dataset. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: Lecturers’ Acceptance of Student Generative AI Use in Assessments
Abstract: The rapid proliferation of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools has disrupted traditional assessment practices in higher education, raising critical questions regarding academic integrity and pedagogical adaptation. This study investigates lecturers’ perceptions of students’ use of Generative AI in university assessments using an extended Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) framework incorporating trust and perceived risk. A pilot empirical investigation was conducted with a sample of 110 lecturers. Descriptive and correlation analyses reveal high behavioural intention to accommodate AI use, despite low trust and high perceived risk. Effort expectancy and social influence emerged as key enablers of acceptance, while facilitating conditions were perceived as weak. The findings highlight a transitional phase in higher education characterised by pragmatic adaptation under uncertainty. The study contributes to theory by extending UTAUT to evaluative contexts and offers practical insights for policy development and assessment redesign in AI integrated learning environments. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Dark Side of AI in Higher Education – A Scoping Review
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is progressively transforming teaching and learning experiences in higher education. Some of the advances include simplified practices and smart processes, such as interactive learning content and grading assessments. Students are receiving instant support for complex problems and simplified approaches towards completing assignments or projects. However, there is a “dark side” that comes with the integration of AI, such as compromised academic integrity, among others. This study adopts a scoping review approach to examine the negative impact and challenges associated with the adoption of AI in higher education. Applying inclusion and exclusion criteria, 43 peer-reviewed articles from various databases were reviewed. Literature results demonstrate a rapid increase in studies focusing on AI, with academic integrity and ethical concerns emerging as the most frequently addressed topics. Key findings suggest many students use AI tools for academic work, specifically for assignments and exam questions. The review identifies critical gaps in institutional governance, policy frameworks, and the need for comprehensive AI literacy programs. The results also reveal concerns across four primary domains: ethical issues, algorithmic and implementation biases, negative impacts on student learning, and threats to academic integrity. The study provides recommendations on how the negative impact of AI can be addressed or minimized in education. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Sociodemographic Biases in Educational Counselling by Large Language Models
Abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into educational settings, understanding their potential biases is critical. This study examines sociodemographic biases in LLM-based educational counselling. We evaluate responses from six LLMs answering questions about 900 vignettes describing students in diverse circumstances. Each vignette is systematically tested across 14 sociodemographic identifiers – spanning race and gender, socioeconomic status, and immigrant background – along with a control condition, yielding 243,000 model responses. Title: A pretraining-enhanced hyperspherical prototype framework for open-set recognition
Abstract: Traditional pattern recognition systems, tasked with categorizing input samples into known classes, often struggle when encountering never-seen samples. This introduces the need for open-set recognition (OSR), enhancing models to identify and reject unidentified samples effectively. To implement better OSR in practical applications, we propose a prototype-based OSR framework. It learns a hypersphere for each class and applies a dynamic anchor & anti-anchor quadruplet constraint to enlarge inter-class margins and reserve rejection space for unknowns. Built on a pretrained encoder with a lightweight head and with an optional streaming update rule for test-stage refinement, these mechanisms jointly map samples into stable and well-separated regions of the deep prototype feature space, which directly supports reliable open-set decisions. Authors: Shi Y.; Wang J.
Title: A Machine Learning Study of Country-Level ESG Modeling Using Open Indicators
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) indicators are increasingly used to assess sustainability and institutional quality at the country level. Despite their growing importance, ESG data pose significant challenges for machine learning due to heterogeneity, high dimensionality, temporal dependence, and limited transparency in many existing scoring frameworks. This paper presents a systematic machine learning study of country-level ESG modeling using publicly available World Bank indicators. Rather than proposing a new ESG score, we formulate ESG analysis as four computational tasks: representation learning, level forecasting, directional change classification, and explainability. Using a time-aware evaluation protocol, we compare linear and nonlinear models across these tasks. Our results show that ESG indicators form a largely linear, low-rank space and that simple linear models trained on raw indicators outperform more complex approaches for forecasting ESG levels. While ESG levels are highly predictable, directional changes are substantially harder to anticipate. Explainability analysis further reveals that governance-related indicators dominate predictive performance across tasks. Together, these findings highlight both the opportunities and inherent limits of machine learning for ESG modeling and provide a transparent, reproducible benchmark using open data. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Who’s Behind the Feedback? Students’ Use of AI and Perceived Feedback Usefulness When the Evaluator May Be Human or AI
Abstract: This study examines university students’ use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in academic writing assignments and their perceptions of feedback usefulness when feedback may have been provided by either a human or an AI evaluator. The study was conducted in an introductory academic writing course in which 46 students completed ten assignments during one semester. Before the course, students completed a questionnaire capturing AI-related learner characteristics and self-regulated learning. After each assignment, they reported whether they had used AI tools and how useful they found the feedback. Throughout the semester, students received feedback from either a human or an AI evaluator, but were not informed about the source. To address the longitudinal structure of the data, we estimated mixed-effects models. We examined (1) which factors were associated with assignment-level AI use and (2) whether perceived feedback usefulness varied according to feedback source, assignment-level AI use, and learner characteristics. The results showed that prior AI use in study contexts, AI dependency, and self-regulated learning in AI-mediated interaction predicted assignment-level AI use. Title: Explaining, Solving, or Generating? Functional Differences in Students’ AI Use in a University Database Course
Abstract: The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in computer science education has highlighted the need to better understand how students use AI in learning, rather than treating AI use as single, uniform behavior. This study examines dimensions of students’ AI use and their associations with motivational as well as individual and contextual characteristics. Survey data were collected from 236 students enrolled in an undergraduate database course. Using confirmatory factor analysis, three distinct dimensions of AI use were identified: AI use for explanations, AI use for task solving, and generative AI use. Multiple regression analyses showed that AI use is functionally differentiated. Perceived trust in AI emerged as a cross-cutting predictor across all three usage dimensions, whereas more differentiated patterns were observed for other factors, and several background characteristics, including gender, showed no meaningful associations. Title: Female Entrepreneurs 4.0 in Bosnia and Herzegovina: Is 4IR an Opportunity or a Threat?

Abstract: The Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) is bringing fundamental changes to the global social context, ushering technologies such as automation and artificial intelligence. For female entrepreneurship in Bosnia and Herzegovina, this era represents a specific duality: on one hand, digitalization offers opportunities to overcome traditional gender barriers and facilitates easier access to the global market; on the other hand, it poses a threat by further deepening the digital divide and marginalizing sectors where women-led businesses are traditionally most prominent. The paper explores the position of female entrepreneurs in Bosnia and Herzegovina by analyzing current trends in both, the accessibility and utilization of 4IR resources. The objective is to answer a key question: does technological disruption serve as a catalyst for gender equality or as a new barrier within the transitional economic landscape of Bosnia and Herzegovina for women-led micro and small enterprises? Title: An AI-Assisted Co-planning System for Early English Reading Practice
Abstract: We present a human-in-the-loop system for early English reading practice that supports caregivers and teachers in lesson preparation and personalized review planning. Generated illustrations serve both as motivation and as semantic grounding in an English-only setting. During each session, interaction logs are recorded, capturing timestamps, attempt counts, and correctness. These logs are then used to propose review items targeting words and constructions that challenged the learner. At each stage, AI-generated suggestions can be edited, overridden, or regenerated by the instructor. We report a case study with six Japanese elementary school learners in grades two through four. Using read-aloud interaction logs collected during deployment, we examine whether these logs alone are sufficient to inform review and practice selection. In a time-based forward prediction setting, a logistic regression model using past reading behavior outperforms baselines based on global accuracy, per-learner accuracy, and simple exposure counts. Title: Deep learning methods for EEG-based speech classification and decoding: A PRISMA review
Abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG)-based speech brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) have gained increasing research interest as a potential means to restore or decode speech for individuals with severe communication impairments, particularly with the recent integration of deep learning techniques. This systematic review, conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, provides a comprehensive and quantitative overview of deep learning methods applied to EEG and intracranial EEG (iEEG) speech processing tasks published between 2018 and 2025. A systematic search was conducted across Scopus, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, Web of Science, and PubMed, yielding 1,148 records. Following duplicate removal, screening, and eligibility assessment, 80 peer-reviewed original research articles were included. Studies were organized by task type (speech classification, spectrogram reconstruction, and speech synthesis), neural signal type (non-invasive EEG versus invasive electrocorticography (ECoG) and stereo-electroencephalography (sEEG)), and model architecture to enable structured comparison. Results demonstrate that deep learning models significantly outperform traditional methods in speech classification tasks, while spectrogram reconstruction and speech synthesis remain challenging, particularly for non-invasive EEG. Invasive recordings consistently yield superior performance for reconstruction and synthesis tasks. Despite methodological advances, only a limited number of studies address real-time feasibility or cross-subject generalization, highlighting persistent barriers to clinical translation. Overall, this review provides an integrated, task-oriented synthesis of deep learning–based neural speech decoding and highlights the key methodological and translational barriers that must be addressed to enable robust, real-time, and clinically viable speech neuroprosthetic systems. Authors: Chen X.; Gu J.; Jia F.; Ying S.; Ma L.
Title: URG-MRI: Unpaired reference guided MRI reconstruction
Abstract: Reference-based MRI reconstruction uses fully-sampled images to facilitate the reconstruction of under-sampled data, enhancing imaging efficiency and quality. However, most existing reference-based approaches require strict spatial and modality correspondence between the reference and target images, a condition rarely satisfied in routine clinical practice and one that limits their broader deployment. To overcome this limitation, we propose URG-MRI, a generative-prior framework that distils high-quality anatomical priors from unpaired reference images, removing the need for the reference and target to share subject, contrast, or spatial registration. The method follows a two-stage training strategy: a vector-quantized generative model first learns a discrete codebook of informative features from fully-sampled images; a feature-consistency loss then guides the retrieval of relevant priors during under-sampled reconstruction, while spatial and distribution alignment modules mitigate residual misalignments between retrieved priors and target features. The framework is designed as a plug-in module compatible with diverse reconstruction backbones. On the IXI and fastMRI datasets, integrating it into six representative networks (U-Net, KIKI-Net, DuDoRNet, HUMUS-Net, FPSFormer, and E2E-VarNet) yields PSNR improvements across 4 × /8 ×  Random and Equispaced under-sampling, with representative gains of +1.01 dB for U-Net on IXI (4 ×  Random) and up to +1.63 dB for KIKI-Net on fastMRI (8 ×  Equispaced). Paired t-test and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests further confirm that the improvements are statistically significant (p < .001) in nearly all configurations. Title: Faculty Response to Generative AI: Attitudes, Change in Practice and Policy Towards Students’ Use
Abstract: This study investigates how faculty attitudes toward generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) relate to policy orientations and pedagogical practices in higher education, focusing on the mediating role of pedagogical change in shaping faculty policy orientations. Drawing on a quantitative survey of 160 faculty members, the study examines faculty attitudes toward students’ use of AI tools, self-reported changes in pedagogical practice, and resulting policy orientations of encouragement, prevention, or ignoring. The findings indicate that faculty hold ambivalent attitudes toward GenAI: while recognizing its positive potential, they simultaneously express concerns and hold negative attitudes towards it. Mediation analyses reveal that faculty attitudes are not directly associated with all policy orientations; rather, their effects are mediated by changes in pedagogical practice. Faculty who translate positive attitudes into pedagogical adaptations and change their practices accordingly, are more likely to adopt encouraging policy orientations, whereas limited or absent pedagogical change is associated with preventive or ignoring policies. Authors: Chen Q.; Yu Y.; Cheng N.; Guo R.; Yin R.; Wang X.
Title: From Trajectories to States: State-Constrained Plan Execution for LLM Agents
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong performance on multi-hop web question answering, where planning-based paradigms enable structured reasoning. However, existing architectures predominantly rely on trajectory-centric patterns, where accumulating interaction histories lead to uncontrolled context growth and systematic error propagation. To address this, we propose SCOPE (State-Constrained Plan Execution), a framework that formulates multi-hop reasoning as a process of explicit state transitions. SCOPE decomposes tasks into a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) of executable subtasks, encapsulating intermediate outcomes into discrete state objects called capsules. By employing a repository governed by verification, SCOPE ensures that each state is locally validated before propagation, effectively isolating reasoning steps and halting the spread of hallucinations. Experiments on HotpotQA, MuSiQue, and Bamboogle demonstrate consistent performance gains across varying reasoning depths and LLM backbones. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: M4EI: A Hierarchical Multimodal Memory Framework for Embodied Intelligence with Causal-Driven Retrieval
Abstract: Embodied agents require memory to couple perception, reasoning, and action, yet many memory architectures remain flat, modality-specific, and reliant on shallow similarity search, hindering long-horizon, reasoning-intensive interaction. We introduce M4EI (Memory for Embodied Intelligence), a hierarchical, modular, and multimodal memory framework with short-term, long-term, and skill layers and perceptual, action, and cognitive indexing; modality-specific encoders project into a shared multimodal embedding space for unified retrieval. We build on a Causal Knowledge Graph (CKG) that stores embodied experiences as Episode nodes and extracts executable causal templates (GoalTemplate, CausalTemplate, Step/Condition nodes). Dual-key causal indexing performs two-stage retrieval—semantic matching, then executability filtering with causal gating and execution-aware ranking—to retrieve memories that are semantically aligned yet executable under current embodied states. Authors: Li B.; Hu T.; Liu X.; Zhang B.; Ouyang Q.; Yi P.; Zhang S.; Ma H.
Title: Minimal-Overhead Backdoor Detection via Entropy-Guided Activation Substitution
Abstract: The rapid adoption of Machine Learning as a Service (MLaaS) amplifies security risks from backdoor attacks, yet effective pre-deployment detection remains a critical bottleneck. Existing defenses suffer from debilitating limitations, relying either on computationally expensive trigger inversion or prohibitive prior knowledge of specific attack patterns. In this work, we uncover a novel intrinsic vulnerability in compromised networks: Output Bias Induced by Activation Substitution (BAS). We demonstrate that unlike benign models, backdoor models exhibit a deterministic collapse toward the malicious target label when their activation functions are heterogeneously substituted, even in the absence of triggers. Capitalizing on this fragility, we propose EAPAS (Entropy Analysis of Progressive Activation Substitution), a lightweight detection framework. EAPAS progressively substitutes activation layers and quantifies the rate of predictive collapse via a novel entropy-based metric, NEPDE. This approach eliminates the need for complex optimization, offering a fully agnostic solution. Extensive experiments validate that EAPAS achieves state-of-the-art detection performance and accurate target label identification across diverse benchmarks, while reducing computational costs by orders of magnitude compared to existing baselines. Title: Analysis of public health influencers on social media
Abstract: This study aims to identify health-related themes on X, determine major public health influencers within each thematic category, analyze interrelationships among categories, and examine relationships among key platform variables. Social network analysis, inferential statistics, and visualization methods were used to achieve these aims. Subject analysis identified eight categories: Academia, Corporate, Government, Healthcare, Health Advocacy Program, Individual, Media, and Organization. Government and Health Advocacy Program were the most salient categories in both size and structural influence. Katz centrality was not significantly associated with either Following or Follower counts, whereas Following and Follower counts showed a moderate, statistically significant positive correlation. Katz centrality, Following and Follower counts also differed significantly across the eight categories. Accounts tended to follow Government and Organization accounts, whereas Individual accounts attracted fewer cross-category connections due to their lower structural visibility within the CDC-centered network. The results also indicated category-level homophily, with accounts tending to follow accounts in the same category. These findings have theoretical and practical implications. The identified subject schema provides a framework for guiding health information seeking on X and can help public health officials evaluate the reach and structure of their communication networks. The study also demonstrates a workflow for identifying structurally influential accounts and shows how Following and Follower counts, and Katz centrality reflect different aspects of health-related networks on X. Title: Special Thematic Session: From Assistance to AI: Inclusion and Co-design in Later Life
Abstract: This special session focuses on the evolving role of the AI-enabled technologies, continuing discussions at the intersection of ageing, inclusion, and technologies for assistance. The papers in this session collectively explore how emerging systems can support the full spectrum of later life. A central theme across the contributions is the importance of inclusion through participatory approaches. Title: Extracting Models of Dynamic Human Health Behaviour from Real-Life Personal Health Data
Abstract: The rise of lifestyle-related chronic diseases has increased the need for data-driven methods that capture how health behaviours unfold in daily life. Mobile and wearable technologies now enable continuous, multimodal health data collection, but most behavioural models use static or aggregated representations that overlook temporal dependencies and context. In this work, we adopt a process-oriented perspective, modelling health behaviour as a dynamic process and present a novel methodological contribution: a pipeline that transforms multimodal streams (meals, physical activity, continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), self-reports) into event logs suitable for both traditional and object-centric process discovery. We apply and compare several process discovery algorithms to a longitudinal multimodal dataset from individuals with diabetes, deriving models that capture interactions among activities, physiological measures, and daily routines. Title: How Explanation Framing Shapes Reliance on AI in Clinical Decision Support
Abstract: The integration of AI-based decision-support systems in clinical settings has raised concerns about how professionals interpret and rely on algorithmic recommendations. In particular, explainable AI (XAI) systems are not only technical tools but communicative artifacts that can shape user behavior. Within this context, the persuasive impact of linguistic framing in AI-generated explanations remains underexplored. This study addresses this gap by reporting findings from a controlled experiment in which 52 training nurses completed obstetric decision-making tasks with AI support, examining how neutral, cost-oriented, and gain-oriented explanation framings affect performance, confidence, and reliance behavior among clinical professionals. Results show that while both cost- and gain-oriented framings improved diagnostic accuracy over neutral explanations, cost-oriented framing uniquely increased appropriate reliance, deference, and automation bias. Conversely, self-anchoring bias was lowest under cost-oriented framing. These findings suggest that framing not only affects performance but can increase susceptibility to flawed AI suggestions, calling for design strategies that balance rhetorical effectiveness with professional autonomy in safety-critical environments. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Xu J.; Liu Y.; Wang Y.
Title: Modeling Cross-Paragraph Consistency for Few-Shot AI-Generated Text Detection: A Dual-Path Framework
Abstract: With the continuous advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs), existing AI text detection methods relying on document-level stylistic distribution features have shown diminishing performance gains in recent studies. We propose a dual-path detection framework that integrates a semantic evidence path with a cross-paragraph consistency path. Our key observation is that human writing often exhibits greater stylistic variation across discourse segments, whereas AI-generated text tends to maintain a more uniform stylistic distribution. Motivated by this insight, we model cross-paragraph consistency using structural statistics, perplexity-based measures, and stylistic distribution features. These multi-dimensional features are aggregated into a unified consistency score via a three-level stacked fusion architecture. Notably, we adopt a few-shot calibration mechanism with only 200 labeled samples per class, which is jointly used to stabilize the stacked fusion and optimize the dual-path integration. Experiments across three domains with texts generated by state-of-the-art LLMs (GPT-4, Gemini, and Claude) show that the proposed method outperforms both zero-shot detectors and supervised baselines while remaining robust across different pretrained backbones. Title: CCMA-CLIP: Concept-Guided Cross-Modal Adaptation for Robust AI-Generated Image Detection
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: To address the challenges posed by emerging generative models and image post-processing, we study robust AI-generated image detection under out-of-distribution and post-processing conditions. Recent CLIP-based methods improve cross-generator generalization by leveraging high-level semantic representations learned through vision-language pretraining. Prior work such as C2P further suggests that CLIP mainly distinguishes real and synthetic images by identifying forgery-related semantic concepts rather than relying solely on low-level artifacts. However, their performance still degrades notably under post-processing operations such as compression and resizing, indicating that existing adaptation strategies remain sensitive to fragile cues. To improve robustness, this work proposes CCMA-CLIP, a concept-guided block-level cross-modal adaptation framework. Specifically, concept-enhanced prompts provide stronger semantic supervision, while multimodal adapters inserted into high-level CLIP Transformer blocks encourage the model to focus on stable semantic cues instead of shallow textures. A shared cross-modal bottleneck and asymmetric image-text contrastive objective further stabilize vision-language alignment. Title: Trustworthy AI for Energy-Efficient HPC Under Prediction Errors and Uncertainty
Abstract: As High-Performance Computing (HPC) systems become faster and more complex, their energy consumption continues to increase, raising both economic and environmental concerns. Therefore, it is essential to manage energy usage efficiently, balancing energy consumption with application performance. In this work, we extend our prior research on predictive modeling for energy-efficient resource allocation in HPC systems, which uses the Energy-Delay Product (EDP) as a measure of energy efficiency. Furthermore, instead of focusing solely on predictive accuracy, we aim to provide a deeper understanding of model behavior and its impact on configuration decisions. While previous results demonstrated that an Extra Trees Regressor (ETR) can approximate Oracle configurations with high accuracy, little is known about when and why prediction errors occur. In this work, we present an analysis of prediction errors, an initial uncertainty-aware perspective, and model interpretability in EDP prediction. Our results show that although exact-match accuracy is 81.25%, over 90% of predictions fall within a small regret margin, indicating robust practical performance. Furthermore, uncertainty-aware filtering reduces high-error recommendations, improving reliability for real-world deployment. These findings position the proposed model as not only an accurate but also trustworthy tool for sustainable HPC resource allocation. Title: SemAS - Semantic Alignment Score for XAI Applications in Clinical Decision Support
Abstract: This paper introduces SemAS, a novel tool designed to assess the semantic alignment between clinical encounter data and textual explanations of decision support outputs, with the goal of evaluating their actual clinical usefulness for patient management. A clinician evaluation of sample explanations largely agrees with the SemAS results, but reveals inconsistencies in identifying alignment in more nuanced cases. Title: Representing Uncertainty in Open Learner Models: How Well Do People Interpret It?
Abstract: Open learner models (OLM) and learning analytics dashboards (LAD) are commonly provided visualizations of learner performance, knowledge, and behaviours. Title: DC-FM: A logic-fact dual consistency filtering method for aligned samples in graph-to-text generation
Abstract: In graph-to-text (G2T) generation, high-quality graph–text alignment is crucial, but alignment noise makes reliable aligned data costly and scarce. The proposed DC-FM is constituted by an “inquiry-guided logical verification” module and a “fact consistency verification” module. In experiments, the samples filtered by DC-FM and other existing methods are feed into pretrained language models (PLMs) for fine-tuning, respectively. The observed results show that PLMs demonstrate superior G2T generation performance when using aligned samples filtered by DC-FM, to that by other existing methods. On the ontology-free WikiGraph dataset, our method accurately extracted approximately 110k high-quality samples from the raw data. Experimental results demonstrate that leveraging aligned samples filtered by DC-FM enhances the generation quality of downstream models. Compared to the strongest baseline methods, DC-FM achieves performance gains of up to 30%. Furthermore, when contrasted with baselines fine-tuned on unfiltered data, it realizes an increase of 70%. Abstract: Micro-expression recognition plays a vital role in emotion analysis and human-computer interaction. Title: Customize-A-Video: Learning Personalized Video Generation From Subject Videos

Abstract: With the rapid development of large-scale pre-trained text-to-image generative models, generating images of user-specified subjects has gained increasing attention. Title: NVLPD: Benchmarking Detection, Corner Localization, and Recognition for Two-Line NMV Plates
Abstract: Non-motorized vehicles (NMVs), especially electric bicycles, are widely used for short-distance travel in China. Their popularity creates increasing demand for automatic plate-based identification in campus access control, parking management, and routine supervision. However, NMV license plates are difficult to analyze because they are often small, irregularly mounted, affected by perspective distortion, and frequently arranged in a two-line layout. Existing license plate datasets mainly focus on conventional motor vehicles and provide limited support for geometry-aware evaluation. This paper presents NVLPD, a real-world benchmark for two-line NMV license plate analysis. The dataset contains 2,932 images, each annotated with an axis-aligned bounding box, four ordered corner keypoints, and the corresponding plate text. These annotations support detection, corner localization, perspective rectification, recognition, and end-to-end evaluation. We also provide a reproducible baseline using YOLOv8-pose, homography-based rectification, and LPRNet. Under a matched sample size, the baseline obtains 73.5% image-level recognition accuracy on NVLPD and 77.5% on CCPD. The results show that NVLPD introduces challenges beyond conventional motor-vehicle plate datasets and can serve as a useful benchmark for future NMV plate research. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: Exploring the Internal and External Factors Influencing the Stickiness of Mobile Payment Apps
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: After linking a credit card to a mobile phone, mobile payment apps allow users to make payments at any merchant that supports mobile payments, significantly increasing the convenience of shopping and leading to a rapid increase in their usage. This study explores the factors that contribute to consumer stickiness with mobile payment apps from both internal and external perspectives, and identifies which variables within these factors have a greater impact. Data was collected via online questionnaires, and after a month of collection and removal of invalid questionnaires, 337 valid questionnaires were obtained. Smart PLS 4.0 software was used to conduct structural equation modeling analysis and test the research hypotheses. The results show that only hedonistic value has no significant positive impact on satisfaction among the nine hypotheses, while the other eight hypotheses are valid. Title: Decoding Latent Reasoning: Mechanistic Interpretability of Chain of Continuous Thought with Sparse Autoencoders
Abstract: Large language models are going silent. As mathematical reasoning evolves from explicit Chain-of-Thought to efficient “latent reasoning,” models using methods like Chain of Continuous Thought (CoConut) no longer show their work, they “think” through continuous, inscrutable hidden states. For education, this creates a critical transparency crisis: how can we trust an AI tutor that solves problems without revealing its reasoning process? When should it intervene if we cannot detect its uncertainty or errors? We break open this black box by applying Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to interpret CoConut’s internal reasoning states during step-by-step problem solving on GSM8k. Through systematic analysis of 7,914 reasoning steps and manual annotation of problems across 9 mathematical skills, we discover something remarkable: buried within these inscrutable activations are interpretable features that reliably detect specific reasoning patterns (F1=0.542, 135% better than random). When we surgically ablate these features, performance collapses. Removing the top feature causes a 44.6% drop, with some skills degrading by 67%, proving these aren’t spurious correlations but causally important mechanisms. Most strikingly, we reveal that features detecting uncertainty and logical contradictions are nearly perfectly correlated (r=0.988, p<0.0001): the model maintains a unified internal “reasoning quality monitor.” These findings reveal that latent reasoning, despite its opacity, contains structured representations that enable skill detection and error monitoring, providing a foundation for more transparent mathematical reasoning systems. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Raw–Topic–TempLex: An Interpretable Multi-branch Framework for Apparent Personality Prediction
Abstract: Apparent personality prediction (APP) aims to estimate first impressions of the Big Five traits from short videos. Existing APP methods often rely on opaque multimodal representations, making it difficult to understand how predictive evidence is organized and used. A standardized Ridge regression layer enables branch-wise attribution and concept-level interpretation. Experiments on the ChaLearn First Impressions V2 dataset show that the proposed framework achieves competitive performance (R2 = 0.4677, PCC = 0.6811, CCC = 0.6378) while maintaining intrinsic interpretability. Results further indicate that TempLex provides the strongest discriminative signal, Raw contributes complementary direct behavioral evidence, and Topic mainly functions as a compact structural summary branch. Title: Color Prior and Direction-Guided Convolution for Soccer Foul Recognition
Abstract: Automated soccer foul recognition in broadcast videos struggles with strong background interference, heavy limb occlusion, and motion blur. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a pure pixel-level recognition method combining color prior attention and Direction Vector-Guided Convolution (DVC). First, a training-free color prior gating mechanism suppresses background noise to retain high-quality foreground features. Next, the DVC module explicitly extracts fine-grained directional features under heavy occlusion by dynamically modulating convolution weights based on local texture directions. Finally, a spatiotemporal hybrid pooling strategy is applied for foul severity classification. Evaluations on the SoccerNet-MVFouls dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms mainstream baselines in both overall accuracy and severe foul recall, showing strong potential for real-world application. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: Ontology-Aligned Clinical NER in Emergency Medicine Using Weak Supervision
Abstract: This study presents a weakly supervised framework for clinical named entity recognition (NER) in emergency medicine, leveraging ontology-aligned representations to enhance downstream modeling. Title: Deciphering leader decision-making patterns from open-source information: A temporal knowledge graph-based approach
Abstract: In an era characterized by complex geopolitical and economic volatility, analyzing leader decision patterns is crucial for strategic foresight and organizational risk assessment. While leaders’ decision-making footprints are increasingly captured in massive open-source information, deciphering these patterns presents significant challenges. Traditional decision-making analysis heavily relies on subjective expert judgment and struggles with large-scale unstructured data, whereas modern data-driven deep learning models often operate as uninterpretable black boxes lacking theoretical grounding. Furthermore, the inherent sparsity and temporal dispersion of open-source data complicate effective modeling. To address these limitations, this study proposes a theory-grounded computational framework that integrates a Temporal Knowledge Graph with a Decision Pattern Neural Network. The Temporal Knowledge Graph structures fragmented open-source information into temporally ordered semantic quadruples, enabling the dynamic representation of decision-related entities, relations, and contextual factors. The Decision Pattern Neural Network further models decision-making as a hierarchical process in which external environmental factors are filtered through leader-specific individual factors before producing action tendencies. In a case study of Saudi Aramco, we construct a Temporal Knowledge Graph containing 153,267 quadruples from more than 440,000 open-source records and evaluate the framework on 352 annotated decision events of CEO Amin Nasser. The proposed model achieves an overall prediction accuracy of 83.02%, with a precision of 86.49% and a recall of 88.89%. This study provides a theoretically sound and computationally scalable solution for deciphering leadership logic, effectively bridging the gap between qualitative decision theory and quantitative data analytics. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: AdaTable: Learning to Calibrate for Robust VNF Auto-scaling under Capacity Drift
Abstract: Dynamic auto-scaling of Virtual Network Functions (VNFs) requires balancing resource efficiency with Service Level Agreement (SLA) compliance under changing operating conditions. This task is made harder when the relationship between observed traffic and effective service capacity is not stable over time, a phenomenon we refer to as hidden capacity drift. Existing methods face a trade-off between responsiveness, adaptability, and deployment simplicity, and few address drift explicitly. To address this challenge, we propose AdaTable, which separates real-time execution from long-timescale adaptation through a dual-plane hierarchical design. A deterministic fast plane executes scaling decisions through a parameterized capacity table with anti-jitter mechanisms, while a DRL-based slow plane calibrates the table parameters from aggregated system behavior. Training further incorporates adaptive penalty adjustment to balance resource cost and SLA compliance. We evaluate the method under two complementary protocols, namely a fixed-target cross-scenario comparison and a target-swept Pareto analysis on trace data. Results show that AdaTable improves over reactive and prediction-based baselines and remains competitive with end-to-end DRL, while achieving stronger cost-SLA trade-offs in drift-sensitive regions. On the trace-based Pareto evaluation, at the operating point nearest the 5% SLA target, AdaTable reduces average active instances by about 31% relative to HPA while lowering the SLA violation rate from 7.77% to 3.94%. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: Fostering “Smart People” for the Digital Metropolis: Pedagogical Models of AI-Enhanced Cultural Heritage Preservation at Saint Petersburg State University and Russian Museum
Abstract: This paper explores the synergetic potential of university-museum collaborations within the framework of a Human-Centric Smart City. Results: the implementation yielded the creation of a “Digital Twin of Cultural Memory” for the museum’s media library, including AI-driven animated narratives and inclusive digital resources. Quantitative assessments confirmed that 92% of participants achieved advanced proficiency in Prompt Engineering and AI-content curation. Title: Computing the Distribution of the Traces of a Business Process by Their Lengths
Abstract: Business process models may generate large sets of execution traces whose size and structure depend on control-flow constructs such as choice, parallelism, and iteration. Title: An Optimization Method to Ensure Reliability in the Assessment of Special Properties
Abstract: The valuation of special properties is often characterised by a high degree of complexity due to limited market comparability, functional specificity, and the subjectivity involved in the estimation of key appraisal parameters. This issue is particularly relevant in the case of socio-healthcare facilities, whose market value is commonly assessed through the Discounted Cash Flow Analysis (DCFA). Applied to the case of Italian private nursing homes, the proposed framework is intended to support a more structured and reliable estimation process, while also considering the different perspectives of the parties involved in the transaction. Title: SLAI: AI Support for Multilingual Small Group Discussions in Science Classrooms
Abstract: The purpose of the proposed tool, bridging Science and Language with AI (SLAI) Tool, is to empower teachers to engage with ideas expressed by all students, including multilingual learners, that might otherwise go unnoticed in small group discussions. We designed the pilot SLAI tool to be synergistic with current classroom practices, positive beliefs about multilingualism, and contemporary standards in science and language learning. Our reflexive thematic analysis of teacher interview data (N = 20) reveals three key trends in teacher perceptions. First, the pilot SLAI Tool allows students to engage deeply with content in their home languages while allowing teachers to access the same. Second, teachers underlined potential improvements to the SLAI Tool like novel analytics, real-time transcription, speaker recognition, and a student-facing version of the SLAI tool. Third, there are factors beyond technical adaptation that impact how teachers use the tool such as stigmatization of home language in classroom, ensuring the ethical use of the SLAI Tool by teachers (e.g., formative assessment and engaging with student ideas versus surveillance), and balancing students’ overreliance on translation and English language learning. Title: Diffusion sequential recommendation model based on item co-occurrence anchoring and user semantic collaboration
Abstract: Diffusion models have emerged as a prominent paradigm in the field of Sequential Recommendation (SR) due to their superior generative capabilities that effectively model the diversity and uncertainty of user preferences. However, existing diffusion-based sequential recommendation models face two critical challenges. The first challenge is the issue of data distribution inconsistency in item co-occurrence representations. Specifically, graph-enhanced item embeddings evolve dynamically during the end-to-end training process. This dynamic evolution conflicts with the stationary conditional probability distribution required by the diffusion reverse process, thereby disrupting the convergence stability of the model. The second challenge is that it is difficult to construct precise denoising conditions solely from sparse and noisy raw interaction sequences. To address these challenges, a Diffusion Sequential Recommendation model based on Item Co-occurrence Anchoring and User Semantic Collaboration (ICUSRec) is proposed in this paper. An Item Co-occurrence Anchor is proposed to address distribution inconsistency to provide stable semantic anchors for the denoising process, which effectively mitigates data distribution inconsistency while improving training efficiency. Meanwhile, a dual-side collaborative guidance mechanism is designed, integrating a user semantic codebook and item co-occurrence information to construct precise and complementary diffusion denoising conditions spanning both intra-sequence and inter-sequence contexts. Extensive experiments are conducted on four public datasets including ML-1M, Toys, Beauty, and Steam to compare ICUSRec with multiple baseline models. The experimental results demonstrate that ICUSRec consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods and achieves a 12.75% improvement in HR@20, which validates the effectiveness of the proposed method. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Real-Time Identification and Evaluation of DoS Attacks for Embedded Systems

Title: Planning as graphs: Adaptive agentic planning for LLM agents
Abstract: Planning is fundamental to LLM agents that solve complex, multi-step tasks, yet how to represent plans in a structured form that supports controllable execution remains an open challenge. Existing approaches often express plans as unstructured natural language or linear Chain-of-Thought (CoT), making it difficult to explicitly capture dependency structures among subtasks. CoT and Unstructured plans correspond to two operating points within this representation: an over-constrained linear chain and a zero-edge degeneratation. Both are consumed by the same execution engine, enabling a controlled comparison of plan layers on a shared executor stack. Within this representation we introduce evidence-conditioned adaptive parsimony: after exploration, the planner emits the sparsest executable graph, remaining linear on simple instances and expanding into richer graph structures on complex tasks. The executor interprets the static graph through outcome-conditioned routing and bounded branch switching. On SWE-bench Lite, a long-horizon interactive benchmark for repository-level repair, GraphPlan improves over CoT and Unstructured planning variants, with the largest gains on hard instances where explicit failure routing matters most. Title: Scaling Down Hallucinations: Mitigation Strategies for Compact LLMs
Abstract: The deployment of generative artificial intelligence on consumer hardware is substantially constrained by the tendency of smaller architectures to hallucinate unfaithful or factually incorrect content. This study investigates and categorizes contemporary mitigation strategies through a systematic literature review, classifying them into four distinct groups comprising Model Optimization, Inference and Output Enhancement, External Knowledge and Interaction, and Latent Space Intervention. After applying reproducibility and computational feasibility criteria, eight representative techniques (including Shadow-FT, DoLa, REPLUG, and ITI) were selected for experimental analysis on two representative small language models, Llama-3.2-3B and Qwen3-4B. Evaluations using deterministic reasoning, generative factuality, and summarization benchmarks revealed variable performance across the two models. Specifically, REPLUG was the strongest stabilizer for the tested Qwen3-4B configuration, with no drift events observed in this evaluation. Meanwhile, ITI and Hermes 3 achieved the best results in generative truthfulness for the standard baseline with gains exceeding 30% points, and DoLa demonstrated consistent improvements in source faithfulness. Furthermore, empirical results indicate that mitigation effectiveness is heavily contingent on the interaction between the method and the underlying model. For instance, retrieval acted as a stabilizer for the dual-mode architecture but introduced distractor sensitivity in the standard instruct counterpart. Title: METER-DETR: A Water Meter Reading Recognition Algorithm Based on RT-DETR Under Complex Imaging Conditions
Abstract: Accurate water meter reading recognition supports reliable billing and water-resource management. Title: Dual-boosted capsule networks: Attention-enhanced routing and feedback learning for leaf disease classification on heterogeneous datasets
Abstract: Identifying the complex leaf disease is a major challenge in crop production. Traditional Capsule Networks face challenges in capturing the complex features associated with various plant diseases, even though they can effectively retain spatial hierarchies. To overcome challenges, this research presents a novel Capsule Networks framework for the identification of leaf disease and its classification. The research proposes a Feedback-Enabled Capsule Routing and a Capsule-Level Attention mechanism. The Feedback-Enabled Capsule Routing method that refines classification outcomes also introduces top-down contextual signals, whereas the Capsule-Level Attention mechanism dynamically weighs capsule outputs based on their relevance. Incorporating this, we also integrated Primary Capsule Squashing and Dynamic Routing. All methods are grounded in formal mathematical definitions. The XAI techniques are integrated to visualize the model’s decision-making process for transparency. Empirical evaluations demonstrate the model’s effectiveness in achieving classification accuracies of 98.97% and 98.49% in the PlantVillage and the PLD datasets, respectively. This framework addresses the trust gap in AI-driven agricultural diagnostics, allowing for a transparent and reliable method of disease detection in agricultural applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Sustainable Watershed Management and Morphometric Characteristics: The Bijelo Polje Basin, Montenegro
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: River basin management is a key segment of modern natural resource management, based on an integrated approach to land, water and spatial protection. This research analyzed the basins of the lower part of the Bijelo Polje basin: Kisjele vode, Sutivanska rijeka, Orahovčka rijeka, Bistrica and Miočki potoks in northeastern Montenegro. The aim of the research was to determine the basic geometric and topographic characteristics of the basins, using morphometric analysis, GIS tools and computer graphics models, and to assess their hydrological potential as a basis for sustainable management of river systems. The results indicate that the observed basins have pronounced mountainous characteristics, moderate to high compactness (A = 0.55–0.95), and a moderately developed drainage network (G = 0.22–0.55). Average slopes (Isr = 20.9–32.5%) and elevation differences (D = 300–565 m) confirm the presence of active, but stable mountain systems. A comparative analysis with river basins in Morocco, Iran, Nepal, Brazil and Serbia showed that the Bijelo Polje basin belongs to the group of morphologically stable, but hydrologically active mountain areas. The obtained results confirm the applicability of the IntErO, River Basins models and GIS methods in quantitative assessment of land protection measures planning, and represent a significant contribution to the development of integrated and sustainable river basin management in Montenegro and similar mountainous regions of Southeast Europe. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Operationalizing Uncertainty via Structural Coupling for Reliable 3D Dental Point Cloud Segmentation
Abstract: Automated 3D dental model analysis is foundational to computer-aided dentistry. Existing segmentation pipelines treat uncertainty as a post-hoc diagnostic, preventing its use for structural decisions at ambiguous boundaries. We propose MSBA-Net, which aligns normalized predictive entropy with boundary probability through a structural coupling objective, making ambiguity actionable during training. A boundary-aware contrastive scheme with kNN-based hard-negative mining further enhances feature discriminability. On Teeth3DS, MSBA-Net achieves 95.33% mIoU and 84.89% B-IoU. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: Identity suppression awareness for facial expression recognition via dual-path learning
Abstract: Facial Expression Recognition (FER) is a significant research area with broad applications. However, it faces substantial challenges in accurate and reliable generalization. Multi-Task Learning (MTL) has shown high performance in FER. However, FER still faces some difficulties, such as identity-specific features overlap, dataset imbalance, and so on. To address these issues, we propose an Identity Suppression Awareness for Facial Expression Recognition via Dual-Path Learning (ISA-DPL). The proposed method features a dual-pathway MTL architecture with separate paths for feature extraction and expression recognition. In addition, by averaging features across the batch dimension and compensating for minority classes during feature extraction, our approach further suppresses identity-related features. The dual-pathway features are cross-fused in a pyramid structure to highlight expression-related features across different scales, which can learn feature importance and suppress identity-related features, thus preventing dominant identity features from overshadowing them. Our model achieves state-of-the-art results on the RAF-DB (Real-world Affective Faces Database), SFEW2.0 (Static Facial Expression in the Wild 2.0), and AffectNet datasets, effectively mitigating the impact of identity information on FER. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Ordered fusion from head to tail in imbalanced node classification
Abstract: Imbalanced distributions are prevalent in real-world graphs, particularly in the form of class imbalance and degree imbalance. These distributions are not entirely aligned: nodes from head classes may reside in the tail region of the degree distribution, posing additional challenges for Graph Representation Learning (GRL) models. Existing approaches often overlook imbalanced conditions, assuming balanced input graph distributions, which leads to performance dominance by head nodes while tail nodes underperform. Some studies acknowledge imbalanced distributions but focus solely on isolated performance improvements, failing to achieve a balanced trade-off between overall and tail performance. To address the above issues, we propose a plug-and-play tail augmentation module. We design a triple information flow architecture that comprehensively covers both global and local structures. We simultaneously integrate two sequences ordered by class and degree as global structures, enhancing the models’ perception of both types of imbalanced distributions. We leverage graph serialization techniques to establish ordered information flows from head to tail, mitigating feature scarcity in tail nodes. We evaluate our module on node classification tasks across four real-world datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that our module effectively adapts to tail nodes while delivering comprehensive performance gains. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Clustering-Based Automated Generation and Multiscale Analysis of Metamaterial Representative Volume Elements
Abstract: Drawing on representative volume elements (RVEs), artificial intelligence (AI) approaches and computational methods, an automated methodology was integrated to generate and assess mechanical metamaterials. The method is aimed at directly converting image-based inputs into 3D geometries independently of manual CAD simulations to substantially accelerate preprocessing. This study performed material region identification and complex geometry reconstruction through learning-based image segmentation and incorporated filtering into the method to establish a feasible structure and discard configurations with mechanical inconsistency and/or instability. Emphasizing the dependence of key mechanical properties on geometric variables, lattice-based structures were evaluated to validate the proposed method. The equivalent modulus of elasticity was found to be smaller relative to the base material by up to two orders of magnitude, with the numerical results being in good agreement with experimental data. The computational cost was also found to be remarkably (≈95%) lower than conventional modeling. This effective and efficient methodology with superb scalability can be employed in a range of applications, including additive manufacturing (AM), multiscale modeling, and structural engineering, where metamaterials are designed and analyzed in an automated manner. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Design of a Mobile Stress Assessment and Management System for Neurodivergent Individuals
Abstract: Neurodivergent individuals, particularly those on the autism spectrum, often experience increased stress in everyday situations and may benefit from accessible digital support tools. This work presents the human-centered development and evaluation of a mobile application for stress self-assessment and management, involving neurodivergent users and caregivers. Interactive mock-ups were evaluated with 16 participants using the System Usability Scale (SUS), achieving a mean score of 81, indicating high perceived usability. A functional prototype was subsequently tested in a think-aloud usability study with four participants. Qualitative content analysis revealed key strengths in intuitive interaction, alongside challenges in navigation, interaction feedback, data visualization, and terminology. Participants also emphasized the need for enhanced personalization, accessibility features, and clearer visual communication. The results suggest that mobile applications can provide effective and accessible support for stress management in neurodivergent populations, while highlighting important design considerations for future development and real-world deployment. © The Author(s) 2027.

Title: Large language model counterarguments in older adults: Cognitive offloading or susceptibility to moral persuasion?
Abstract: This study examined whether counterarguments generated by large language models (LLMs) influence the moral judgments of younger and older adults, and whether these effects vary by dilemma type, cognitive functioning, trust in AI, and prior LLM experience. Using the switch and footbridge trolley dilemmas, 130 participants (56 younger adults and 74 older adults) were presented with ChatGPT-generated counterarguments that opposed their initial judgments. More than 30% of participants reversed their judgments in both dilemmas (32.31% in the switch dilemma and 36.92% in the footbridge dilemma). Older adults tended to be more likely than younger adults to reverse their judgments and showed a significantly greater degree of judgment change in the switch dilemma. In the emotionally aversive footbridge dilemma, older adults with lower cognitive functioning were significantly more likely to align with the LLM-generated counterargument. General trust in AI and prior LLM experience did not predict judgment reversal, whereas lower initial confidence and higher perceived task difficulty were associated with greater susceptibility to LLM influence. These findings suggest that LLMs may support cognitive offloading but increase susceptibility among individuals with limited cognitive resources. The ecological generalizability of these findings to everyday dilemma situations remains to be examined in future research. © 2026 The Authors
