Title: Prototype-guided dual-gate multimodal fusion for robust crop disease recognition
Abstract: Real-world agricultural field conditions introduce substantial challenges for crop disease recognition models, particularly in maintaining stable performance under varying illumination and complex backgrounds. Previous studies have shown that incorporating textual descriptions into multimodal disease recognition frameworks can improve diagnostic performance. However, semantic inconsistency in textual annotations, variability in modality quality, and the lack of effective mechanisms for dynamically regulating modal contributions continue to limit the robustness of existing multimodal fusion approaches. To address these challenges, this study proposes a dual-gate multimodal disease recognition framework guided by class text-based prototypes. The proposed architecture enhances cross-modal consistency and robustness by introducing structured semantic priors and a reliability-aware modality regulation strategy. Specifically, class-level textual prototypes are constructed from expert-defined descriptions, and similarity-based modeling is employed to semantically refine both visual and textual representations. A dual-gating mechanism then adaptively adjusts the degree of prototype-guided enhancement in the visual and textual branches according to their relative reliability, thereby mitigating the adverse impact of low-quality modalities on recognition performance. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves an F1-score of 72.08% in complex agricultural field scenarios, outperforming multiple existing multimodal methods and exhibiting improved robustness in practical disease recognition tasks. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Bringing Plain Language Principles Into Interaction Design Practices: Insights from a Wizard of Oz Approach

Abstract: Language, whether textual, verbal, or visual, can become a barrier to access and understanding in human-computer interaction when not effectively designed or tailored to users’ needs. One way to address these communication barriers is to adopt Plain Language guidelines to help users find, comprehend, and use vital information. This study investigated the challenges development teams face when applying PL principles to the design of interactive systems. Using the Wizard of Oz technique, we simulated a chatbot supporting novice developers in implementing PL in health-related applications. The results highlight challenges in addressing diverse literacy levels and extending PL beyond text to visual and interaction design aspects. Title: Scaffolding Critical Engagement with GenAI: Transforming Ethnic Minority Preparatory Students’ Collaborative Discourse in Prompt Engineering Tasks
Abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) holds significant promise for advancing educational equity among ethnic minority students by broadening access to learning resources and mitigating linguistic barriers. However, these benefits are counterbalanced by the risk of cognitive laziness, whereby students may treat GenAI as an answer engine or shortcut rather than as a partner in thinking. This design-based research investigated how pedagogical scaffolding can shift students from passive consumption to critical co-creation with GenAI. The study involved 78 ethnic minority preparatory students in China participating in a three-week GenAI course that integrated a human-in-the-loop workflow and teacher modeling with contrasting cases to disrupt uncritical reliance on GenAI. We employed epistemic network analysis to examine collaborative discourse, thematic analysis to analyze student reflections, and paired-samples t-tests to assess changes in prompt self-efficacy. Results revealed a phenomenon of strategic repurposing: initially, students instrumentalized strategy talk to coordinate efficient copying; however, after the intervention, they realigned strategic planning to scaffold critical evaluation and peer co-construction. Qualitative findings further indicated that the teacher’s scaffolding helped students overcome their initial authority bias and prompt paralysis, repositioning themselves as active gatekeepers of AI-generated content; these shifts were corroborated by a significant increase in students’ prompt self-efficacy. The study suggests that, particularly for ethnic minority students, technical training alone is insufficient; educators should design targeted pedagogical interventions around human–AI collaboration to prevent cognitive complacency and cultivate epistemic agency. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Zhang L.; Zou J.
Title: Hierarchical query denoising and text-guided dimension-wise gated fusion for multimodal sentiment analysis
Abstract: Multimodal sentiment analysis aims to improve sentiment prediction by integrating affective cues from heterogeneous modalities such as text, acoustics, and vision. However, most existing methods directly interact or fuse the raw modality representations, lacking sufficient denoising capability and failing to fully exploit multi-level semantic affective information. Consequently, noise and redundancy are prone to be introduced, which restricts the modeling of fine-grained affective cues. Moreover, existing methods generally lack fine-grained selective modeling in cross-modal interaction and fusion, making it difficult to adaptively regulate modality contributions across feature dimensions. To address these issues, we propose a Hierarchical Query Denoising and Text-Guided Dimension-Wise Gated Fusion framework for multimodal sentiment analysis, termed HQDF. Specifically, a hierarchical query denoising module is first constructed, where learnable query tokens progressively interact with multi-level semantic representations to extract sentiment-relevant information while suppressing noise and redundancy. Next, a text-anchored interaction module uses the textual representation as a semantic anchor to retrieve acoustic and visual cues, which are then incorporated to refine the textual representation for subsequent fusion. Finally, an interaction-aware dimension-wise gated fusion module is developed to adaptively weight cross-modally enhanced representations at the feature-dimension level, enabling fine-grained cross-modal selection and fusion. Experimental results on CMU-MOSI and CMU-MOSEI demonstrate the competitiveness of the proposed method. Ablation studies and visualization analyses further verify the effectiveness of the proposed modules. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Understanding Teacher Revisions of Large Language Model-Generated Feedback
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly generate formative feedback for students, yet little is known about how teachers revise this feedback before it reaches learners. Teachers’ revisions shape what students receive, making revision practices central to evaluating AI classroom tools. We analyze a dataset of 1,349 instances of AI-generated feedback and corresponding teacher-edited explanations from 117 teachers. We examine (i) textual characteristics associated with teacher revisions, (ii) whether revision decisions can be predicted from the AI feedback text, and (iii) how revisions change the pedagogical type of feedback delivered. First, we find that teachers accept AI feedback without modification in about 80% of cases, while edited feedback tends to be significantly longer and subsequently shortened by teachers. Editing behavior varies substantially across teachers: about 50% never edit AI feedback, and only about 10% edit more than two-thirds of feedback instances. Second, machine learning models trained only on the AI feedback text as input features, using sentence embeddings, achieve fair performance in identifying which feedback will be revised (AUC=0.75). Third, qualitative coding shows that when revisions occur, teachers often simplify AI-generated feedback, shifting it away from high-information explanations toward more concise, corrective forms. Together, these findings characterize how teachers engage with AI-generated feedback in practice and highlight opportunities to design feedback systems that better align with teacher priorities while reducing unnecessary editing effort. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Cognitive Processes Underlying Divergent Levels of Performance and Agency in AI-Assisted Programming
Abstract: Generative AI (GAI) tools such as ChatGPT are increasingly used in programming education, offering potential benefits for learning while also raising concerns about students’ agency. Prior research calls for achieving performance gains with GAI while maintaining agency, yet the cognitive processes yielding divergent levels of performance and agency remain unclear. We therefore examine how cognitive processes unfold among learners with different levels of programming performance and agency in AI-assisted programming. In this controlled laboratory study, 150 undergraduates completed individual programming tasks with ChatGPT. Programming processes and interactions with GAI were captured through screen recordings and eye-tracking. We developed a codebook that includes 14 types of cognitive processes, each associated with a high or low agency label (Krippendorff’s α = 0.78). Based on programming performance and agency, participants were classified into four groups: high performance–high agency (PH–AH), high performance–low agency (PH–AL), low performance–high agency (PL–AH), and low performance–low agency (PL–AL). Sequential pattern mining and χ2 tests revealed distinct cognitive sequences across groups: PH–AH students asked original questions and selectively adapted AI outputs; PL–AH students relied on AI for debugging, suggesting weaknesses in handling errors and refining code. In contrast, PH–AL students achieved high performance largely through copying GAI-generated code, and PL–AL learners exhibited fragmented engagement between writing code independently and copying GAI-generated code. Title: Combating Modality Imbalance via Gradient Variance-Guided Tuning
Abstract: Modality imbalance in multimodal learning (MML) often causes one modality to dominate optimization, thereby suppressing the contribution of other modalities and limiting the effectiveness of joint training. Existing methods typically rebalance multimodal training through architecture redesign, loss reweighting, or optimizer-level adjustments, but they often overlook the temporal disparity in gradient dynamics across modalities. In this work, we identify that modality imbalance is closely associated with a persistent gap in gradient variance, especially during the early stage of training when the model rapidly acquires information from data. To address this issue, we propose a simple yet effective framework that combines Gap Monitor in Gradient Variance (GMGV) with Gradient Norm Tuning (GNT). Specifically, GMGV continuously monitors the temporal gap in gradient variance between modalities and detects statistically significant imbalance through sequential hypothesis testing. Once imbalance is detected, GNT performs step-wise gradient correction by reducing the update magnitude of the dominant modality and enhancing that of the suppressed modality through norm-based gradient scaling. Extensive experiments across multiple multimodal fusion methods, backbone architectures, and optimizers demonstrate that the proposed method consistently improves performance, enhances representation quality, and provides a robust and generalizable solution to modality imbalance in MML. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: Entropy-Based Graph Embedding for Credit Risk Evaluation Incorporating Sample Correlations
Abstract: Substantial empirical evidences indicate that the defaulting users often share certain commonalities, such as similar economic conditions, education background and living environments. Yet, these shared characteristics have been frequently overlooked in traditional statistical or machine learning based credit risk assessment models, which tend to focus on the unique attributes of each individual borrower. By incorporating sample correlations into the evaluation framework, we may capture more significant latent dependencies among credit users and improve model predictive accuracy. To this end, in this paper we develop a new entropy-based graph embedding method to model and quantify sample correlations and further apply this approach to the credit classification tasks. To validate the performance of the proposed method, we perform a series of experiments and compare with current evaluation models on three public credit datasets. Title: Adversarial semantic correction distillation with boundary-guided feature alignment for object detection
Abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective approach for compressing object detection models, yet it remains challenging because dense predictions and joint classification–regression learning make distillation signals vulnerable to background noise. Teacher–student capacity gaps also induce prediction distribution shifts that are difficult to characterize with conventional point-wise distance metrics. In addition, most existing methods follow a one-way teacher-to-student supervision paradigm and lack explicit supervision for the high-level semantic structure of the student detection head. To address these issues, we propose Adversarial Semantic Correction Distillation (ASCD), a unified framework that jointly optimizes spatial constraint, distributional alignment, and semantic structure correction. Specifically, Boundary-Guided Local Distillation (BGLD) utilizes ground-truth boundaries to construct foreground masks and aligns features within object-relevant regions. Adversarial Distribution Alignment (ADA) introduces a lightweight discriminator to implicitly reduce prediction distribution discrepancies via adversarial learning. Teacher Semantic Correction (TSC) feeds teacher features into the student detection head and applies multi-scale contrastive learning to improve the semantic consistency of the student head. Extensive experiments on COCO and PASCAL VOC demonstrate that ASCD consistently improves detection performance across various detectors, heterogeneous backbones, and cross-detector distillation settings. Moreover, ASCD introduces no additional inference overhead, showing strong effectiveness and generalization for object detection distillation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Human–AI Collaboration Reconfigures Group Regulation from Socially Shared to Hybrid Co-regulation
Abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) is increasingly used in collaborative learning, yet its effects on how groups regulate collaboration remain unclear. Effective collaboration depends not only on what groups discuss, but on how they jointly manage goals, participation, strategy use, monitoring, and repair through co-regulation and socially shared regulation. We compared collaborative regulation between Human–AI and Human–Human groups in a parallel-group randomised experiment with 71 university students completing the same collaborative tasks with GenAI either available or unavailable. Focusing on human discourse, we used statistical analyses to examine differences in the distribution of collaborative regulation across regulatory modes, regulatory processes, and participatory focuses. Title: Transforming Hospitals with Artificial Intelligence: Applications in Clinical Education and Patient Care
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping hospital-based care and medical education, yet frontline clinicians often lack practical frameworks to evaluate and implement these tools safely and effectively. This presentation describes a multidisciplinary, hospital-based approach to adopting AI applications in both clinical workflows and teaching. The use of AI scribes, automated discharge summaries, and educational chatbots are used as representative case studies. First, we outline key medico-legal, privacy, bias, and workflow considerations derived from national guidance and institutional experience at a large community teaching hospital in Toronto with a multidisciplinary AI working group. We then examine AI scribes for patient care, focusing on informed consent, data handling, specialty-specific prompting, and their impact on cognitive burden and documentation quality in history-heavy fields such as geriatric medicine. Next, we present early work on large language model–generated discharge summaries, highlighting feasibility, workload reduction potential, and current barriers related to data privacy, hallucinations, and integration with electronic medical records. Finally, we report results from an AI chatbot named Medbot designed to teach medical syndromes to learners, including completion rates and agreement between AI and human raters on performance assessment. Collectively, these examples illustrate how thoughtfully governed AI solutions can decrease clinician cognitive load, enhance patient care and enrich medical education while underscoring ongoing ethical, legal, and sociotechnical challenges that require clinician leadership and interdisciplinary collaboration. Title: Semantic Risk Scoring of Aggregated Metrics: An AI-Driven Approach for Healthcare Data Governance

Abstract: Large healthcare institutions typically operate multiple business intelligence (BI) teams segmented by domain, including clinical performance, fundraising, operations, and compliance. Due to HIPAA, FERPA, and IRB restrictions, these teams face challenges in sharing patient-level data needed for analytics. To mitigate this, A metric aggregation table is proposed, which is a precomputed, privacy-compliant summary such as “Average Patient Wait Times by Department” or “Donor Conversion by Campaign.” These abstractions enable decision-making without direct access to sensitive data. Title: Quantum Entropy–Driven Temperature Scaling for Hallucination Mitigation in Generative Models
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: Hallucination in generative AI models, particularly large language models (LLMs), presents a critical barrier to reliable and trustworthy deployment in safety-critical applications. Title: Exploring the Role of Emerging Digital Technologies in Enhancing Managerial Decision-Making

Title: Fuzzy-DJSF: DJSF Optimization Method with Adaptive Scheduling Algorithm for Handling Uncertainty in Hadoop YARN Clusters
Abstract: In the era of Big Data, Apache Hadoop YARN is a standard framework, but schedulers like Shortest-Job-First (SJF) and Densest-Job-Set-First (DJSF) perform suboptimally in production. They rely on deterministic estimates for job completion times (JCT) and resources, failing to handle uncertainties from data skewness, contention, and cluster dynamics. This paper proposes Fuzzy-DJSF, a novel framework integrating fuzzy logic into job set formation and prioritization. By modeling JCT and resource demands as fuzzy numbers, it efficiently quantifies and handles estimation errors. Additionally, an adaptive learning controller dynamically fine-tunes fuzzy membership functions using performance feedback. Title: MMVUF: Improving video-based human value understanding in multimodal large language models
Abstract: Understanding human values is a crucial capability for AI systems to promote social norms and align with ethical principles. While prior work focused on language or static images, videos embed rich, dynamic cues through actions, interactions, and temporal context, making value inference more challenging. We study video-based value understanding in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) and identify two main challenges: aligning video content with abstract human values, and ensuring high-quality, diverse training under imbalanced value distributions. To address these, we propose MMVUF, a value-grounded post-training framework with a two-stage paradigm: the Multimodal Alignment Stage generates value-aware textual representations from video, and the Value Alignment Stage maps these representations to human value dimensions while preserving visual grounding through parameter-level inheritance. Additionally, we introduce VSDS, a value-specific data selection algorithm that emphasizes representative and diverse samples through value density weighting and structured sampling. Experiments on the VVALUES dataset show that MMVUF significantly enhances MLLM performance in video value understanding, highlighting the importance of structured alignment and value-aware data selection. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Age-Related Differences and Implications for Development of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems

Abstract: Vehicles continue to be instrumented with more advanced technology to enhance safety and support drivers. Title: SPINE: Context-guided iterative protein inference from spatial transcriptomes
Abstract: Spatially resolved protein abundance is critical for understanding cellular function, yet remains difficult to measure at scale, motivating its inference from transcriptomic data as an important intelligent prediction problem in spatial multi-omics. Here, we present SPINE, a neighborhood-guided, flow-matching-inspired iterative refinement framework for protein inference from spatial transcriptomes. Rather than treating protein prediction as independent point-wise regression, SPINE reformulates this task as a conditional refinement problem, in which an initial protein prior is iteratively updated toward the target protein profile under transcriptomic and spatial-neighborhood guidance. To incorporate tissue-context information, SPINE combines neighborhood-aware spatial modeling with expression-based graph structure, while an auxiliary reconstruction branch helps preserve transcriptomic semantics during cross-modal inference. Title: MetaLAN: Physics-Guided Meta-Learning with Bilinear Attention for Image Dehazing
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: Hazy weather severely degrades image quality, placing significant constraints on visual applications such as autonomous driving and intelligent surveillance. Existing deep learning-based dehazing methods rely on large-scale annotated data and possess limited generalization capabilities under haze scenes of varying concentrations and distributions. To this end, this paper proposes MetaLAN, an image dehazing network that integrates physical model constraints with a meta-learning framework. By incorporating the prior knowledge of the physical scattering model into the deep learning architecture, it achieves an efficient solution for single-image dehazing tasks. The network employs deformable convolutions to enhance the adaptive capability of feature extraction, designs a physics-guided branch to jointly estimate the transmission map and atmospheric light parameters, and innovatively introduces a Bidirectional Attention Fusion Module to optimize the estimation accuracy of physical parameters. Combined with a meta-learning adaptation mechanism to dynamically generate task-specific weights, the multi-level feature reconstruction group employs a residual structure integrating channel, pixel, and spatial attention to recover detail textures obscured by haze. Finally, the physical reconstruction layer adaptively fuses the data-driven output with the model inference results based on transmission confidence, achieving end-to-end image restoration. Title: A Constraint-Based Stockyard Planning Problem on a Realistic Time-Dependent Setting

Title: Beyond pairwise user transfer: Multimodal group-level relational preference modeling for cross-domain recommendation
Abstract: Cross-domain recommendation (CDR) offers an effective way to alleviate the cold-start problem, but most existing methods still model cross-domain preference transfer at the level of individual users. This point-wise paradigm relies heavily on overlapping users and struggles to capture the higher-order relational patterns underlying user interests across domains, resulting in limited performance when overlap is scarce. Meanwhile, representing items solely with ID embeddings ignores rich multimodal content, further constraining transferable preference modeling. In this work, we propose Multimodal Group-Level Relational Preference Modeling for Cross-Domain Recommendation, a framework that reformulates the transferable unit from direct user-to-user embedding mappings to user-to-key-user relational signatures, where overlapping users provide supervision and non-overlapping users serve as relational anchors. This design captures more stable and transferable cross-domain interest structures, yielding consistently improved performance. Concretely, we employ a multimodal large language model to extract item representations from textual and visual content, and further adopt a temporal attention pooling encoder to integrate users’ historical interactions with multimodal item semantics for constructing multimodal user representations. Based on these enriched representations, we develop a group-level relation learning module that models relational dependencies between each overlapping user and a domain-specific key user set selected from the non-overlapping ones, thereby enabling group-level preference transfer across domains. We further introduce an adversarial alignment strategy to reduce cross-domain representation discrepancies and enhance generalization. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: AI-Informed 30-Day MACE Risk Predictions in ED Arrivals

Title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Interpretable Pressure Prediction in Medical Compression Stockings

Authors: Zhang L.; Liu H.; Wu E.Q.; Deng W.; Zhang J.; Lin Y.
Title: An improved differential evolutionary algorithm integrating neighborhood search variation mechanism and multi-strategies for airport gate allocation
Abstract: As a key resource on the airport surface, gates are critical for coordinating aircraft arrivals and departures efficiently. In this work, a differential evolution-based gate allocation approach is proposed to improve the allocation efficiency of real-world gate allocation problems, integrating a neighborhood search variation mechanism and multiple strategies (NSVMDE). A mathematical model is constructed by comprehensively considering the interests of multiple stakeholders, including airports, airline companies, operators, and passengers, and is solved using an improved differential evolution (DE) algorithm. However, due to the high-dimensional and highly constrained nature of the airport gate allocation problem, the search process is prone to inefficient exploration in the early stage. To address this issue, a binary code-initialization strategy is designed to enhance the search performance. Furthermore, the complexity of the problem makes it difficult to maintain population diversity and increases the risk of premature convergence. To tackle these challenges, a neighborhood search variation mechanism is proposed to improve diversity and convergence performance. In addition, a hybrid multi-strategy approach is developed to enhance optimization performance, which combines a targeted individual promotion mechanism to improve the competitiveness of inferior individuals with a Gaussian-based superior individual optimization strategy to fully exploit high-quality solutions, thereby enabling the full potential of both weaker and stronger individuals. The effectiveness of NSVMDE is validated on 27 benchmark functions from CEC 2005 and CEC 2017, where it consistently outperforms other advanced algorithms. The CPU complexity test further shows that the dimensionless complexity ratios of NSVMDE remain stable at 2.11, 3.84, and 4.01 for the 10-, 30-, and 50-dimensional cases, respectively. Moreover, experiments on real-world airport gate allocation datasets demonstrate that NSVMDE achieves maximum gate allocation rates of 98.3% and 92.5% for scenarios with 250 and 1000 flights, respectively, with corresponding average allocation rates of 97.6% and 90.0%. Meanwhile, the average scheduling times are only 14.22 s and 44.21 s, respectively, showing that NSVMDE can generate high-quality gate allocation schemes within an acceptable computational time. These results confirm the strong optimization capability, scalability, and practical scheduling efficiency of the proposed method. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Impact of Contextual Features on Energy Consumption: An Exploratory and Predictive Analytics Approach
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: Efficient energy management in office buildings plays a critical role in achieving sustainability goals and reducing operational costs. Energy consumption in such buildings varies due to contextual factors such as time-of-day, temperature, humidity, and the operation of HVAC and lighting systems. Conventional energy management approaches often overlook these dynamic influences, resulting in energy inefficiencies. To overcome this limitation, context reasoning plays a pivotal role by transforming raw sensor data and contextual inputs into high-level knowledge that supports intelligent decision-making. This paper presents a context-aware, data-driven framework for smart energy management in office buildings. Historical energy and weather data of 20 office buildings is analyzed through Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA). Consumption patterns, seasonal variations, and contextual relationships are identified through correlation heatmaps and Seasonal-Trend Decomposition using LOESS (STL). In addition, Granger Causality (GC) analysis is applied to examine the influence of contextual factors on energy consumption. To enable proactive energy optimization, forecasting models including ARIMA, SARIMA, and Random Forest are employed to predict energy demand with contextual inputs. Experimental results show that Random Forest outperforms traditional statistical models, demonstrating superior predictive capability when contextual information is incorporated. Random Forest achieves an Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.4518 and an R-Squared (R2) score of 0.9079 indicating that 90% of the variance in energy consumption is explained by the model on the test set. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of context analysis and reasoning in improving forecasting accuracy and supporting intelligent and sustainable energy management in office buildings. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Dialogue Act Patterns in GenAI-Mediated L2 Oral Practice: A Sequential Analysis of Learner–Chatbot Interactions
Abstract: While generative AI (GenAI) voice chatbots offer scalable opportunities for second language (L2) oral practice, the interactional processes related to learners’ gains remain underexplored. This study investigates dialogue act (DA) patterns in interactions between Grade 9 Chinese English as a foreign language (EFL) learners and a GenAI voice chatbot over a 10-week intervention. Seventy sessions from 12 students were annotated by human coders using a pedagogy-informed coding scheme, yielding 6,957 coded DAs. DA distributions and sequential patterns were compared between high- and low-progress sessions. At the DA level, high-progress sessions showed more learner-initiated questions, whereas low-progress sessions exhibited higher rates of clarification-seeking, indicating greater comprehension difficulty. At the sequential level, high-progress sessions were characterised by more frequent prompting-based corrective feedback sequences, consistently positioned after learner responses, highlighting the role of feedback type and timing in effective interaction. Overall, these findings underscore the value of a dialogic lens in GenAI chatbot design, contribute a pedagogy-informed DA coding framework, and inform the design of adaptive GenAI chatbots for L2 education. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: A Position-Based Taxonomy of In-Generation Watermarking for Latent Diffusion Models
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence, especially Text-to-Image technology represented by latent diffusion models, has reshaped the landscape of digital content creation but has also raised deep concerns about false information, copyright ownership, and content traceability. Digital watermarking technology, as an imperceptible identification and traceability mechanism, has become a key technical means to achieve AI-generated content (AIGC) governance and copyright protection. This paper presents a systematic review of in-generation watermarking for latent diffusion models and develops a position-based taxonomy according to where watermarks are embedded in the generation pipeline and model architecture. Furthermore, we analyze the adversarial security threats faced by these watermarks and summarize corresponding defense strategies. Finally, we systematize key evaluation dimensions and identify the open challenges currently faced by the technology. This paper serves as a reference to facilitate future research in this field. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: From Barriers to Actions: A Thematic Analysis of Swedish K-12 Teachers’ Perspectives on AI Integration
Abstract: While professional development (PD) programs aim to prepare teachers for AI integration, understanding what obstacles teachers perceive and what support they need to begin or expand AI use in their classrooms remains crucial for effective implementation. This study presents a thematic analysis of open-ended survey responses from Swedish K–12 educators who completed an AI-focused PD program. We analyzed 781 responses describing barriers to AI use and 816 responses articulating support needs. Using AI-assisted thematic analysis, we identified six barrier themes: student-related concerns, knowledge and competence gaps, time constraints, cost and access, technical infrastructure, and policy uncertainty. For support needs, six themes emerged: time for exploration, already using AI (teachers who reported no additional support needs), tools and access, training and education, practical examples, and collegial support. The prominence of student-related concerns, particularly about academic integrity and learning dependency, suggests that AI presents qualitatively different challenges than previous educational technologies. Therefore, we discuss implications for designing multi-level support systems that address barriers at the teacher, school, and policy levels. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Liu A.
Title: Adaptive Entropy and Smoothness-Constrained Reinforcement Learning for Chemical Process Control
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: Chemical processes are typically characterized by strong nonlinearity, variable coupling, and multi-stability, which pose significant challenges to control design. Traditional control methods often exhibit limited robustness under complex and uncertain operating conditions. In recent years, deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has emerged as a data-driven approach for nonlinear process control. However, existing DRL methods still face key limitations in continuous control tasks, including inefficient exploration and excessive fluctuations in control signals, which restrict their practical applicability in industrial systems. To address these issues, this paper investigates the temperature control problem of a double continuous stirred tank reactor (CSTR) system in series and proposes an Adaptive Entropy and Smoothness-constrained Soft Actor-Critic (AES-SAC) method. Specifically, a state-dependent adaptive entropy regulation mechanism is introduced to adjust exploration intensity according to the system state, enhancing exploration when the system deviates from the setpoint and reducing randomness near steady-state operation. In addition, a control smoothness constraint is incorporated into the policy optimization process to suppress abrupt variations in control inputs between consecutive time steps, thereby improving control stability and implementability. Experimental results on the double-CSTR control task demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms standard SAC and its variants in terms of convergence speed, temperature tracking accuracy, and control input smoothness, achieving improved control performance while maintaining system stability. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: Domain-Semantic Subspace Stacking for Financial Fraud Detection
Abstract: Financial fraud detection faces persistent challenges including severe class imbalance, high-dimensional heterogeneous features, and diverse fraud patterns. Existing methods that integrate unsupervised anomaly scores with supervised classifiers typically operate on the full feature space, ignoring the semantic structure of transaction attributes. In this paper, we propose DSSA-S (Domain-Semantic Subspace Stacking), a two-level framework that partitions transaction features into semantically meaningful subgroups based on domain knowledge and performs both unsupervised anomaly scoring and supervised subspace-level classification within each subgroup. In the first level, multiple unsupervised anomaly detectors generate subspace-specific anomaly scores, while independent XGBoost classifiers trained on each subspace produce fraud probability predictions via out-of-fold cross-validation. In the second level, the original features, subspace anomaly scores, and subspace classification predictions are fused as a dual-channel augmented feature set for a final XGBoost meta-classifier. We further employ SHAP-based group-level interpretability analysis to reveal which subspace signals are most indicative of fraud. Experiments on the IEEE-CIS Fraud Detection dataset (590,540 transactions) demonstrate that DSSA-S achieves an AUC-ROC of 0.9425, outperforming XGBoost (AUC-ROC 0.9391), XGBOD (AUC-ROC 0.9383), and random subspace partitioning (AUC-ROC 0.9376), with stacking predictions contributing substantially more than anomaly scores alone. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: When do Electricity Price Forecasts Create Operational Value? A Regime-Aware Evaluation Case Study
Abstract: Whether electricity price forecasts generate operational value in industrial settings—beyond improving predictive accuracy—remains an open question, particularly under extended 168-h horizons where forecast skill degrades, and tariff-facing decisions must be made against a plausible fixed-tariff baseline. This work evaluated a leakage-safe hybrid model of OMIE gross hourly prices in a backtest of 15 audited Portuguese weeks, balanced across low-, average-, and high-volatility regimes (5/5/5), and compared a fixed BAU tariff (0.0829 €/kWh) with a forecast-informed dynamic hourly tariff, under fixed production conditions. The electricity price forecast is assessed with MAE, RMSE, bias, empirical 90% interval coverage, and Diebold-Mariano tests against naïve lag-24 and lag-168 persistence. Then, the forecast’s cost ranking quality was assessed, along with realized proxy-cost gains and downside risk. The results show the electricity price model with mean MAEs of 24.1, 26.4, and 43.0 €/MWh across low-, average-, and high-volatility weeks, and empirical coverage of 66.4%, 58.5%, and 39.8%. The model beat lag-24 persistence in all regimes (p ≤ 0.001) but beat lag-168 persistence only in average-volatility weeks (p < 0.001). However, the broad tariff ordering remained stable (Spearman ρ 0.67–0.69, pairwise accuracy 0.747–0.749). Mean realized gains relative to BAU were €559.3, €458.0, and €311.2, with positive outcomes in 60%, 80%, and 80% of weeks, and underperformance probabilities of 40%, 20%, and 20%. The results indicate a conditional decision value driven more by tariff-order preservation than by point accuracy alone. This study contributes an applied, regime-aware backtesting framework that evaluates forecast value under bounded industrial flexibility—a setting underrepresented in the existing forecast-value literature, which predominantly addresses trading and market-operator contexts. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Feasibility of Immersive Exergames Using Head-Mounted Displays in Dementia Care: A Pilot Study
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: Current pharmacological treatments for dementia remain limited, highlighting the importance of complementary non-pharmacological approaches. Serious games and exergames have emerged as promising interventions to promote cognitive stimulation, physical activity, and engagement among People with Dementia (PwD). However, most existing interventions rely on non-immersive delivery platforms, such as tablets or floor-projection systems, which may constrain user engagement and ecological validity. This work presents a pilot feasibility study exploring the use of culturally adapted exergames delivered through a head-mounted display (HMD) in a daycare context for PwD. Three exergames, previously validated for older adults in a floor-projection format, were adapted to an immersive virtual reality environment and administered over five sessions across two weeks. Feasibility was evaluated through adherence rates, behavioral observation, session-based interviews, and pre- and post-intervention cognitive screening using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA). All participants (n = 4) completed the intervention, indicating high adherence and overall acceptability. Behavioral observations and self-reports suggested high engagement, enjoyment, and motivation to participate in the activities. Cognitive outcomes showed heterogeneous patterns, including slight improvements or maintenance of cognitive functioning in most participants, while one participant exhibited reduced tolerance to the HMD. Mild adverse effects, such as dizziness and discomfort, were reported in isolated cases. Overall, the findings indicate that immersive exergames delivered via HMD are feasible and acceptable for PwD in supervised care settings, while also highlighting important usability considerations related to individual tolerance and device comfort. These preliminary results support further longitudinal and controlled studies to assess the long-term clinical impact and design requirements of HMD-based exergaming interventions in dementia care. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Multimodal Physiological Modelling for Early Emotional Stress Prediction
Abstract: Prediction of emotional stress in catastrophic events such as earthquakes, fires, or floods is crucial for planning reliable evacuation strategies and life support systems. Recent techniques have mainly focused on stress detection during or after high-arousal episodes using isolated laboratory settings. However, physiological signals before stress episodes are rarely considered to predict upcoming emotional stress situations. This shows a significant gap in current stress detection approaches. To address this gap, we propose a Multimodal Physiological Modelling for Early Emotional Stress Prediction (MPEESP) framework to perform stress prediction by capturing multimodal physiological data from daily routines. First, we propose a data preparation and feature engineering pipeline that cleans, labels, and transforms the raw ETRI multimodal lifelog data into structured feature sets for stress prediction. Then, we propose a framework, MPEESP, that uses temporal windows, engineered features, and machine learning models to predict stress episodes over the structured feature sets. Title: Multi-model Data Warehouse for Multidimensional Analysis of Flavescence Dorée: Application to the Bordeaux Region
Abstract: Flavescence Dorée is a highly contagious grapevine disease that poses a significant economic threat to European viticulture. Its current management relies on symptom monitoring, uprooting infected plants, insecticide treatments, and reservoir management. However, effective disease control is hindered by the disease’s asymptomatic period and symptom similarities with Bois Noir, necessitating complex data-driven monitoring. Currently, the reliance on traditional spreadsheet software limits the scalability and spatio-temporal analysis of the massive datasets collected. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Business Intelligence architecture based on Spatial OLAP (OnLine Analytical Processing). By integrating Data Warehousing with Geographic Information Systems, the proposed system enables intuitive, multi-dimensional analysis of diverse data types—–including graphs for dispersal modeling and JSON for scientific flexibility. Relying on a Multi-Model Data Warehouse with schema-on-read extensibility, this architecture provides an agile, “drag-and-drop” platform for extension services, farmers and researchers in epidemiology. This approach could facilitate rapid detection, predictive modeling, and optimized resource allocation, ultimately shifting pest control towards a more ecological and economically sustainable model. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: BioFC-GAT: Biomarker-Oriented GAT for ASD Diagnosis from rs-fMRI Data
Abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neuro-developmental disorder for which decisive neuroimaging biomarkers remain limited. Resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) enables whole-brain functional connectivity (FC) analysis, yet many existing models emphasize predictive accuracy over biological interpretability. In this study, we present BioFC-GAT, a biomarker-oriented graph attention framework for rs-fMRI-based ASD diagnosis. Each subject is represented as an FC graph, where regions of interest (ROIs) are modeled as nodes with connectivity-profile features. A sparse multi-head graph attention mechanism captures discriminative interactions by focusing on the strongest connections while suppressing noisy edges. To enhance interpretability, attention weights are integrated with gradient-based attribution to identify salient ROIs and functional connections. Experiments on ABIDE I demonstrate stable classification performance (AUC 0.823±0.041) and reveal consistent multi-scale biomarkers. The identified patterns show a clear concentration in somatomotor and visual systems, with additional involvement of default mode, attention, salience, and subcortical networks. At the connectivity level, both strong within-network interactions and structured cross-network connections are observed, supporting the network dysconnectivity hypothesis of ASD. Cross-atlas analysis further indicates that these biomarkers exhibit stable spatial and network-level consistency. These results highlight BioFC-GAT as an interpretable and robust framework for connectome-based biomarker discovery in ASD. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: Evaluating Static and Dynamic Approaches for Assessing Trustworthiness in Medical Risk Factor Forecasting
Abstract: The adoption of machine-learning models in clinical practice requires not only accurate predictions but also an understanding of their trustworthiness. We study predictive trustworthiness in forecasting cardiovascular risk factors from childhood and adolescence to later ages using real-world medical data. We compare two approaches for identifying unreliable predictions: a dynamic approach based on predictive uncertainty from a probabilistic heteroscedastic regression model and a static approach that identifies interpretable subgroups with consistently high prediction error. We further evaluate whether combining both approaches improves performance, and gather feedback from domain experts on practical utility. Across multiple risk factors, both approaches perform similarly, with a slight advantage for the static approach (F1 score 0.58 vs 0.56). Title: IDG-Diff: Intent-Driven Grasp Generation with Latent Diffusion and Affordance-Aware Refinement
Abstract: Human grasp synthesis aims to generate plausible hand poses for a given object. Existing methods are largely geometry-driven and often produce generic grasps, overlooking diverse human intents. We propose IDG-Diff, an intent-driven grasp generation framework based on latent diffusion. A VAE compresses high-dimensional MANO hand parameters into a compact latent manifold, and a conditional diffusion model samples multi-modal intent-conditioned grasp via iterative denoising. We design a bidirectional cross-attention module that jointly fuses object point features and intent embed-dings, allowing intent to attend to functional object regions. To address penetration artifacts in diffusion-based generation, we integrate a post-generation refinement stage that iteratively adjusts hand pose to reduce hand–object intersection while preserving intent-aligned contacts. We further introduce a model-free affordance accuracy metric that evaluates intent alignment by checking whether generated contacts land on correct function-al parts using ground-truth part segmentation, eliminating the circular evaluation risk of classifier-based metrics. Title: Code Generation for Open Data Statistics: Case Study on the Genesis Database
Abstract: This paper introduces a robust pipeline enabling Large Language Models (LLMs) to perform precise Table Question Answering (Table-QA) on complex statistical tables. Processing complex, visually oriented table formats remains a major challenge for large language models, as they exhibit inherent multi-dimensional and hierarchical structures. Despite their visual complexity, these formats adhere to strict structural conventions. Our approach leverages these regularities—such as specific cell border styles and hierarchical indentations—to transform these files into a unified JSON structure using a deterministic extraction method. Instead of generating direct answers, the LLM is fine-tuned to produce Python scripts that programmatically extract information from the generated JSON files. To achieve this, we generated a synthetic dataset comprising approximately 13,000 high-quality question-code pairs. Our fine-tuned Microsoft Phi-4 model achieves a functional success score of 88.5% (peaking at 95.2% on XLSX files), on par with the most advanced proprietary models, such as GPT-4.1. Title: Unsupervised topic modeling of song lyrics with large language models: A zero-shot framework for discourse analysis
Abstract: Song lyrics reflect social and cultural dynamics, yet their large-scale computational analysis remains challenging. Supervised approaches depend on costly annotations, while conventional topic models rely primarily on lexical similarity, limiting their ability to capture implicit meanings, figurative language, and culturally grounded expressions, particularly in informal and metaphor-rich genres such as Brazilian funk. The framework first employs zero-shot generative theme induction combined with semantic clustering to construct coherent and interpretable topics from small reference corpora. Topic classification constitutes a key component of the framework, enabling scalable corpus-level analysis, and is performed through LLM-based zero-shot inference. To address the stochastic variability inherent to generative models, we propose a reliability-aware multilabel strategy based on self-consistency and agreement filtering, producing stable and confidence-controlled predictions without annotated data. Two large-scale case studies on the top-1000 Brazilian funk songs demonstrate improved interpretability, robustness, and scalability for uncovering dominant discourses and their interactions. Title: Neuro-Symbolic Verification of LLM Outputs for Data-Sensitive Domains
Abstract: LLMs deployed in high-stakes domains face fundamental reliability challenges: hallucinations and privacy vulnerabilities create unacceptable risks when errors carry legal, financial, or safety consequences. Authors: Li H.; Li H.; Li H.; Zhang B.; Wan L.; Chen R.; Han H.; Huang H.
Title: Quaternion-based multi-branch attention network for hyperspectral image classification
Abstract: With rapid advances in remote sensing technology, the hyperspectral image (HSI) offers rich spectral information across contiguous bands and is widely applied in many fields. However, some existing data representation methods frequently confront challenges such as inadequate information acquisition and poor interactivity. Quaternion representations have shown remarkable effectiveness in image data processing. Their algebraic structure and operational properties enable more informative feature representations and enhance information interaction of the network. To this end, this paper proposes a novel quaternion multi-branch attention network (QMAN). The main contributions are as follows: 1) the designed quaternion generator (QG) maps the data into the quaternion space, capturing richer features and significantly enhancing information interaction; 2) the constructed multi-branch architecture can process data in parallel, which not only learns discriminative information but also boosts the network learning efficiency; 3) the embedded multi-scale quaternion attention (MQA) module further strengthens important features and characterizes the diversity of homogeneous regions through a multi-scale strategy; 4) the designed weighted loss function focuses on minority class samples, effectively alleviating class imbalance. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed QMAN is superior to some existing state-of-the-art methods. Title: Towards a Multidimensional Assessment of Urban Bikeability: Integrating GIS and User Perception
Abstract: Cycling is widely acknowledged as a key component of sustainable urban mobility, but its adoption remains limited in many high-motorization Mediterranean cities. In these contexts, bikeability cannot be evaluated only through cycling infrastructure provision, but should be interpreted as the result of the interaction between spatial, environmental, and perceptual dimensions. This paper proposes a multidimensional framework for the assessment of urban bikeability through the integration of spatial evidence and user perception data. The analysis is applied to the case study of Catania, combining the current and planned cycling network derived from the official Biciplan with the distribution of vegetated areas obtained from regional cartography as a proxy for environmental quality and survey-based evidence on mobility habits, perceived barriers and cycling incentives. The findings point out a fragmented existing cycling network and a broader but still spatially uneven planned configuration. Moreover, they highlight an unequal distribution of vegetated areas, with more extensive green coverage in peripheral zones than in the dense urban core. Survey findings show that cycling still plays a marginal role in everyday mobility and the most relevant barriers are safety-related concerns due to the interaction with motorized traffic and inadequate infrastructures. The study reveals a mismatch between planning intentions and experienced cycling environments by users. Thus, improving bikeability requires an integrated approach which combines infrastructure provision, environmental quality and perceived safety. The proposed framework can be transferred to other urban contexts characterized by high motorization rates and limited cycling uptake. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: An Explainable Hybrid Natural Language Processing and CatBoost Framework for Phishing Website Detection
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: Phishing websites remain a major cybersecurity threat, often leading to identity theft, financial fraud, and data breaches. Traditional defenses like blacklists and heuristic filters fail against zero-day attacks, where attackers modify URLs and site structures to avoid detection. This study proposes an explainable hybrid framework that integrates lexical and structural features from URLs and HTML with semantic representations derived from TF–IDF and DistilBERT embeddings. To handle dataset imbalance, a combined oversampling and cleaning strategy is applied, and classification is performed using CatBoost, a gradient-boosted decision tree model suited for mixed data types. Trained on the PhishStorm dataset and validated with the independent PhishTank Frontier dataset to mimic real-world zero-day scenarios, the framework achieved over 91% accuracy with a ROC–AUC of about 0.97. Authors: Wu T.; Chen P.; Han Q.; Li J.; Dong Y.
Title: KAN-DTA: Interaction-Aware DTA Prediction via Cross-Modal: Attention and Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks
Abstract: Modeling heterogeneous feature interactions is a central challenge in drug–target affinity (DTA) prediction and, more broadly, in structured interaction learning. Existing deep learning methods often rely on implicit feature fusion and black-box regression heads, which limit both interaction expressiveness and interpretability. We propose KAN-DTA, an end-to-end interaction-aware framework that combines explicit cross-modal attention with structured nonlinear regression. Specifically, the model first projects drug and protein representations into a scale-consistent shared latent space to support reliable cross-modal interaction learning. It then employs a bidirectional cross-attention module to capture fine-grained dependencies between drugs and targets. Finally, an enhanced Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (KAN) is used as the regression head, modeling affinity prediction as a composition of learnable univariate nonlinear functions and offering a more structured and interpretable alternative to conventional multilayer perceptrons. Title: Multilingual Embedders for Explainable Hinglish Retrieval in RAG
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of retrieving formal English documents from informal Hinglish queries in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems. We propose a dual-pipeline framework to evaluate both strict lexical alignment (T1) and broader semantic generalization (T2) of multilingual embedders and further analyze token level contribution in case studies. For an upper bound, we compare several multilingual embedders with our Hinglish fine-tuned model on these tasks. Our results reveal a significant performance gap: a purpose-built, fine-tuned model achieves 96.3% accuracy on the strict task, far sur-passing the best zero-shot model at 76.7%. Furthermore, an explainable error analysis shows that fine-tuning shifts the primary failure type from deep semantic confusion to more tractable lexical ambiguity. Title: Simulating Validity: Modal Decoupling in MLLM Generated Feedback on Science Drawings
Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are increasingly used to generate feedback on students’ hand-drawn scientific models. However, modal decoupling, where outputs remain pedagogically plausible while contradicting the drawing or treating depicted elements as missing, threatens feedback validity. Using N = 150 middle school drawings spanning five modeling tasks and three competence levels, we generated N = 300 feedback instances with GPT-5.1 and coded four grounding error types. Grounding failures were common: 41.3% of feedback contained at least one error. In the direct workflow, 49.3% of instances were flawed; the inventory-list-first workflow reduced this to 33.3%. False absence was the dominant failure mode and increased with drawing complexity. An inventory-list-first workflow reduced error rates but did not eliminate them: one in three outputs remained flawed. Title: ArguAgent: AI-Supported Real-Time Grouping for Productive Argumentation in STEM Classrooms
Abstract: Argumentation is a core practice in STEM education, but its productivity depends on who participates and how they interact. Higher-achieving students often dominate the talk and decision-making, while lower-achieving peers may disengage, defer, or comply without contributing substantive reasoning. As a result, forming groups strategically–based on students’ stances and argumentation skills–is critical for sustaining inclusive, productive, and evidence-based discourse. In practice, however, teachers seldom implement such grouping because it requires real-time insight into students’ positions and the quality of their argumentation—information that is difficult to assess reliably and at scale during instruction. We present a generative AI-powered system, ArguAgent, that creates groups optimizing for stance heterogeneity while constraining argumentation quality differences to ±1 level on a validated learning progression. ArguAgent uses a two-component assessment pipeline: first scoring student arguments on a 0–4 rubric, then clustering positions via semantic analysis. We validated the scoring component against human expert consensus (Krippendorff’s α = 0.817) using 200 expert-generated scores. Testing three OpenAI models (GPT-4o-mini, GPT-5.1, GPT-5.2) with identical calibrated prompts, we found that systematic prompt engineering informed by human disagreement analysis contributed 89% of scoring improvement (QWK: 0.531 → 0.686), while model upgrades contributed an additional 11% (QWK: 0.686 → 0.708). Simulation testing across 100 classes demonstrated that the grouping algorithm achieves 95.4% of groups that meet both design criteria, a 3.2× improvement over random assignment. Title: Cultural, organisational, and individual factors contributing to cyber incident reporting: A systematic literature review
Abstract: Incident reporting behaviour is a critical yet underexplored human factor in organisational cyber resilience, shaping how organisations learn from incidents and adapt to evolving digital threats. This systematic literature review synthesises evidence from 106 peer-reviewed studies across cyber resilience, healthcare, and aviation to examine how cultural, organisational, technological, and psychological factors influence employees’ reporting behaviour. The review identifies five thematic clusters of antecedents—organisational, psychological, technical, social, and motivational—and shows how their interaction can either facilitate or hinder incident reporting behaviour. Building on these findings, we propose a novel, integrative multilevel conceptual model that extends the Cybersecurity Culture–Behaviour (CSCB) framework of Sutton and Tompson (2024) by incorporating a widely used behaviour-change framework, perceived consequences of reporting, and the moderating roles of incident characteristics and reporter attributes. The results highlight the importance of multilevel, human-centred interventions that foster psychological safety, provide timely and meaningful feedback, and align managerial practices with principles of a just culture. This study advances understanding of incident reporting behaviour as a socio-technical behaviour and offers a unifying framework for designing interventions to strengthen cyber resilience through improved human reporting practices. © 2026 The Authors

Title: TabDDPM-Aug: Adaptive diffusion-based hybrid augmentation for imbalanced tabular classification
Abstract: Augmenting imbalanced tabular data is critical for improving classification performance, yet existing generative models face utility-privacy-fidelity trade-offs, particularly when data is limited. They often achieve high utility through memorization or suffer severe distributional collapse. We demonstrate this is not an inherent limitation but a consequence of fixed augmentation strategies that ignore dataset scale, quantified by the minority sample-to-feature ratio ((Formula presented)). We present TabDDPM-Aug, which addresses this through dataset-adaptive strategy selection (DBHA for low-density regimes, FDHA for high-density regimes), Distance-to-Closest-Real (DCR) filtering to eliminate memorized copies, and ensemble generation to prevent mode collapse. Comprehensive evaluation across 13 benchmarks spanning diverse domains, dimensionalities, and imbalance ratios shows TabDDPM-Aug achieves the best average rank on classification utility (rank 1.85 of 9 methods), privacy preservation (rank 1.00), and distributional fidelity (MMD rank 1.46, DCR rank 1.15). In low-density regimes, it maintains competitive utility while achieving up to 48% privacy risk reduction over GAN-based methods. In high-density settings, it yields up to 15% higher F1-score and 94% better distributional fidelity compared to standalone diffusion augmentation on minority samples. These properties make TabDDPM-Aug suitable for fraud detection, healthcare diagnostics, and other privacy-sensitive domains where regulatory compliance is essential. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: A global point cloud semantic mapping method for underground spaces under extreme spatial constraints
Abstract: Narrow and irregular underground roadways commonly suffer from dim lighting, absence of satellite signals, and complex spatial topologies, making it difficult for traditional methods to achieve rapid and accurate spatial perception and semantic modeling in such environments. Existing studies mostly focus on large-scale underground spaces such as tunnels and subways, where datasets feature single scenes and limited scales and cannot support point cloud understanding tasks under extreme spatial constraints. Thus, insufficient exploration has been conducted on small, narrow, and geologically complex underground roadways. To address this research gap, this study has constructed the NUH-PCD (Narrow Underground High-fidelity Point Cloud Dataset), which is the first point cloud dataset for ultra-narrow and irregular underground roadways. This study employs Simultaneous Localisation and Mapping (SLAM) integrated with Real-Time Kinematic (RTK) technology to achieve high-density point cloud data acquisition and geometric modelling. The core focus lies on point cloud semantic segmentation and the generation of global semantic maps. Through point cloud semantic segmentation techniques, unstructured point clouds are transformed into global maps rich in semantic information, providing technical support for the monitoring of underground space conditions. The PointNet++_DAG semantic segmentation model was constructed by innovatively embedding the dynamic attention gating (DAG) module into the PointNet++ framework, enabling accurate segmentation of eight core categories of targets in underground roadways and further generating global semantic maps with abundant semantic information. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed PointNet++_DAG model achieves a mean intersection over union (mIoU) of 76.73%, which is 14.51 percentage points higher than that of the baseline PointNet++ model. This work effectively breaks through the bottleneck of global point cloud semantic mapping for underground spaces under extreme spatial constraints, offering an efficient solution for intelligent cognition of underground roadway environments. It also lays the foundation for subsequent safety monitoring and emergency response, possessing significant theoretical value and engineering application prospects. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Screen Reader Usage, Customization, and Perceived Usability Among Persons with Visual Impairments: A Large-Scale Survey in Japan
Abstract: Screen readers are essential for digital accessibility, but regional and linguistic differences in their use remain underexplored. This study surveyed 592 Japanese individuals with visual impairments to examine usage patterns, configuration settings, and perceived usability. Older participants tended to select settings corresponding to slower playback speeds. Title: UGCA-DTI: Uncertainty-Gated Cross-Attention for Robust Drug–Target Interaction Prediction
Abstract: Drug–target interaction prediction is fundamental to computational drug discovery, yet robust generalization remains challenging under cold-start settings and experimental noise. In this study, we propose UGCA-DTI, a structure-aware multimodal framework that combines a prior-driven structured interaction decoupling strategy with Uncertainty-Gated Cross-Attention for robust drug–target interaction prediction. Motivated by the joint roles of semantic compatibility and structural complementarity in drug–target recognition, UGCA-DTI decouples the interaction process and uses evidential uncertainty to gate cross-attention, thereby suppressing unreliable cross-modal evidence during fusion. An evidential prediction head further provides interaction probability together with predictive uncertainty. Experiments on DAVIS and KIBA under warm and cold-start settings demonstrate consistent improvements over strong baselines, with the largest gains on unseen-protein evaluation. Title: Deep hashing via mean centroid representation for large-scale image retrieval
Abstract: Deep hashing has potential application prospects in large-scale image retrieval due to its low-cost and efficient retrieval advantages. However, traditional instance-based hashing methods match images by directly comparing their hash codes, but this process is easily disturbed by appearance factors such as color, angle, and background, resulting in semantic mismatches. Approaches based on centroid/proxy representations have been proposed to alleviate the above problems. Existing centroid/proxy-based approaches are limited to training and do not optimize retrieval efficiency, which goes against the core benefits of hashing. Specifically, by calculating the mean centroid of each class of samples, a novel mean centroid triplet loss is designed to alleviate the negative impact of outliers, thereby generating compact and discriminative hash codes. In addition, since the samples of each class are represented by a mean centroid, the number of target vectors in the database set is significantly reduced, thereby greatly narrowing the search space, reducing retrieval time and storage requirements, which is suitable for production deployment. Comprehensive experiments conducted on three public datasets demonstrate that our proposed MCRDH framework surpasses various state-of-the-art methods. Title: A Comprehensive Framework for Digital Intelligence Quotient (DQ): Developing Digital Citizenship Competencies for K-12 Learners
Abstract: The rapid advancement of digital technologies and artificial intelligence has created an urgent need for comprehensive frameworks to assess and develop digital competencies among young learners. This paper proposes a Digital Intelligence Quotient (DQ) framework comprising four core dimensions and 20 competencies designed to measure learners’ abilities to use digital technology appropriately, safely, ethically, and responsibly. Each dimension includes five core competencies with specific indicators suitable for K-12 learners. Title: Detecting Real Software Faults Through Resource Consumption Anomalies: An Evaluation of the Tricorder Methodology
Abstract: Software faults in production environments pose significant challenges to software reliability, as traditional testing approaches do not always account for non-deterministic or operational conditions. A one-tailed Wilcoxon signed-rank test confirmed a statistically significant difference in the number of iterations required to detect actual faults versus control-group executions, producing an F1-score of 39.18%. These results demonstrate the potential of the Tricorder methodology to identify real software faults through resource-consumption anomalies, while highlighting challenges introduced by API constraints in the dataset that limited execution to unit tests. Title: Intelligent systems for occupant-centric HVAC control: a systematic review of perception, analysis, and control components
Abstract: Occupant-centric HVAC control promises to balance occupant comfort and energy efficiency, representing a key application domain of intelligent systems in building engineering. However, its widespread implementation faces substantial challenges requiring integration of multiple system components. This study addresses a critical gap by conceptualizing occupant-centric HVAC control as an integrated intelligent system and systematically reviewing the evolution of its three core components, namely perception, analysis, and control, in 104 publications from 2019 to 2025 retrieved via Web of Science. Our objectives are to: (a) identify technological development patterns across system components; (b) analyze their functional interdependencies and integration mechanisms; and (c) identify key challenges affecting real-world implementation. Our findings reveal a clear trend toward technological convergence, characterized by multimodal sensing, advanced machine learning models, and increasingly personalized control strategies. Significant challenges persist, including multimodal data fusion complexity, context-specific implementation requirements, disciplinary knowledge silos, privacy concerns, and integration with existing infrastructure. From an expert systems perspective, the findings highlight that system effectiveness relies on the coordinated interaction of perception, learning, and control modules to enable adaptive decision-making. This study contributes by providing a unified analytical framework and a system-level roadmap for the design and deployment of scalable occupant-centric HVAC systems, supporting the development of next-generation intelligent building environments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: AnchorNet: A Clinically Grounded Causal Model for Personalized Medicine
Abstract: Causal inference methods for personalized prediction provide valuable information for clinical decision-making. However, validating such estimates is inherently challenging, as counterfactual outcomes are unobservable in practice. Recent causal machine learning approaches have addressed this issue through theoretical error bounds and advances in model architecture. Despite strong performance in controlled settings, these approaches often lack a direct link to clinically measurable quantities, such as population-level treatment effects reported in trials, limiting clinical trust and reliable deployment in real-world healthcare settings. To improve the usefulness of causal inference in healthcare, we propose a method that aligns individualized predictions with clinically meaningful and assessable quantities while retaining the ability to model patient heterogeneity. Our approach, called AnchorNet, enforces global consistency with an externally estimated average treatment effect (ATE) while allowing for patient-level variation. AnchorNet achieves this by regularizing individual treatment effect predictions toward a population-level estimate through an ATE-matching objective. We further derive a generalization bound, demonstrating guarantees comparable to existing methods under bounded treatment heterogeneity. Experiments on a semi-simulated infant care benchmark and a real-world geriatric dataset demonstrate competitive performance and robustness to estimation bias. Overall, anchoring individualized predictions to clinically interpretable population-level effects preserves predictive accuracy while promoting coherent and trustworthy behavior in real-world healthcare settings. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: SEPT Privacy-By-Design Framework for Early Teacher Intervention: Modeling Difficulty as a Deviation from a Student's Success Signature
Abstract: In remote and hybrid learning environments, instructors suffer from “attentional blindness”: they cannot simultaneously monitor the non-verbal cues of an entire cohort to identify students in difficulty. While Affective Computing offers automated solutions to restore this pedagogical bond, their performances are often limited by the highly personal expression of emotional states. Moreover, students’ difficulties are not reflected by emotions only, and more dimensions need to be considered. To address these challenges, we propose SEPT (Student Emotional and Physical Trajectories), a privacy-by-design framework that leverages the dynamics of emotional and behavioral trajectories to enable the robust and early detection of academic difficulty. In this paper, we detail the extraction of multimodal signals and the formalization of SEPT, which models the student's journey as a continuous time series. We define “success engagement signature”, computed from past successful trajectories, to characterize positive attitudes and states of mind, at individual and group levels. During new activities, we compute the deviations from success signatures for each SEPT dimension and compare the performances of several classification models for students’ difficulty prediction. Results demonstrate that modeling difficulty as a deviation from a student's own signature outperforms group signature models by +17% (F1-Score). Furthermore, regarding early-warning capabilities, the framework maintains robust predictive power even when observing only the first 30% of the activity, with negligible performance degradation (< 6% F1-Score drop). This allows for privacy-preserving intervention (AUC 0.67) comparable to invasive biometric methods. We show that SEPT framework helps instructors identifying the 10–15% of students showing significant difficulties. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.
